summary: 970K scale-test forecast: encoder has 2 separable readouts by decode regime -- discrete SBC block-argmax algebra (collision-count family) forecast to HOLD at 970K (combinatorial margin ~180 orders of magnitude, P_deflated~0.60-0.65); continuous dense retrieval ret_agree10 (order-statistic/distance-concentration family) is ALREADY failing at 0.18-0.27 at only 18pct of scale and is forecast to degrade FURTHER with no cliff (P_deflated~0.05 HARD-PASS on plain SBC at 970K). GSBC graded-code lever already measures 1.5-3x better at the SAME scale but its density-dial retune is unverified past ~160K -- the one place a genuine sharp Donoho-Tanner-class cliff is plausible if not retuned (P_deflated~0.30-0.35 capped).
plain_language: Before spending a GPU run on the 970K-scale test, I forward-derived what it should show. The encoders algebra channel (bind/unbind) looks structurally safe at full scale -- the math margin is enormous. But the retrieval-ranking channel is ALREADY below its target at just 18pct of production scale, and the physics says more entities can only make that worse, not better -- so the plain encoder is very likely to fail the 970K retrieval bar regardless of the scale-test outcome. The newer graded-code fix already measures 1.5-3x better at current scale and is the right lever, but its own scale-safety past 160K is unverified and needs its tuning dial re-set for the bigger vocabulary, not reused as-is.

summary: Test 0 (near-dup density in real 970K KB): exact-dup low (0.66%), but 15.86% of V (note/prereg chunks) near-identical by construction (within-doc Jaccard 0.96-0.97), WordNet polysemy collapses 121,274 rows to 89,395 lemmas (39.6% share lemma). Effective-distinct/V ~0.79-0.83 vs naive 0.9966. Birthday margin recompute with effective-N: still ~180.5+ orders (GREEN, robust). Structured-collision risk real but narrow, concentrated in 2 dedupable sources (YELLOW not RED). KB composition itself is NOT ConceptNet-like (mixed dogfood ingest incl. project self-notes/preregs chunked) -- revises the prior forecasts framing.
plain_language: We measured how many near-duplicate entries actually exist in the real 970,000-item knowledge base before spending any GPU time on the big scale test. Good news: the core math margin that says the encoder wont scramble entries into each other at scale is confirmed solid even after accounting for duplicates. But we found the duplicates are concentrated in a specific, fixable place -- chunks of the projects own research notes that get split into overlapping pieces, plus dictionary word-sense entries that share spelling. Recommendation: clean up those two sources before the big test, which also gives a concrete number to retune one of the encoders dials against.

summary: 970K retrieval-margin re-slice: attempted to stratify keyed@J5/shuffled_key by chunk-vs-non-chunk membership (Test 0 next-step); found per-item data was never persisted (aggregate-only metrics.json across whole encoder lineage, confirmed via eval-code read of _keyed_unit/_semantic_unit) -- verdict is DATA-ABSENT, not concentrated/diffuse/mixed.
plain_language: We tried a cheap check to see whether the encoder retrieval weak-spot is concentrated in the near-duplicate documents we found earlier (which would make a simple cleanup fix it) or spread out everywhere (which would need a harder fix). We could not tell either way: the historical test results were only ever saved as summary numbers, never broken down item-by-item, so there is nothing to re-slice. This is a logging gap, not a bad result -- it rules out the free option and confirms the only path forward is re-running a check with logging added.

summary: brain-structure->consumer re-map post-ingest-live: CLS-consolidation classic interference-avoidance flavor REFUTED as a consumer for the shipped ingest architecture (discrete graph-store writes, zero shared weights, exact completeness 142219/142219) -- 2 external lit-scans confirm catastrophic interference is scoped to shared/distributed representations, not symbolic KG storage. CLS schema-extraction flavor (relation-type promotion from N witnesses) is real-in-principle (lit-corroborated design pattern) but deferred to ingest Stage 4, not live. Overall ranking UNCHANGED from 07-05/07-07: hippocampal recall + basal-ganglia gate remain the only PROVEN consumers; top recommended next build stays the already-spec'd cerebellar SR-rollout for the basal-ganglia gate's own d4->d6 depth-degradation gap.
plain_language: I checked whether the newly-launched knowledge-ingest pipeline creates a real need for a brain-inspired sleep-consolidation mechanism (moving facts from fast short-term memory into slower long-term storage, the way brains do overnight). It does not: the ingest system we actually built writes each fact as its own separate, addressable record, so there is nothing for one new fact to interfere with or overwrite -- the classic problem that consolidation solves in brains simply does not arise in this design, and outside literature backs that up. A related, smaller idea (learning to recognize brand-new types of relationships only after seeing them repeated a few times) is real and worth building eventually, but not yet -- it only matters once we ingest open, unstructured text instead of today's pre-organized sources. The practical upshot: no new brain-component build is justified by ingest going live; we stay focused on the encoder/ingest path and the one already-planned next experiment (teaching our existing control-gate to anticipate further ahead).

summary: Stage-needs x brain-component FORWARD map: cross-checked the consumer-first brain-component audits (07-05/07-07) into a forward stage-by-stage need map. Key findings: (1) 2 of 3 neuromodulation flavors are already built under different cortex-primitive names (M1.3 NoiseChannel = arousal/stochastic-coupling; cfrpe = dopamine-RPE), not waiting on-hold as prior notes implied; (2) Stage 4 (LM equivalence) is the load that would finally activate thalamic dynamic routing + N-way basal-ganglia action-selection + a second cerebellum consumer (multi-turn dialogue horizon, inferred not yet evidenced); (3) cortical microcircuit/predictive coding is likely permanently unneeded for Stage 4 generation since frame-slot decoding already fills that function; (4) Stage 1 12% gap decomposed: correctly-closed housekeeping (Probe 1/6/7/8 demotion), 2 non-load-bearing long-tail items (CRT grid-cell smoke-only, N8 ConceptNet never dispatched), and exactly ONE genuine load-bearing gap worth shoring up before Stage 4: refuse-gate 1D-to-2D (alpha,sigma) joint-controller upgrade, because refuse-gate is M3 capability-block-5 (self-knowledge), a hard M3 dependency.
plain_language: We mapped which brain-inspired components each development stage will need, looking FORWARD instead of just at what is needed right now. The good news: some pieces we thought were still missing (like neuromodulation) turn out to already be built under different names. The main actionable finding is a cheap, concrete fix worth doing soon: upgrade the fabrication-refusal safety gate from a 1-dimensional to a 2-dimensional control surface, because that gate is a hard dependency for the eventual conversational-AI milestone.

summary: resonator reachability ceiling: post-verifier residual (oracle_any=0.806 at K4,T0=0.5,R=10) decomposed via geometric-race model -> p_basin~0.15/restart (not vanishing); R~19 restarts reaches 0.95 (1.9x compute). T0-escape curve is textbook Kramers saturation (further T0 unlikely to help). Open risk: whether p_basin collapses at K>4 (clustering/condensation transition, OGP-hardness) is untested here (K in {3,4} only) -- ties to CG_META basin-proliferation falsification. Recommends R-sweep (cheap, confirms restart-budget framing) then K-sweep (decisive for wall-vs-budget) -- neither dispatched.
plain_language: We figured out why the K4 factorization search sometimes never finds the right answer even with 10 tries: each try has roughly a 1-in-7 chance of landing on the correct answer, so it is mostly a matter of trying more times (about 19 tries gets you to 95% success, at under 2x the compute) rather than a fundamental wall. But whether this stays true for harder problems (more factors) is still an open question worth a cheap follow-up test.

summary: Integrity audit of what-is-implemented tracking: cert store (cert_ledger.jsonl 1492 atoms, live) CONFIRMED canonical append-only; PROGRESS.md (3d stale, still lists refuse-gate V_REL=256) and cap_map (0 mentions of v9) are LAGGING snapshots that both missed refuse_gate_v9 landed 07-02. HEADLINE: invisible-result rate UNMEASURABLE mechanically because 92pct (1382/1492) of ledger atoms carry no anchor field; hand spot-check of 6 consequential landed HARD_PASS cells = 0 truly missing (all atomized under prose atom_ids). Semantic recall 3/3 above cosine 0.30 but char_trigram lexical/thin-margin. Added PROT-023 (anchor-keyed atomization + store-query-before-dispatch Director gate). Top fix: require anchor+cell_commit on every atom to make reconciliation possible.
plain_language: Our master list of what has been built (the cert store) is trustworthy and up to date, but the two human-readable summary docs lag behind it and both had already forgotten the refuse-gate we rebuilt-and-passed 5 days ago. The real weakness: 92 percent of records do not say which experiment produced them, so we cannot automatically check whether anything passed but was never recorded. Nothing important was actually lost this time, and I added a rule to fix the record-keeping going forward.

summary: dimension-vs-N scaling for NN retrieval: JL/Larsen-Nelson gives exact d~c*log(N) (tight, matching lower bound); distance-concentration/hubness lit (Beyer99, Radovanovic10, Aggarwal-Hinneburg-Keim01) has NO N-compensation formula (asymptotic in d only); FlyHash/sparse-expansion lit has no N-scaling law but Willshaw/Knoblauch-Palm-Sommer associative memory gives m~sqrt(N)*log(N) at fixed critical load; participation-ratio-vs-N target-ratio heuristic NOT established anywhere searched, with one directly on-point 2026 negative result (Tamamori, kernel-Hopfield) showing a Cover-theorem-style PR/N geometric bound explicitly FAILS to predict retrieval collapse (dynamical SNR threshold dominates instead).
outcome: inline text answer to Director (no note file per task instruction — pure external lit-scan, findings returned directly)
plain_language: Checked the math/CS literature for a formula answering: how much bigger does the encoding dimension need to be as the number of stored items grows, to keep retrieval accuracy the same? Found one clean, well-established answer (Johnson-Lindenstrauss: dimension needs to grow like log of the item count, and this is proven tight) but three related bodies of literature (distance-concentration/hubness, sparse-hash-expansion, participation-ratio-based capacity heuristics) do NOT have an established formula for this — and one very recent paper directly tested a participation-ratio-style capacity bound and found it FAILS, with real collapse instead governed by signal-to-noise dynamics, not the geometric ratio. This is useful negative evidence against leaning on a PR/N heuristic for the substrate.

summary: Density x scale sweep design (m*(N) prediction for 970K GSBC retune): 3 lit-scans found NO single closed-form m*(N) law -- 3 disagreeing theoretical anchors (JL/Larsen-Nelson predicts mild ~14pct density growth via m~ln(V); Willshaw/Palm optimal-fill-factor predicts density should roughly HALVE via m~1/sqrt(V); Knoblauch-Palm-Sommer fixed-fidelity predicts ~2.7x growth via m~sqrt(V)*log(V)) -- consistent with this channel already being a confirmed self-margin-taxonomy RESISTOR (2026-07-06). New empirical finding from re-analyzing the ALREADY-LANDED 5-seed marginpush data: cross-seed CV is U-shaped (tight 2.7 pct at m5, wide 15-16 pct at both m3 and m8) -- a critical-slowing-down early-warning signature for the approaching cliff, not previously flagged. Designed a cheap 4-rung adaptive sweep (50K/100K free-subsample, 177,899 already-landed, ~400K folded into the already-planned Stage-3 scale-test) with dual-functional-form fitting (log vs power-law) and a pre-registered validation check against the real 970K dispatch. Total marginal NEW cost ~30-50 min of already-idle GPU time.
plain_language: We designed (did not run) the cheapest possible test plan to predict, before spending a full day of GPU time, exactly how dense the encoders graded code needs to be at the full 970,000-item production knowledge base. We checked the math literature for a shortcut formula and found three different, disagreeing formulas -- one says density should barely change, one says it should nearly double, one says it should nearly halve. Since no single formula wins outright, we designed a small, cheap experiment (about 30-50 minutes of already-idle GPU time) that tests a few small-scale points first and fits the two most plausible formulas against real data, so the eventual full-scale run gets a validated best guess instead of a blind one. We also found a free bonus insight by re-reading data we already had: watching how much the result varies across random seeds (not just the average result) gives an early-warning sign of an approaching cliff before it actually happens.

summary: density_scale_theory_reconciliation_970k: reconciled the 3 disagreeing m*(N) scaling theories (JL/Larsen-Nelson, Willshaw/Palm fill-factor, Knoblauch-Palm-Sommer fixed-fidelity) via DECODE MECHANISM matching (additive-interference/superposition storage vs geometric-placement/crowding), not orthogonality alone; ret_agree10 channel is Family-1 geometric-crowding (matches taxonomy row already on file) -> JL/Larsen-Nelson is the mechanism-matched theory, not KPS or Willshaw (whose i.i.d.-additive-interference assumptions belong to the DISCRETE SBC channel, a separate already-forecast-to-hold question). Orthogonality correction (effective-distinct 771K-804K) shrinks Anchor A growth 14.0%->12.3%, small effect; the larger effect is excluding Anchor C mechanism-mismatched pull, narrowing the prior blended [5,9] density-grid band to [5,7], central estimate m=6. New falsifiable trajectory-discrimination test pre-registered (flat/mild = confirms match, steep sqrt(V)*ln(V) climb = mechanism-classification refuted). New hub-formation caveat identified (chunk-cluster near-dup rows should show worse ret_agree10 than non-chunk rows at same m, independent of aggregate trend) -- cheap stratified test proposed, zero new GPU cost.
plain_language: We had three respected but disagreeing math theories predicting whether the encoders density setting should grow, shrink, or barely change as we scale from 177K to 970K facts. We figured out the disagreement is not really about how similar the facts are to each other -- its about which of the encoders two internal readout mechanisms each theory is secretly describing. Once we match each theory to the RIGHT mechanism, the theory that fits our actual retrieval-ranking channel predicts only a small, mild density increase (not a big jump), which narrows our prediction for the upcoming scale-up test and gives us a cheap way to check, for free, whether were right before spending GPU time.

summary: multihop_composition_gap_closure_scoping: re-clean-alone hypothesis REFUTED by direct code read (June-19 ConceptNet cell already hard-argmax-cleans every hop, still lost to BGE 0.451<0.502); decomposed to 2 lit-confirmed independent causes (branching-factor/to-many-relations needing beam not just cleanup; zero-semantic-content entity codes vs BGE pretrained semantics); proposed semantic-seed+beam cell, P_deflated HARD-PASS~0.15-0.20 / MIDDLE~0.40-0.45; refines noise-compounding taxonomy with a 3rd regime (reset present but codebook high-branching+semantically-empty)
plain_language: Looked at whether we can fix the substrate weak spot where it loses to a strong AI text-embedding model on multi-step knowledge-graph reasoning. Found the obvious fix (clean up noise at each step) was already built in and still lost -- so the real problem is two other things: the graph has many entities with multiple valid answers per step (confuses a single best-guess chase), and the substrate assigns entities totally random codes with no built-in meaning, unlike the embedding model which was pretrained on language. Proposed a cheap next experiment combining both fixes, honestly expect a partial improvement not a clean win.

summary: self_improvement_monitor_loop_scoping: specified the minimal narrow glass-box self-improvement MONITOR loop (observe margin+CV -> apply JL/Larsen-Nelson density law -> propose density adjustment -> external apply -> re-measure), composing self-audit ladder (Nelson & Narens monitor/control boundary), self-margin taxonomy (Family-1 order-statistic law), and density-scale reconciliation (m*(V) extrapolation) into one new rung. Two firing controls specified (scrambled-law, scrambled-CV, the latter borrowed from Dakos/Boettiger-Hastings surrogate-null early-warning-signal discriminator design per external lit-scan) to separate genuine self-improvement-proposal from trivial lookup. Zero marginal GPU cost -- rides on already-committed Stage-3 R1-R4 density sweep. Honest bound: narrow density-only special case, not the general portal -- self-margin taxonomy already failed one held-out transfer test (resonator K4 HARD_FAIL), 3 of 12 taxonomy rows are RESISTORS with no law to apply, and this loop closes exactly one knob against one scale axis. Named concrete generalization test (resonator restart-budget R, geometric-race law) as the required n=2 instance before claiming loop-shape transfers.
plain_language: We specified the smallest possible version of the substrate watching its own performance and suggesting a fix, without ever letting it change itself -- like a smoke detector that recommends opening a window but never opens it itself. It would observe how stable its retrieval accuracy is at different settings, apply a math formula we already validated to predict the right setting for a bigger dataset, and propose a specific number -- then a human decides whether to apply it, and we check afterward whether the suggestion was actually good, using two honesty checks (one that breaks the formula on purpose, one that scrambles the early-warning signal on purpose) to make sure it is not just copying a lookup table. This costs nothing extra to build since it reuses experiments already planned. The honest catch: this is a narrow one-knob version, not the general self-improvement capability, and the underlying prediction method has already failed once before on a different problem, so we are not overselling it.

summary: orthogonality-as-capacity-lever scoping: two distinct mechanisms found -- passive N_eff/PR correction (already in JL bound, log-compressed, ~1.5% effect, safe) vs active frame-theoretic decorrelation (Welch bound / ETF / quasi-orthogonality regime, larger ceiling but assumes free point placement our semantically-fixed codes lack). Dedup-retired margin-fix finding (177K, misses diffuse) does NOT refute the capacity-lever hypothesis -- wrong corpus (177K lacks 970Ks measured 15.86pct near-dup structure) and wrong dependent variable (margin distribution vs cliff location). Ranked levers: dedup (cheap safe) > targeted whitening (conditional on test) > semantic-region code allocation (highest ceiling, most invasive, unscoped). Cheap test folds a whitened-vs-baseline arm into the already-planned R1/R2 density sweep, zero new dispatch. Honest bound: full decorrelation is self-defeating for semantic retrieval per 2 independent papers; sweet spot is nuisance-direction-only decorrelation (dedup/mean-centering).
plain_language: We asked: can actively de-overlapping our stored memory codes let us pack in more items at the same quality, not just measure the overlap that is already there? The answer is yes in theory but with a real catch -- there are two very different ways to reduce overlap. The safe way (removing near-duplicate document chunks, already a known cleanup) gives a small, reliable gain. The aggressive way (forcing everything to be maximally spread apart) has a much bigger theoretical payoff but risks destroying the very similarity signal that retrieval depends on, per outside research on embedding whitening. We also showed that an earlier finding (dedup did not help retrieval on the small test corpus) does not disprove this idea -- it tested a different corpus and a different question, so the door stays open. We designed a cheap test that piggybacks on an already-planned experiment, no new compute needed.

summary: resonator_restart_budget_geometric_race_law: derived p_basin(K) bracket (Model A constant-ratio budget vs Model B accelerating wall, q=2 central) grounded in K-SAT/tensor/p-spin disordered-systems lit (exponential-in-order proliferation is the modal cross-domain pattern) vs resonator-founding-paper own graded/non-cliff F-sweep (reconciled via fixed-M,N regime difference); pre-registered p_basin(K5)=0.060(A)/0.030(B), p_basin(K6)=0.024(A)/0.003(B) against exp_resonator_ksweep_reachability_v1 own BUDGET/MIDDLE/WALL bands; on-disk smoke pilot (0/30 hits K5,K6) already statistically disfavors both models at p<1e-3, directional not confirmatory; delivered n=2 self-improvement-loop instance (OBSERVE oracle_any -> LAW geometric-race regime-branch -> PROPOSE R-for-target or WALL-flag -> gated by regime-discrimination control -> apply externally -> score) sharing common shape with the density-loop n=1 instance, one honest gap (Control-2 analogue not yet built to equal rigor).
plain_language: I worked out the math for how likely the resonator (a component that unscrambles multiple bound-together concepts) is to find the right answer as we ask it to unscramble MORE concepts at once (K=5, K=6), and how many retries it would take to get 95% reliable. Outside physics research on similar hard-search problems says this kind of difficulty usually gets dramatically worse (not just a little worse) as you add more things to untangle at once -- and an early low-confidence pilot test we already have on disk (zero successes out of 30 tries at K=5 and K=6) leans the same direction. My honest bet: the upcoming full test is more likely to show a real wall than an easy fix. I also showed this fits the same observe-predict-propose pattern as the other self-improvement-loop instance from today, which is the second proof point needed before calling that loop-shape a genuine repeatable pattern rather than a one-off.

summary: glass_box_qa_weakness_decomposition: scoped M3 QA benchmark as an error-attribution instrument (not scoreboard, per USER mid-drill reframe) -> ranked weakness map: composition/branching (HARD_FAIL, but decomposed via fresh on-disk smoke into 2 opposite-sign causes -- beam-width HELPS [RANDOM_BEAM 0.529 beats bge_cached 0.490], semantic-seeding HURTS [SEM_K1 0.216, worse than random baseline]); encoder-970K-scale (untested, density-law predicts m*=6 band[5,7]); self-audit 5th rung (smoke-proven, not canonical); per-item/per-stage LOGGING gap (verified missing on disk, status_log 2026-07-07T17:07:59Z) is the single blocker preventing clean attribution of everything else; refuse-gate (AUROC 0.958-0.999, strongest capability, protect not fix). Cheapest next steps: FULL multi-seed rerun of the already-smoked composition cell + a 200-row LLM closed-book pilot on the existing ConceptNet held-out split (contamination check).
plain_language: Scoped the next big benchmark for testing whether the substrate can genuinely answer questions using its own knowledge, self-audit its reasoning, and hold up against an LLM/encoder. Per USER direction, framed it not as a contest to win but as a diagnostic tool: the comparison exists to reveal exactly which capability (retrieval, multi-hop reasoning, self-checking, or knowing when to refuse) is weakest so we know where to focus. A fresh result found this session already shows why this matters: a combined fix looked like a flat failure, but breaking it into its two parts showed one half genuinely helps and the other backfires -- information an aggregate score would have hidden. The single biggest blocker found is not a missing capability but a missing logging layer: per-question detail is not currently being saved, so failures cannot yet be traced back to their cause at scale.

summary: Stage-4 advance-scouting: THE gate is genuine predictive generation (next-item prediction), not frame-slot structured decode (already solved, different task). 4 prior context-depth-extension cells (HD-bind accumulation) landed 3 HARD_FAIL + 1 MIDDLE_BAND, 0 HARD_PASS -- context makes predictions WORSE not better. Top probe: wire per-step CA3 cleanup into context accumulation (composes proven positional-bind + cleanup-attractor + hetero-associative readout), testing noise-compounding (fixable, same law as reasoning-depth) vs representation-capacity-ceiling (needs new context encoding). Startable now, freed GPU, zero Stage-3 dependency, cheap smoke go/no-go before FULL.
plain_language: Looked ahead at what Stage 4 (teaching the substrate to generate language on its own, no outside AI helping) actually needs before we build it. Found the substrate already has a proven way to lay out KNOWN sentences in order, but has NOT yet proven it can PREDICT new, unseen words the way a real language model must -- and it has tried and narrowly failed at this several times already when it tries to use more than one word of context. The next cheap test uses the freed-up GPU to see whether adding a self-cleaning step after each word (the same trick that already works for multi-step reasoning) fixes that problem, or whether the substrate needs a fundamentally different way of remembering context. Either answer teaches us something real and is ready to run now, in parallel with the current work.

summary: brain_predictive_generation_mechanism: ranked 5 brain predictive mechanisms for Stage-4 generation antidote. Successor representation (Dayan/Stachenfeld TD-bootstrap) and predictive coding (Rao-Ballard/Friston, Kalman-bounded error) both converge on: never accumulate raw context, accumulate only the prediction RESIDUAL via a bootstrapped delta-rule -- this is the DEEP version of the already-queued CLEANUP_PER_STEP GPU probe (shallow version: denoise raw-accumulated context after the fact). Hippocampal theta/replay literature corroborates but does not extend the already-queued shallow probe. Cerebellar forward models ruled out (wrong problem class -- cancels known self-generated noise, not unknown-external-content prediction). Composed build: PREDICT_RESIDUAL_TD arm (residual injection + TD-bootstrap W_hetero update + retained CA3 cleanup) as a sequenced follow-on to CLEANUP_PER_STEP on the same cell. P_deflated ~0.25-0.30. Flagged real risk: 0.507 concept-recall rate means ~half of predictions are wrong, so residual could be NOISIER not cleaner -- named as the specific HARD-FAIL condition.
plain_language: We asked how the brain predicts what comes next without its predictions getting noisier the longer it thinks -- since our substrate has the opposite problem (predictions get WORSE the more context we feed it). Two well-studied brain mechanisms (predictive coding and the hippocampal successor representation) both point to the same trick: the brain never piles up raw sensory history, it keeps a prediction, checks it against what actually happened, and only remembers the DIFFERENCE (the surprise), constantly refining its own predictor as it goes -- like a smart thermostat that learns your habits rather than a tape recorder that plays back everything it heard. We already had a plan to just clean up the noisy pile-up after the fact (like periodically wiping a whiteboard); this brain-grounded mechanism is deeper -- it stops most of the mess from being written on the whiteboard in the first place. We wrote up a concrete, cheap follow-on experiment for the team building experiments, sequenced correctly behind the cleanup-only test already queued, with an honest flagged risk that it could backfire if our next-word predictions are wrong too often.

summary: gen_noise_compounding_scour: fast targeted internal scour (no cell dispatch) confirms Stage-4 generation-build guidance already fully synthesized TODAY in research_brain_predictive_generation_mechanism_2026-07-07.md + companion; this scour only verifies-on-disk and tabulates. Prior generation cells: 3 HARD_FAIL (context_depth_hd_binding, trigram_concept_lm, wikitext_trigram_v3-smoke) + 1 MIDDLE_BAND (2ndorder_trigram_v2-GPU, the cell targeted for next arms). CA3-cleanup-on-generation is QUEUED not yet run (not a retread). SR/TD-bootstrap-on-W_hetero is genuinely novel; predictive-coding-as-residual-compression has one old pre-substrate positive precedent (EXP_lap2_9, HARD_PASS, legacy). No re-scan needed -- route straight to dispatching CLEANUP_PER_STEP + PREDICT_RESIDUAL_TD sibling arms per the already-filed decision-sequencing table.
plain_language: Did a quick, targeted search through our existing experiment records and notes (not a new deep-dive) to check whether the plan for building Stage-4 language generation was already worked out, so we would not waste time re-doing research we already did today. Found that the full answer already exists from earlier today: four past attempts at teaching the substrate to predict upcoming words got worse (not better) the more context we gave them, three failed outright and one showed a modest positive signal. The self-cleaning fix and the deeper brain-inspired predict-the-difference fix are both already designed and queued to test, and neither has actually been run yet, so there is nothing wasted -- we can go straight to running those tests.

summary: semantic-retrieval-capacity-decouple revival drill: pressure-tested 4 mechanisms to capture BGE semantic benefit without the store-collision that HARD_FAILED SEM_BEAM (0.227 vs RANDOM_BEAM 0.502). Decoupled retrieval-vs-storage (semantics-as-external-reranker, store untouched) is a real cheap untested revival candidate (2 convergent lit-scans: Hopfield/SDM correlation-degrades-capacity + IR retrieve-then-rerank practice). Sparse/low-overlap semantic codes (Willshaw f^2-scaling) is a genuine but expensive second-tier thread. Whitened in-store seeding is worst-fitted -- correlation IS the semantic signal here, and a new quantitative check shows classical alpha_c(rho) badly underestimates this store measured collapse (predicts ~4% loss at rho=0.20, actual ~55%), meaning the store already operates far past its classical wall.
plain_language: We asked: when semantic hints (from BGE embeddings) helped find related concepts but broke the memory store, is there a way to get the benefit without the breakage? Answer: yes, in one specific narrow way -- use the semantic hints only to break ties AFTER the memory-native search already ran, never inside the memory itself. That combination has not been tested yet but is cheap and low-risk to try. Two other fixes (making codes sparser, or mathematically whitening out the correlation) are less promising: one is expensive to build, and the other tries to remove exactly the signal that makes it semantic in the first place.

summary: self_improvement_regime_ranking_revival: density-loop HARD_FAIL re-read confirms genuine flat argmax (b~1e-15 across 3.5x V, not metric-limited) -- honest null, controls correctly silent. Ranked 5 candidate regimes for a non-trivial self-improvement law by (non-flatness x self-observability x controls-would-fire): rank-1 = reasoning-depth capacity-provisioning (CG-tier D=ln(FLOOR)/ln(p_hop_exact), Control-1-equivalent ALREADY measured on disk: naive-binary 2.02x biased vs exact-capture 0.98x unbiased, cross-cell replicated, zero new GPU cost); rank-2 = pre-identified resonator restart-budget (MM-tier, non-flat p_basin(K) 0.383->0.151, FULL not yet dispatched, own note predicts P=0.40 MIDDLE/WALL not clean pass); rank-3 = density CV-magnitude growth at fixed density (same HARD_FAILed corpus, narrower target, modest 57% growth over 3.5x V); rank-4/5 = compositional-math depth (reuse) and comprehension PR-substitution (MIDDLE_BAND); unconfirmed candidate = composition Hits@10 vs out_degree (computed in-code but not persisted in aggregate metrics, needs new instrumentation). Confirmed resonator regime is legitimate and worth dispatching regardless. P_deflated(non-trivial law demonstrable in >=1 regime)=0.50 capped; P_deflated(reasoning-depth specifically)=0.45.
plain_language: The self-improvement monitor loop correctly found nothing to learn about the best storage density -- that setting genuinely does not change as the dataset grows, confirmed by directly re-reading the failed test data (not a measurement-resolution problem, a real flat landscape). Rather than treating this as a dead end, I ranked five other places in the substrate where a similar self-improvement check could find something genuinely learnable. The best one, found sitting already-measured on disk at zero extra compute cost, is reasoning-chain depth: how far the substrate can chain reasoning steps before losing reliability changes sharply and predictably with how full its memory is, and we already have proof (on two separate test setups) that a naive guess is twice as wrong as the exact formula -- meaning the honesty-check machinery would have real signal to catch, unlike the flat density case. The resonator-unscrambling regime the team already had in mind remains a good second test, though it is a less certain, still-unrun candidate. Bottom line: self-improvement is not dead, it just needs the right regime -- and I found one that is cheaper and more promising than the one originally queued up.

summary: brain-grounding drill (resonator basin-proliferation): ranked 4 brain mechanisms (DG pattern-separation front-end top-ranked but mechanistically unproven per lit-scan; theta-gamma phase-slotting structurally correct but bigger redesign; WTA-sharpening and neurogenesis rank low/mixed). Found existing validated DGProjection primitive (hdlab/hippocampal_encoder.py) never wired to resonator. Proposed exp_resonator_dg_frontend_ksweep_v1 cell, BUILD-GATED on skunkworks confirming the K5/K6 smoke wall is genuine (not harness artifact).
plain_language: Studied how the brain avoids getting confused when it holds many bound items at once (the problem our factorization mechanism hits at K5-K6). Found a promising, cheap, already-built substrate primitive (a dentate-gyrus-style sparsify-and-expand front end) that has never been tried on this specific mechanism, plus a deeper but bigger brain-inspired redesign (sequential phase-slotting) as a longer-horizon option. The proposed test is on hold until skunkworks confirms the K5/K6 failure is a real wall and not a test-harness bug.

summary: brain-grounded self-capacity extrapolation: ranked 4 brain mechanisms (model-based prospective simulation from hippocampal-PFC preplay + RL theorem = top candidate; cerebellar forward models = negative prior, argues current approach is local not extrapolative; metacognitive uncertainty = trust-gate add-on not point-estimate fix). Disk-verified test: substituting measured collision_frac_emp for assumed fill in the survival-law phi() improves overall LOO MAE 1.20->1.06 and narrows the extrapolation-fold gap 1.86->1.75 err but still short of nearest-lookup (1.60) -- directional confirmation, not resolution. Proposed GPU-testable cell: derive a percolation/transmission-coefficient compounding law (matches Tier-1b mesoscopic-transport/percolation-critical-phenomena field-adjacency independently) + generate new provisioning levels beyond fill=0.3516 for genuine held-out extrapolation folds. HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL/MIDDLE bands pre-registered.
plain_language: Studied how the brain predicts outcomes it has never experienced (cerebellum, prospective hippocampal simulation, confidence/uncertainty), to see which mechanism could let the substrate predict its own reasoning-capacity limits beyond what it has actually measured. Found the most promising analog is model-based simulation from a learned dynamics model (not memory lookup), and already ran a free test on existing data showing a mechanism-grounded fix partially narrows the gap but does not fully close it yet -- next step is a concrete, cheap experiment proposal to test the fuller fix.

summary: content-gate brain-grounding: 3-way lit-scan (biased-competition/Desimone-Duncan, PBWM basal-ganglia, hippocampal CA3) converges on similarity-weighted (query-key) admission as the content-dependent gate primitive, structurally == modern-Hopfield attention (Ramsauer 2020). Proposes CONTENT_GATE vs RECENCY_GATE vs RAW on a variable-lag flagged-dependency corpus where the relevant slot index is uniform-random (recency-gate analytically bounded at 1/(K-1) recall) -- extends exp_substrate_gen_lm_contextgate_depth_v5.
plain_language: Tonight the substrate learned to ignore irrelevant older context, but only by always trusting the MOST RECENT thing said -- fine for simple chit-chat, useless the moment the important fact was said a while ago. This research maps how the brain actually picks the relevant memory by WHAT it is, not WHEN it happened (attention templates in visual cortex, dopamine-trained relevance gating in prefrontal/basal-ganglia circuits, and hippocampal content-based recall all reduce to the same trick: match-by-content). It proposes one concrete next test built to make recency-only strategies fail on purpose, so we can prove the smarter content-based version actually works before spending GPU time on it broadly.

summary: value-based action-selection (basal-ganglia Go/NoGo) brain-grounding: SCOUR-first finding overturns the premise -- the mechanism (SR-value Go/NoGo actor trained by cfrpe/RPE delta-rule, exp_pfc_gate_cfrpe_trained_v2) is ALREADY HARD_PASS (closure=0.661 @ V1200_d4, 2026-07-05), not a gap. Ranked 3 mechanisms (BG Go/NoGo=#1 confirmed-built; actor-critic/RPE=#2 same primitive different lineage; softmax-explore=#3 unused adjacent). Real gap = composition: v8 attention-routing gate (just CG-certified) and cfrpe BG value-gate have never been wired together (Chatham and Badre 2021 PLOS CompBio predicts they should be the same primitive at two loci -- input-gating vs output-gating). Proposed exp_pfc_bg_composed_attention_value_gate_v1: feeds v8 combined-gate output as the goal signal into the unchanged cfrpe Go/NoGo actor, with a mandatory scramble-gap telemetry-sensitivity guard (>=0.30) given tonights 2 metric-tautology incidents. HARD-PASS/MIDDLE/HARD-FAIL bands preregistered; P_deflated=0.38 (HARD-PASS), 0.50 capped (>=MIDDLE-BAND).
plain_language: We were told value-based action-selection (the brains reward-driven action-picking system) was the next missing piece. Scouring the existing experiment corpus first found it was actually already built and proven a few days ago, just for a different task (goal-directed navigation) -- so it is not missing. What IS missing is connecting that action-picker to the attention system we just finished certifying tonight, so attention decides what to pay attention to and the action-picker decides what to do about it, working together instead of separately. We designed the exact test for that connection, including a built-in check that catches a fake-looking pass (a problem that bit us twice tonight already).

note: GPU idle->picked up immediately; FULL 5-seed N8192 V1200 SR8000; post-ship verify pending on landing

summary: Built+smoked a CHEAP DIAGNOSTIC decomposing the ~0.507 concept-recall ceiling into CAPACITY (N/dim/code-crowding) vs SEMANTIC-FIDELITY (encoder teacher/objective). 6-arm ANOVA factorial (FULL/CAP_IDEAL/SEM_IDEAL/ORACLE/SEM_FIDELITY_IDEAL/SEM_CORR_IDEAL) at a substrate-faithful provisioned-N regime + per-factor sensitivity sweeps (N,sigma_e,rho) + a capacity-SATURATION credibility control (starved N). 3-seed SMOKE = HARD_SEMANTIC: load-bearing rank fidelity(+0.44)>correlation(+0.23)>capacity(+0.11); cos-to-target ceiling N-INVARIANT (N-effect 0.018 vs teacher-effect +0.46 -> capacity provably cannot buy fidelity); slopes dR/dN~5e-05 (saturated) dR/dSigmaE=-1.02 dR/dRho=-0.89. Capacity lever fires when starved (+0.55) and saturates when provisioned (+0.11), proving the semantic verdict is not a blind spot. KEY physics finding: capacity and semantic-fidelity are ENTANGLED through the argmax margin, so a clean capacity-only-wins regime is physically impossible; only cos-to-target isolates cleanly (and it is purely semantic). Self-test PASS (telemetry-sensitive; seed-moves-recall; arms-differ). Commit 2162f4b1e. SMOKE-local only; FULL handed to orchestrator for remote_cpu_queue (timeout 3600).
dispatch: handed_off_to_orchestrator (pause_state active; exp_dev does not ship remote)
plain_language: We do not yet know WHY the substrate can only recall a concept at about 50% fidelity. Two suspects: it does not have enough dimensions/space to keep concepts apart (a CAPACITY problem, fixable by making the vectors bigger), or the encoder that turns meanings into codes is just not sharp enough (a SEMANTIC-FIDELITY problem, only fixable by a better encoder/teacher). This cheap test builds a clean synthetic version of the problem and idealizes each suspect one at a time to see which one, when fixed, brings recall back. The smoke answer is clear: the ENCODER is the load-bearing weakness, not the dimensionality -- at the substrate's operating size, adding more dimensions barely helps (it is already saturated), while a sharper encoder recovers almost all the lost recall. We also proved the test is not rigged: in a deliberately dimension-starved setting it correctly flips to blaming capacity. Bottom line for strategy: invest in the encoder objective/teacher, not in bigger vectors. The full multi-seed run is queued for the orchestrator to ship.

note: encoder-fidelity-pivot GATE; FULL landing verify + 5-seed robustness + saturation-control deferred to landed-VET

summary: encoder-objective-beyond-BGE-distillation: 4-arm lit-scan (sparse coding/SAE, JEPA self-prediction, decorrelation-as-loss, contrastive SSL) plus 1 narrow pass on hybrid distill+decorrelation. Key mechanism finding: pure distillation is a ceiling (never repels off-target instances), so every candidate with a real exceeds-parity argument ADDS a repulsion/decorrelation/reconstruction term to the in-flight R1 distillation cell rather than replacing it. Ranked: 1) distill+VICReg-covariance-penalty (P=0.27, LOW effort, additive to running cell), 2) distill+sparse-coding-on-input auxiliary (P=0.30, MED effort, superposition mechanism), 3) distill+InfoNCE relational/dropout-view auxiliary (P=0.30, MED effort, SimCSE precedent), 4) JEPA-style self-prediction (P=0.16, HIGH effort, SEED lit shows opposite direction at matched data scale, consistent with substrate own PC-encoder HARD_FAIL). Cheap decisive test: add VICReg covariance term to R1, compare student off-target separation vs BGE own separation on same concept set.
plain_language: Researched how to train the concept encoder so it can genuinely beat the quality of the off-the-shelf teacher model (BGE) it currently copies, instead of just matching it. Finding: simply copying a teacher can never beat that teacher by definition. The promising fix is cheap: add one extra training signal (a term that pushes different concepts apart from each other, on top of the existing copy-the-teacher signal) to the encoder-fix experiment already in flight, then check directly whether the result separates concepts better than the teacher itself does. That single check will tell us in one experiment whether this direction is real.

summary: Authored+smoked teacher-cap-vs-student-underfit disambiguation cell (real BGE); smoke PASS -> OBJECTIVE_MISMATCH_SUBSTRATE_NATIVE. Committed cdfe7b465. FULL -> local_cpu_queue (BGE cache gitignored).
plain_language: The prior decomposition said our ~0.5 concept-recall ceiling is a SEMANTIC problem, but it used a fake teacher. This cell put the REAL BGE teacher and a substrate student on the SAME task/dictionary/cleanup to see who is actually the bottleneck. Two clean readouts on real BGE: (1) On the PRODUCTION superposition task (bundle 5 concepts, recall members ~0.5), the BGE teacher itself only scores 0.34 while the substrate sparse code scores 0.93 -- matching BGE geometry CAPS you; the substrate already beats the teacher by decorrelating. So training the student to imitate BGE harder is the WRONG fix; the distillation objective should be replaced with a substrate-native one (fix b). (2) On single-concept discrimination under noise, the teacher (0.998) keeps pointwise fidelity the sparse student (0.79) loses -- so the code family DOES leave some fidelity on the table there. Net: NOT plain student-underfit and NOT plain teacher-cap; it depends on the task, and for the load-bearing production task the answer is objective-mismatch. Teacher concept space is very crowded (median nearest-neighbor cosine 0.86, a third of concepts >0.90).

plain_language: Did a deep dive into how the actual brain (not chatbots) retrieves memories to reason, holds things in mind, decides what gets to update working memory, mentally previews multi-step paths before acting, and manages nested subgoals. The picture that emerged is NOT a single central controller asking questions and waiting for answers -- it is many small parallel gated loops, each independently tuned by reward-like signals, with memory held in two different ways (one actively sustained, one dormant-but-recoverable) and multi-step planning done by mentally replaying stored experience at high speed before committing to act. The most useful finding: an earlier substrate approach modeled on picking from a fixed menu of learned strategies failed outright, and the brain literature has itself moved away from that same fixed-menu idea toward a more flexible mix-and-match approach -- so this is a genuinely different, brain-backed way to try nested subgoal handling, not a rerun of what already failed.

summary: energy_scaled_selective_depth_nondestructive_refinement_brain_first: 4-angle brain-first drill on the confirmed phase_traversal HARD_FAIL (hard sign+topk quantization, structural_gain=-0.348). Brain never destroys-then-tries-to-recover: coarse-to-fine mechanisms are either (1) parallel intact channels / retained-trace pointers (magno-parvo, hippocampal indexing theory) or (2) formally Markov-degraded successive-refinement codes (Equitz-Cover condition, EZW-style). plain_language: We asked: how does the brain get a cheap quick-glance memory read and still allow a detailed deep-dive later, without throwing away the detail up front the way our failed phase-traversal encoder did? Answer: the brain never compresses-then-tries-to-decompress from a damaged copy -- it either keeps the full detail sitting untouched next to a cheap summary (like a hippocampal index card pointing at a full file), or builds the summary as a strict subset of the full thing (like progressive image loading) so nothing is ever truly lost. Best fix: point our already-proven un-squisher (it got 99.3% percent right when tested on uncompressed data) at the real detailed data for a short list of promising candidates, instead of the throwaway compressed version. Also flagged one genuinely new idea worth a cheap test: store a small leftover-detail sketch alongside the compressed version so we can reconstruct on demand without keeping the whole full-size copy for every single item.

plain_language: Looked at how the brain avoids compounding errors when reasoning many steps deep (the wall our deep multi-hop reasoning build is most likely to hit). Found the brain never fixes a noisy internal estimate by checking it against itself more carefully -- it always brings in an independent second source (a landmark, a second sensor, a reverse pass). Our two already-tried fixes for this substrate failure both checked the same noisy signal against itself and got essentially zero improvement -- this explains why, and proposes a genuinely different, brain-grounded fix (generate several complete candidate answers forward and backward, keep the one both directions agree on) with a clear pass/fail test.

plain_language: Studied how the brain reasons over a lifetime of memories without them interfering with each other as the store grows huge. Answer: it never dumps everything into one big blended pool -- it stores small pointers (not the content itself), lets frequently-used knowledge harden into a compact reusable template, and only ever activates the small neighborhood of memories relevant to the current context, not the whole store. This gives a concrete, testable design (and a cheap test) for keeping the substrate reasoning-quality flat as we grow the knowledge base 10-100x, instead of degrading as it grows.

plain_language: We asked: how does the brain actually write a new sentence or plan a new sequence of actions without the errors piling up step by step, the way our attempts have? Answer: it does not build up a running guess word by word -- it first quietly assembles a short, complete candidate answer offline by recombining real, already-known pieces of memory (like sketching a full draft before speaking), picks the best of several such drafts using a relevance-vs-recency judgment call we already built and proved works, then reads the finished draft out one piece at a time from a fixed, unchanging copy so nothing degrades as it gets longer. We also found out why our best deep fix for this failed: it double-checked its own guess against itself instead of against something independent, which is a known bad pattern. Proposed a cheap test that reuses parts we already have, no new building blocks needed.

plain_language: We looked at how five totally different fields (self-driving-car training, DNA-copying error-correction, spacecraft navigation math, physics coarse-graining, and evolutionary biology) all solve the same problem: how do you stop small errors from snowballing over a long chain of steps. All five gave the same answer -- the fix must come from checking against something genuinely separate from the thing that made the guess, not from double-checking a guess with more of the same guessing process. That exact flaw explains why our last four attempts to fix the deep-reasoning-chain problem all failed the same way -- each one checked the guess against another version of itself. We found the fix: check each reasoning step against the actual raw stored facts (not a processed estimate of them), and we already have live proof this works -- a different memory-routing test earlier today showed almost zero drift when grounded in raw content versus heavy drift when carried forward as a running guess. Proposed the next concrete test, kept the confidence appropriately modest since this is a fifth attempt on a wall that has resisted four times already.

summary: bounded-plan generation drift-free reframe: v9/v10/v11 3x INCONCLUSIVE_NO_COMPOUNDING diagnosed as a metric-wiring bug (compute_verdict/self-test never use the already-computed artifact-free intra_decline discriminator, gate on diluted mean body_token_acc drift instead); hand-recompute from existing v11 smoke JSON shows ACCUMULATE intra_decline 0.1667->0.2166 (clears DECLINE_MIN=0.12, growing) vs REPLAY 0.0/0.0 (flat) -- patched gate predicted to fire cleanly on data already on disk. Proposes cheap patch+rerun test plus a new capacity-collapse kill-test (matched (L+1)/N ratio at different scales) as the RIGHT positive depth-invariance cert.
plain_language: Three generation-mechanism test runs came back as inconclusive because the code was checking the wrong number -- when I recomputed the right number by hand from data already saved on disk, it showed the answer was actually a clean win all along (the growing-memory approach genuinely gets worse with length, the fixed-plan approach genuinely does not). I wrote up the exact one-line code fix needed to confirm this cheaply, plus a sharper follow-up test that would prove WHY it stays flat (a known, predictable capacity limit rather than a mystery).
