summary: stacked_independent_corrections_push_compounding_frontier: cross-domain drill on whether stacking a second independent correction channel with the just-landed KB-grounded gate (MIDDLE_BAND, frontier pushed entropy-8->12, decays 0.926/0.486/0.244 at d4/d6/d8) can extend the compounding-drift frontier further. Kinetic proofreading (p^N), concatenated codes, QEC cyclic suppression, and CoT-verifier theory all converge on multiplicative (not additive) error suppression from independent channels. Key caveat: clean ~0.51x/step decay + rising kb_fresh_rate (0.0->0.013->0.063) suggests a possible SHARED failure cause (fixed KB coverage vs growing branching factor) that would blunt stacking even if point-estimates pass the existing independence screen -- adds a new mandatory corr(failure_mask_A, failure_mask_B) pre-registration screen. Designs a cross-fit calibrated selector (disjoint sample-splitting, non-SR feature family) to OR-gate stack with the KB-gate. Buildable cell spec + falsifiable HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL/MIDDLE_BAND thresholds included.
plain_language: Our best fix so far for AI reasoning-chain drift (grounding each step against real stored facts) works but fades the deeper the reasoning chain goes. This drill asked: if we add a SECOND, genuinely different kind of check (a confidence gauge trained completely separately, not just a re-check of the same numbers), does combining two independent checks help much more than one -- the way DNA-copying uses multiple separate proofreading steps, or how error-correcting codes stack checks, to multiply reliability rather than just add it. Literature across four unrelated fields says yes IF the two checks fail independently. But the data hints the current fix might be running low on the same underlying resource (how many real facts are on hand) that a second check would also depend on -- so it might not be a free win. Proposes a cheap way to test this before building anything new.

summary: native_encoder_relational_vs_grounded_meaning: brain-first cross-domain drill (hub-and-spoke ATL neuroscience, symbol grounding problem, distributional-hypothesis ceiling, embodied-cognition minimal-grounding-channels -- 4 parallel Sonnet lit-scans) on whether teaching a relational-graph encoder is teaching language understanding. Convergent finding: relational/structural knowledge and grounded meaning are categorically different, not a scale gap -- Harnad dictionary-go-round + Bender-Koller octopus test + Coelho Mollo and Milliere Vector Grounding Problem all show relational closure cannot bootstrap reference regardless of density. Congenitally-blind color-knowledge study (Connolly et al PNAS 2007: color explains 23% of similarity variance in sighted vs 0% in blind subjects despite blind subjects verbally knowing color facts) is the sharpest empirical hollow-skeleton case. Cross-thread link: same structural pattern as this-session compounding-error 5x-drill (self-referential closure cannot manufacture the property it lacks -- needs an exogenous/independent channel) -- confirmed across two unrelated domains same day. Reframes the distillation ban: external text-model embeddings are themselves parasitic/second-hand-grounded (epistemic parasitism, Lyre 2024), so distillation would not even deliver primary grounding if permitted. Delivers a cheap no-new-build decisive test (relational-probe vs grounded-attribute-probe split on the existing encoder) plus a buildable self-contained minimal-grounding recipe (small externally-fed numeric-attribute seed set + transitive-inheritance test per Gunther et al 2018) with pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds.
plain_language: We asked cognitive science and neuroscience: when our reader learns how concepts relate to each other, is that the same thing as understanding language? The answer from four independent research fields (brain studies of meaning, philosophy of meaning, computational linguistics, and child language development) is a clear no -- knowing how things relate to each other is real and useful (like knowing the rules of chess), but it is a fundamentally different, incomplete thing from knowing what those things actually refer to in the world, and piling on more relational data cannot close that gap. The most striking proof is a real study of people blind from birth: they can correctly state that bananas are yellow, but that fact never actually influences how they group or judge fruit the way it does for sighted people -- true but functionally dead knowledge, which is exactly the risk with our current reader. Good news: the same research also gives a cheap, concrete, buildable recipe for real grounding without breaking our no-external-AI rule -- a small set of directly-measured (not text-derived) facts that should spread meaning outward through the existing relational graph -- plus an honest test to catch ourselves if we ever start faking it.

summary: brain_independent_channels: resolved the compounding-error-bound tension -- brain does NOT have only itself; it runs a graded portfolio of channels (Tier1 strong-independent: embodiment/action-loop, cerebellar climbing-fiber error, basal-ganglia arbitration, social correction; Tier2 partial-independent: predictive-coding sensory precision-weighting, CLS hippocampus/neocortex -- both share the exact shared-common-cause vulnerability the substrate KB-gate drill already found empirically). Principle survives fully intact with one amendment (independence of FAILURE MODE, not just architecture) already derived by the substrate 07-09 drill before this lit-scan even started -- brain confirms it independently. 5 buildable substrate designs proposed (KB-gate=Tier1 action-loop analog already built; cerebellar-analog different-model-family forward-checker; CLS-analog dual-store with raw-span common-cause guard; BG-analog non-representational veto criterion; failure-signature telemetry as standing diagnostic). Cheap decisive test: retroactive corr(kb_fresh_rate, cv) on already-landed KB-gate metrics -- tests whether substrate exhibits honest-uncertainty or confabulation/delusion signature.
plain_language: We asked: if bounding compounding errors needs an independent check, how does the brain do it with no external AI? Answer: the brain never had just itself -- it uses a ranked set of channels, from very strong (the physical world via action, a distinct cerebellar error signal, a separate basal-ganglia veto, other people) to partially-independent (sensory prediction-error and the hippocampus-cortex memory split, both of which can still share a blind spot). The brain confirms this itself: its worst failures (confabulation, delusions, dream logic, hallucination from sensory deprivation, echo chambers) all happen exactly when one of these channels is cut off or miscalibrated, never when a channel is healthy. For our substrate: the raw ingested knowledge already plays the role of the brain's sensory grounding, so being self-contained (no external AI model) was never in conflict with having an independent channel. We proposed a cheap, free test using data we already collected to check whether our existing knowledge-grounded check is behaving like a healthy brain channel or like a miscalibrated one, plus four more buildable channel designs modeled directly on cerebellum, hippocampus, and basal ganglia.

summary: grounding_cascade_depth_multihop_mechanism: brain-first cross-domain drill (4 parallel Sonnet lit-scans: hub-spoke recurrent-settling neuroscience, child-vocabulary-cascade developmental psych, graph-diffusion-depth theory, compositionality/VSA-binding) diagnosing why the just-measured HARD-PASS transitive-grounding-inheritance (near d1=0.63 vs far d3=0.48, decay 0.146, scrambled control flat) caps at 1 hop. Two-part convergent mechanism: (1) one-shot k-NN readout is the artificial analog of a feedforward pass not recurrent-attractor settling (O Connor/Cree/McRae 2009, Rogers et al 2021 eLife show graded depth requires many within-trial settling cycles; diffusion theory shows k=1 propagation mechanically realizes only the first spectral-gap-decaying term); (2) independently, Fodor/Pylyshyn 1988, Smolensky 1990, Plate/Kanerva/Gayler VSA lit unanimous that multi-hop transfer needs a chainable bind/unbind operator absent from near-random atomic codes -- both fixes compatible with keeping near-random store-codes (binding lets you keep orthogonal codes AND get compositional chaining). Child-vocab lit-scan: fast-mapping/cross-situational-learning are one-shot not compounding, but Smith/Jones 2002 trained shape-bias is a genuine accelerating cascade (reusable inductive template, a third distinct lever). Delivers 5 buildable directions each with pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds and P estimates (iterative-settling readout P=0.40 cheapest/highest-P no new data; bind-chain propagation P=0.30; multi-channel triangulation superadditive-per-multisensory-lit P=0.35; trainable inductive-bias transfer P=0.25 most novel; curriculum/bridging-order seeding percolation test P=0.30 free re-bin of existing data). Honest caveat flagged: if the two cheapest tests both HARD-FAIL, 1-hop is likely a structural floor for near-random-code-plus-similarity-readout requiring binding-operator construction as new build.
plain_language: We just proved a small set of hand-grounded facts genuinely spreads meaning one step outward through our concept map, but not further. This drill asked neuroscience, child-development research, graph-math, and symbolic-AI theory why it stops there and how to make it cascade further, the way a toddlers vocabulary explosion reaches far beyond words a parent directly taught. The answer converges from all four fields: our read-out only takes one quick pass instead of letting the signal settle over many cycles like a real brain does, and it has no way to chain two relationship-steps together compositionally (the striped-horse-implies-zebra kind of reasoning). Both are fixable without changing our core design. Child development research also points to a third, different lever -- a trainable shortcut habit (like a toddlers shape bias) that makes each NEW word easier once acquired, not just deeper reach on one word. Five concrete, cheap tests proposed, ranked by confidence, with built-in checks to catch fake-looking spread (noise smearing everywhere) versus the real thing.

summary: innate_scaffolding_core_knowledge_kernel: 5x deep brain-first cross-domain drill (4 parallel Sonnet lit-scans: infant core-knowledge VOE literature, numerical/spatial core-knowledge literature, nativism-vs-usage-based debate, proto-conceptual-primitive/bootstrapping literature) mapping what is innate in infants before language onto what to bake into the substrate. Convergent finding: innate kernel = small set of encapsulated domain-specific perceptual/relational analyzers (object persistence, agency/goal detection, DUAL number system, geometry, same/different comparator) each outputting sparse analog codes, plus a domain-general bootstrapping process (conceded innate on both nativist and usage-based sides). Sharpest lesson: parallel-individuation and ANS are doubly dissociated in infants (Hyde and Spelke 2011) -- independent biological confirmation of this project existing design lesson (self-margin taxonomy / correlation-hurts-capacity: build N distinct mechanisms not one). New cross-thread distinction: STRUCTURAL grounding (architectural bias on own input processing) is orthogonal to CONTENT grounding (external facts), partially resolving the earlier relational-vs-grounded tension. 4 buildable bake-in-vs-learn recommendations with HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds, P_deflated 0.30-0.40 (capped, novel-synthesis).
plain_language: We asked developmental science: what does a baby already know before it learns any words, and how should that shape what we build into our AI substrate from the start rather than making it learn everything from scratch? The answer: babies come with a handful of separate, specialized starter-kits (a sense that objects keep existing when hidden, a sense of who is an agent with goals, TWO separate number senses -- one for exact small counts like 1-3, one for rough big-number comparisons -- and a sense of shape/space), each producing simple abstract sketches, plus a general-purpose way of combining those sketches into richer ideas later. The clearest actionable finding: baby brains use genuinely different circuits for exact small counts versus rough big-number comparisons (confirmed by brain-wave studies), which matches something we already learned the hard way in our own system (do not force one mechanism to cover jobs with different scaling behavior -- build the right number of separate ones). We also found a helpful new distinction for our grounding problem: some real grounding does not require feeding in outside facts by hand -- it can come from building the right instinctual PROCESSING HABITS into how the system reads its own data, the way a baby is not taught object permanence, it is just wired to expect it. We proposed four concrete, cheap, testable build ideas ranked by confidence.

summary: meaning_growth_abstraction_compositionality_ladder: three-rung ladder (grounded->abstract via metaphor/conflation; abstract/concrete->compositional via bind/unbind operator, now triple-converged across 3 independent literatures this drill arc; compositional->referential via exogenous causal/social channel per Frege/Wittgenstein/Kripke/Quine, with genuine inferentialist minority dissent). New empirical precedent found: Papafragou/Cassidy/Gleitman 2007 belief-verb syntactic bootstrapping directly confirms a non-perceptual grounding-via-structural-position mechanism (P=0.40). Landau/Villion quantitatively falsifies semantics-alone bootstrapping (67.9%/39.9% vs 90.1%/70.1%). Systematicity (binding-sufficiency) predictions carry lowest P (0.20-0.25) given actively contested 2025-26 NN-systematicity literature.
sub_agents: research:sonnet x4 lit-scan (bootstrapping, metaphor/abstraction, compositionality/systematicity, philosophy of reference)
plain_language: Studied how human language meaning grows from concrete grounded concepts into abstract ideas (justice, because) and unbounded combinable sentences, and what philosophy says it takes for symbols to really mean something. Found a 3-step ladder: metaphor-based borrowing extends concrete meaning to abstract concepts; an explicit bind/unbind operator (already flagged by an earlier drill today) is required for open-ended sentence combination, now confirmed by three separate literatures; and full reference to the world needs a channel outside the symbol system itself, per multiple classic philosophers, though one dissenting camp argues rich internal practice alone might suffice. This gives concrete next experiments and clarifies which of our design choices (near-random codes, needing a binding operator) are well-supported by outside science.

summary: social/interactive language acquisition (5x drill): 4 parallel lit-scans (Tomasello usage-based, CDS/negative-evidence, theory-of-mind, Wittgenstein/Steels/emergent-communication) converge on a split: referential GROUNDING needs a partner-like informationally-independent channel (Kuhl 2003 live-vs-recorded ablation; SimSiam NoCom 11%/0.04-align vs SSNG 59%/0.83-align); grammatical productivity/error-recovery does NOT (Taatgen & Anderson corpus-only existence proof). Verdict: self-contained substrate should build an internal asymmetric-view Speaker/Listener self-play loop (bandwidth-capped message, success/failure signal, NOT external-LM distillation) over the already-proposed externally-fed seed-referent set, not rely on ingested data alone for grounding. P_deflated(lit consensus)=0.55-0.60; P_deflated(novel substrate-sufficiency claim, capped)=0.35-0.40.
plain_language: Studied how children actually learn language through social interaction (joint attention, caregiver responsiveness, theory of mind, and language-games research going back to Wittgenstein and modern AI multi-agent-communication experiments). The clearest finding: kids (and AI agents in matched experiments) that only get passive exposure to language, with no communicative back-and-forth, fail to develop real grounded meaning -- but a lot of grammar-learning does NOT need correction/feedback, just enough data. For our substrate: this argues for building an internal self-play speaker/listener loop (two views of our own system playing a naming game against each other) as the grounding mechanism, rather than assuming ingesting more data alone will get us there -- while keeping the no-external-AI-model rule intact.

summary: developmental trajectory: 6-stage curriculum-order map (prelinguistic tuning -> joint attention -> first words -> vocab spurt -> word combos -> grammar), each stage gated by a specific prior-stage output (tuned phonemes, reference-binding, instance-density thresholds); several classic discontinuities (9-month revolution, vocab spurt) directly contested in 2024-25 lit as aggregation artifacts of averaging individually-smooth trajectories.
plain_language: Researched how babies actually learn language, month by month, and what triggers each new skill (babbling -> pointing/eye contact -> first words -> vocabulary explosion -> two-word sentences -> grammar rules). Found a clear recommended training order for our substrate: pure statistics first with no labels, then a small labeled seed set, then scale vocabulary past a size threshold before introducing sentence-level/relational training. Also found that some famous "sudden leap" moments in child development (the 9-month joint-attention leap, the vocabulary explosion at 18 months) are now seriously questioned by newer research as just an illusion from averaging many different kids together, not a real sudden change in any one child -- an important calibration for not over-engineering our substrate around a threshold that may not really exist.

summary: neural_substrates_language_brain_architecture_5x_drill: brain-first drill on dual-stream (Hickok-Poeppel), modern Broca/angular-gyrus, neural-reuse/recycling (Anderson, Dehaene, FOXP2/Ullman basal-ganglia, mirror-neuron F5-Broca, hippocampal-spatial-to-conceptual), critical/sensitive periods (Hensch, Kuhl, Saffran, Hartshorne-Tenenbaum-Pinker), and prediction-as-core-computation (surprisal, N400 pre-activation, cerebellar rTMS). Core finding: brain language network is dominantly REUSE of older general modules (basal-ganglia sequencing, cerebellar forward-model, hippocampal relational-mapping, ATL conjunctive-binding) stitched by a thin new WHITE-MATTER overlay (arcuate fasciculus expansion), not a bespoke module -- validates substrate strategy of composing hdlab primitives via thin cortex.py routing rather than building a monolithic language component. Substrate HAS analogs of VWFA/ATL-hub/DG-CA3/basal-ganglia-Go-NoGo/neuromodulators/predictive-coding/sequence-generation. MISSING: (1) dorsal-stream form-to-form repetition shortcut bypassing the semantic hub (cheapest, most concretely testable -- same conflation-of-jobs shape as the 2026-07-02 VWFA/ATL/CLS monolith finding), (2) Broca-analog recursive/hierarchical structure-builder (converges same-day with the multi-hop grounding-depth drill finding the same missing recursion operator), (3) cerebellar-forward-model wiring explicitly into generation.py (cross-thread with independent-channels compounding-error drift note), (4) a genuine developmental plasticity-decay schedule per linguistic level (most speculative, extrapolated substantially from visual-cortex critical-period biology).
plain_language: We studied how the human brain builds language circuitry by reusing much older brain systems (motor sequencing, spatial mapping, error-correction) rather than growing new dedicated organs, and mapped that onto our own system. Our system already has good analogs for several brain pieces (a word-shape reader, a meaning hub, a memory-completion system, a reward-based action-picker). It is missing a fast shortcut for verbatim repetition that skips the meaning step (the way a stroke patient can repeat words fluently but not understand them, or vice versa), and a way to build nested/recursive structure (like nested clauses in a sentence) -- both are cheap to test using pieces we already built.

summary: selfplay_shared_estimator_independence: 4 parallel Sonnet lit-scans (brain internal-channel differentiation, SSL collapse-prevention theory, emergent-communication weight-tying, formal ensemble/Kalman/self-distillation theory), retargeted mid-drill per USER correction onto the MECHANISM question (possibility of internal self-partnering is settled/closed by brain evidence -- CLS, cerebellum, basal ganglia, hemispheres are genuinely differentiated computational devices, not two copies of one estimator). Convergent finding across all 4 literatures: a SHARED-WEIGHT Speaker/Listener differing ONLY in information access (a mirror) is NOT sufficient for uncorrelated failure modes -- SimSiam/BYOL/DINO ablations show symmetric-info-asymmetric-weights still collapses without added parameter/gradient asymmetry; emergent-comm literature has no validated shared-weight self-play success case (Galke/Ram/Raviv 2022 name this as an open gap); formal ensemble/Kalman/self-distillation theory proves failure-correlation never reaches zero from architectural variation alone, only from disjoint-randomness (Neyman-orthogonal cross-fitting). Named 4 minimal-differentiation axes ranked cheapest-to-costliest (disjoint data/cross-fit; parameter-lag EMA; differentiated objective; differentiated learning-algorithm-class) with a 4-arm cheap decisive test (B0 naive mirror vs B1 EMA-lag vs B2 cross-fit vs B3 population+speed-asymmetry) using the stacked-corrections corr(failure_mask) screen. P_deflated 0.60-0.65 (differentiation-required finding), 0.25-0.30 (cross-fit transfers to substrate, capped), 0.12-0.15 (load-bearing negative that even proven fixes fail).
plain_language: We asked: our plan to have the AI system practice describing things to itself (one part sees the full picture and describes it, another part only sees the description and has to guess what is being described) -- does that actually teach it real grounded meaning, or is it just talking to a mirror that shares all its own blind spots? The brain proves an AI system CAN be its own training partner (memory systems, the two hemispheres, and a specialized movement-correction brain region all check each other internally, no outside partner needed) -- but only because those internal parts are genuinely DIFFERENT machines with different rules, not the same machine looking at itself from two angles. Machine-learning research says the same thing very clearly: if the two describing/guessing roles literally share the same brain and only differ in what they can see, they tend to fail in the exact same places (a mirror sharing blind spots), matching a problem we already found in one of our cells this morning. We named four concrete, cheap fixes ranked from cheapest to most expensive, and a measurable pre-check to run before trusting any future self-practice-based grounding result.

summary: selfplay_upstream_blindspot_brain_fix (5x negative-drill): four independent lit-scans (CLS/hippocampus-neocortex, predictive-coding/exogenous-ground, precision-weighting/arbitration, dentate-gyrus pattern separation + failure modes) converge: the brain fixes a shared-upstream blind spot via UPSTREAM PATTERN SEPARATION (DG-style random expansion + competitive sparsification decorrelating the shared representation before any split), not via downstream reconciliation (replay/wake-sleep = content-transfer/stabilization, orthogonal to independence) or precision-weighting/dynamic arbitration (proven CONSUMER not PRODUCER of independence across 3 sub-literatures -- ruled out as a standalone fix). Failure-mode evidence (folie a deux, confabulation, incomplete split-brain) directly confirms the negative: shared upstream corruption produces shared downstream errors no downstream differentiation can fix. Minimal buildable fix for B1 (disjoint-data cross-fit, corr=0.77->0.39, grounding~0.60): layer a fixed independently-seeded sparse random-projection + top-k sparsification stage per branch at the shared-representation boundary (zero new learned params, cheap CPU cell), with a corr(failmask)<=0.20 + grounding>=0.50 HARD-PASS bar and a diagnostic HARD-FAIL that redirects to an exogenous-referent mechanism if representation-level fix is insufficient. Includes a cheap negative-control arm (precision-weighting gate alone, predicted to fail) to falsify the ruled-out candidate empirically.
sub_agents: research:sonnet x4 lit-scan (CLS/wake-sleep, predictive-coding/exogenous-ground, precision-weighting/arbitration, dentate-gyrus/failure-modes)
plain_language: Following up on this morning finding that two halves of our AI system training against each other (a describer and a guesser) could not become independent enough just by showing them different data -- we asked how the brain solves this exact problem, since the brain constantly runs multiple internal checking systems (memory replay, two hemispheres, model-based vs habit-based decision-making) that all ultimately see the same raw senses. The clear answer across four separate research threads: the brain decorrelates BEFORE splitting, not after -- a specific brain region (the dentate gyrus, part of the hippocampus) takes incoming information and scrambles/sparsifies it into a much larger, more spread-out code before it ever reaches the comparison circuitry downstream, which is the same trick used elsewhere in the brain (hippocampus vs cortex use genuinely different coding styles on the same input, not just different data). We also found what does NOT work: a smart moment-to-moment trust dial (dial up the more reliable one right now) cannot fix this, because it only works once the two halves are already different -- it cannot create the difference. Same for a memory-reconciliation loop -- helpful for keeping the two halves coherent, but not what makes them independent, and can even undo the fix if done carelessly. We designed one cheap next building step directly from this: add a fixed, randomized scrambling-and-sparsifying stage before the split, with clear pass/fail numbers, plus a cheap side-test that should fail (the trust-dial-only approach) to confirm we understood the brain evidence correctly.

summary: Prediction-error as native learning signal (brain-first, 3 lit-scans): predictive coding is a well-established LOCAL learning rule (Rao-Ballard/Whittington-Bogacz) where the SAME error signal drives inference+learning by construction; viable as an ADDITIONAL learning axis alongside the existing no-gradient contrastive-Hebbian channel (testbed/substrate_lm/primitives.py), not a replacement -- prediction has its own collapse mode (regression-to-mean, CPC exists because pure prediction alone risks this). Disk-verify found the substrate ALREADY has a landed Spoke1 predictive-coding cell family (2026-07-02): v2 HARD_PASS with PRED-only arm (gap=0.566) actually beating its own HYBRID arm (gap=0.517); toughest apples-to-apples stress test landed MIDDLE_BAND (not HARD_PASS) so promising but not closed. Grounding cross-link: predicting the real ingest stream (not self-generated) instantiates TWO of the four differentiation axes from the same-day self-play drill (exogenous-data + algorithm-class-split) for free, making it a cheap partial instance of structural grounding -- but ML lit is explicit this does NOT equal full Harnad-sense referential grounding (contested next-token-prediction-as-grounding debate).
plain_language: We asked whether the substrate should learn representations by predicting its own next input (like how brains predict what comes next) instead of, or alongside, its current similarity-based learning rule. The brain evidence says yes, this is a real, cheap, additional learning channel worth adding -- and we found the substrate already partially tested this a week ago with promising (if not fully conclusive) results we had not previously surfaced. We also found a plausible, low-cost way this could double as the missing exogenous anchor for the self-play grounding problem, though this is a bigger, less-proven bet than the encoder-side finding.

summary: encoder_clean_composable_relational_codes: brain-first 4-lit-scan drill on typed-binding HARD_FAIL (role-recovery=0.282 vs ~1.0 needed) -> sparsity is primary interference lever (Treves-Rolls), recovery-vs-sparsity is a sharp phase transition not gradual (Donoho-Tanner), binding-consistency training objective is best-quantified lever (MLC near-0pct->99.78pct), resonator-cleanup stops per-hop compounding. 4-lever buildable stack + cheap no-retrain decisive test. P_deflated(combined HARD-PASS)~0.30.
plain_language: We drilled into why the encoder cannot chain typed relations past 1 hop (it recovers the right role only 28pct of the time when it needs to be near-perfect). Brain research on how the hippocampus keeps memories from blurring together, plus the math of sparse signal recovery, both point the same direction: this kind of failure is a sharp cliff, not a dial you can nudge -- you need several fixes together (sparser codes, a training signal that explicitly rewards clean binding, and an iterative cleanup step) to jump across it, not one small tweak. We designed a cheap, no-retrain test to check the easiest fix first before committing to a bigger rebuild.

summary: exogenous_referent_grounding_predictive_coding: brain-first 4-lit-scan drill (predictive coding/active inference, sensorimotor contingency, Harnad categorical perception, causal representation learning) on the minimal exogenous-referent grounding mechanism following the confirmed DG_XFIT HARD-FAIL (corr=0.377, improvement=0.015, grounding=0.589 -> REPRESENTATION_INSUFFICIENT_REDIRECT_EXOGENOUS, 3rd internal-only grounding negative). Live-verified finding: strongest direct support is Pezzulo/Parr/Cisek/Clark/Friston 2023 (passive prediction explicitly insufficient for genuine understanding, active intervention load-bearing) + Coelho Mollo/Milliere 2023 (teleosemantic condition also unmet) -- corrects an initial closed-loop-DPI framing that turned out to be thin/unreplicated (single 2026 self-play paper) rather than classical doctrine. Harnad transitive-grounding gets a real quantitative anchor: Vincent-Lamarre et al 2016 shows a ~1pct-of-vocabulary MinSet suffices to transitively reach a full dictionary; Greco/Caneva 2010 robotic study shows 51pct novel-composition accuracy from 9 grounded primitives. Recommended next cell: B1+EXOG (wire prediction-error-against-real-ingest-data as shared reconstruction target for both self-play branches, composing directly with the already-scoped W_pred predictive-coding matrix and the already-HARD-PASSED transitive-spread + Prediction-C perturbation screen).
plain_language: After three confirmed negatives showing the substrate cannot manufacture real-world meaning purely from its own internal machinery, we asked the brain literature what the missing exogenous ingredient actually is. The clearest, best-cited answer: predicting real (non-self-generated) data is a genuine, partial anchor -- but the strongest brain research (co-authored by one of the field founders) says passive prediction alone is explicitly NOT enough for full understanding; the system also needs to act on and test its models against the real world, which we do not yet have. We also found solid, quantitative brain-and-robotics evidence that a very small set of directly-grounded concepts can spread meaning to a much larger vocabulary through composition alone, giving a concrete, buildable design: ground a small seed via real-data prediction, let existing propagation spread it, and verify with a perturbation test. This is a real forward step, honestly bounded as partial, not full, grounding.

All four angles came back the same way: internal-only tricks can only cancel out random noise, not the shared systematic mistake both halves are making together -- so real external data really is the right next move, not a shortcut we skipped.

summary: sparse-compatible binding operator: block-local circular convolution (LCC, Frady/Kleyko/Sommer arXiv:2009.06734) on the existing k-WTA block code preserves sparsity by construction (bound output stays exactly as sparse as input) and measures ~0.95 unbind fidelity vs ~0.80 dense-conv-on-sparse vs ~0.30 plain Hadamard-on-sparse; pair with resonator/factorizer iterative cleanup (Hersche et al arXiv:2303.13957) as the CA3-pattern-completion analog for multi-hop retrieval. Brain evidence: none of synchrony/dendritic-coincidence/expansion-sparsification bind sparse codes with a single reversible algebra either -- brain uses modular grid-module RNS-style composition then a SEPARATE denser CA3 stage for retrieval, matching the RANK1+RANK2 proposal. P_deflated=0.40 compound (reach>=2 + DG-expansion net-positive + composes with binding-consistency objective), 0.55 for the narrower sparsity-preserving-fidelity claim alone.
plain_language: We looked at how the brain combines sparse (mostly-off) signals without breaking them, since our own sparse-code experiment made things worse instead of better. Turns out the brain never does one big all-at-once combination either -- it combines small local pieces and then uses a separate cleanup step to look information back up. We found an existing, already-tested engineering recipe that does exactly this, and propose swapping it in as a concrete next build-and-test step.

summary: active-intervention query-selection: 4-lit-scan synthesis (active inference/BALD, efference-copy comparator, developmental manipulation, interventional causal discovery) converges on per-branch own-uncertainty-driven KB-query selection (not literal embodiment) as minimal buildable mechanism; B2_ACT cell = single changed sampling line in landed exp_selfplay_b1_exog_predictive_anchor_v1.py; flags 3-consecutive-mechanism corr~0.38 plateau as structural-ceiling warning (DG 0.377, B1 0.393, B1_EXOG 0.382); P_deflated=0.30
plain_language: Following up on todays passive-prediction result (which grounded but did not decorrelate the two self-play halves), we researched what makes ACTION different from passive prediction in brains: it is not physical movement itself but (1) each learner choosing its own distinct thing to test against based on its own uncertainty, plus (2) an internal predict-then-compare mechanism that isolates what came from the real world. We designed a minimal, cheap way to build this: instead of both halves testing themselves against a randomly-picked real-data example, each half picks the example it is currently MOST unsure about. This is a single changed line in the already-built experiment, not a new architecture. We also flagged a warning sign: three different fix attempts today all landed at nearly the same decorrelation score (~0.38), which could mean the bottleneck is somewhere else entirely (the shared communication channel both halves use) -- if a fourth attempt lands there too, we should stop tweaking the data/objective and look at the channel itself.

summary: learned-code crosstalk / decorrelation-at-scale 5x drill: 3/4 lit-scans landed (hippocampal child synthesized from established neuroscience, flagged unverified-this-cycle). Convergent mechanism across hippocampal/cortical-kWTA/VSA-resonator angles = repeated LOCAL per-hop re-sparsification+comparator gate that strips only incidental redundancy, never semantic correlation (Chalk/Marre/Tkacik PNAS 2018 is the sharpest formal statement of this floor). VSA/resonator capacity theory (Frady/Kent/Olshausen/Sommer) confirmed built entirely on i.i.d./quasi-orthogonal codebook assumptions -- correlated-codebook regime is an OPEN literature gap, not a solved problem we missed. Two Stage-4 candidates pre-registered with one-line discriminators: (1) per-hop DG-style re-separation gate (fresh sparse random re-encoding between hops), (2) CA1-style comparator/residual gate (forward only unpredicted component between hops). Honest ceiling: brain does not beat the correlated-crosstalk limit, it pushes it back via per-hop cleanup while accepting a hard semantic-correlation floor, and keeps functional chains short (transitive inference ~4-7 items) relying on hierarchical chunking, not unlimited chaining.

plain_language: Studied how brains keep overlapping memories chainable without their similarity scrambling multi-step recall. Found: insert a cleanup checkpoint between every retrieval step that resorts and filters for novelty, but never fully separate genuinely related memories (that would destroy the meaning). Gives Stage-4 two concrete buildable ideas plus an honest expectation-setter: even brains only reliably chain about 4-7 steps, so aim for reach 2-3 recovery, not unlimited depth.

summary: same_different_identity_bakein_primitive_2x: 4-lit-scan drill (neuro/infant core-knowledge, comparative-cognition/animal, computational-architecture, VSA/HDC realization) converges on comparator-over-individuated-representations-exposing-only-a-relation-value as minimal mechanism for abstract same-different. Item-level identity match is a free structural VSA primitive (fixed similarity on quasi-orthogonal codebook, no training, generalizes to novel items by construction) -- P_deflated=0.55. Relational/second-order same-different (RMTS, relation-between-relations) requires explicit bind/unbind relation-extraction, is genuine novel synthesis for this substrate, and every literature (brain set-size-expansion phase transition, human/nonhuman RMTS discontinuity debate, CNN feature-entanglement straining, VSA structural/semantic-similarity conflation) independently flags it as capacity-limited, not free -- P_deflated=0.30 capped. Concrete bake-in: fixed-threshold similarity comparator (item tier) + unbind-then-compare relation extractor (relational tier), both with pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL on held-out novel items, no retraining needed.

plain_language: We asked how brains and machines tell things apart as SAME or DIFFERENT, and whether it can be built in rather than learned. Answer: recognizing that two things you can look at side by side are the same or different comes essentially for free in our substrate already, the same way it appears very early and cheaply in brains and even pigeons -- so we can bake that in immediately at no cost. Recognizing that two RELATIONSHIPS are the same kind of relationship (a harder, more abstract version) is genuinely harder everywhere we looked -- animals need thousands of examples, plain neural nets famously fail it, and our own vector math has a known conflation problem there too -- so we are pre-registering that harder version honestly as the next rung, with a fair pass/fail bar, not pretending it will just work.

summary: reader decisive multi-hop win-engineering: 4-angle convergent lit-scan (VSA/Hopfield capacity theory, error-correction-below-threshold coding theory, resource-throw diminishing-returns, path-as-object vs step-by-step chaining) finds Stage-4 MIDDLE_BAND signature (decay_slope unchanged -0.129 vs -0.128 despite cleanup) matches operating ABOVE a capacity-correction threshold in 3 independent literatures. Dominant win-lever = combine exponential-capacity dense-Hopfield cleanup + path-as-single-bound-object encoding (linear-in-length noise budget) + 8x N resource-throw to decisively cross the threshold, not more per-hop-gate tuning. Stage-5 cell exp_grounding_multihop_decisive_win_v1 designed with 7 arms, real WIN bar (reach2>=0.60, reach3>=0.35, gain2>=0.30, slope-flatten>=40pct), P_deflated=0.38.
plain_language: We asked what it would take to make the reader chain 2-3 hops of real knowledge DECISIVELY, not marginally. The math says our system is sitting on the wrong side of a capacity cliff -- cleanup gave a flat boost but did not change the rate memory quality was crashing hop over hop, which matches how error-correction and memory-capacity theory behave just above a critical threshold in three unrelated fields of math. Since we are not stuck with the brains 20-watt budget, the fix is to spend real compute to shove the system decisively across that cliff: a richer cleanup style with room for exponentially more memories, dimensions scaled up 8x, and encoding a whole multi-step chain as one object read out in a single pass instead of three separate noisy hops. We designed a concrete next experiment with a real win bar and an honest, checkable risk (if the overlap between memories is genuine shared meaning rather than sloppy encoding, no amount of compute fixes that, and the experiment is built to tell us honestly if that is what we are facing).

summary: reader load-reduction win-path: 3-angle lit-scan (sparsification, decorrelation/decoupling, structured/Hopfield capacity) converges on the naive dim_needed=79286 bound being dominated by CODEBOOK COUNT (D_f=n_nodes=4440, global vocabulary) not correlation. Back-solving the landed metrics.json df_over_n formula confirms D_f=n_nodes exactly. Substituting local graph-neighborhood branching factor (mean_degree=6.65) for the global count collapses dim_needed to ~119 (1-hop) to ~5250 (3-hop upper bound) -- a ~670x reduction, feasible at dim<=8k with large margin, no new dimension scaling required. Two-layer chain-index (near-orthogonal, block-sparse LCC bound, restricted to true graph-local candidates) + unchanged correlated semantic layer, linked by a DISCRETE node-identity lookup (not an associative map) is the concrete design; HippoRAG (arXiv:2405.14831) is the closest validated real-world precedent (index+PageRank vs dense-embedding split) though not fetched at full fidelity this cycle -- flagged for follow-up verification. Sparsification (log/constant-factor per Willshaw/Palm optimum) and dense-Hopfield/kernel capacity (degrades under correlation per fetched sources) are real but secondary multipliers on the correlation-tax, not the count-tax that actually dominates. P_deflated=0.38.
plain_language: Yesterdays experiment said we need a huge (79,000-dimension) memory to make multi-step reasoning chains work reliably. We checked the math behind that number and found it assumes every retrieval step must stay distinguishable from every single fact we have ever stored (about 4,440), when really, at each step in a chain you only need to stay distinguishable from the handful of neighbors actually connected to where you are (about 7). Correcting that drops the requirement from 79,000 down to the hundreds -- smaller than what we already use. The fix is a small local address-book layer (like the hippocampus uses) sitting in front of the existing rich meaning layer, not a bigger, more expensive memory.

summary: construction_proof_to_capability_bridge: 3-lit-scan synthesis (ML probing/causal-interp epistemics, developmental core-knowledge deployment signature, compositional-generalization benchmark design) converges on identical 3-part criterion for construction-proof vs capability: different-channel + live-alternative + necessity-under-ablation (Hewitt/Liang selectivity, Geirhos shortcut-learning, Geiger/causal-scrubbing necessity-sufficiency, Baillargeon-vs-Diamond/Munakata looking-vs-reaching, COGS in-dist-vs-systematic gap). Audit verdict: landed-VET same-different tiering was CORRECT (construction-proof, not capability); all 3 bake-in MMs (dual-number, object-permanence, same-different) share the same untested-capstone status -- track needs Stage-2 capstone before capability credit. Capstone design delivered: distractor-merge gate inside multi-hop retrieval, measured on final answer accuracy (not the gate itself), real-vs-ablated-vs-chance conditions, dose-response over distractor count, pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL. P_deflated=0.35-0.65 by claim.
plain_language: We asked why a perfect experimental pass got downgraded instead of counted as a win, and used that to design a fix for the whole bake-in track. Answer: three unrelated research fields (AI evaluation, infant psychology, and language-learning benchmarks) all agree on the same 3-step test for telling apart proof-the-math-works from the-system-actually-uses-it: test it a different way than it was built for, make sure it could have failed, and check that removing it actually breaks something. By that test, our three built-in senses (numbers, object permanence, same-different) have only cleared step zero -- proven as wiring, not yet proven as used. We designed one concrete next experiment to close that gap: hide the same-different check inside a bigger multi-step retrieval task, never grade it directly, and confirm the bigger task gets measurably worse when we swap the real check for a coin flip, especially as the task gets harder.

summary: multihop_test_fairness_brain_goal_directed_traversal: 3-angle brain-first drill finds (source,relation)->single-sibling query is intrinsically underdetermined per convergent evidence from PFC goal-maintenance + hippocampal goal-modulated replay/VTE (brain never asks this question memorylessly), transitive-inference probe design (always specific pairs, never open queries), DB functional-dependency/Hadamard well-posedness theory, and KG query-embedding set-semantics (GQE/Query2Box/BetaE). VERDICT: our v3 win-cell test is unfair-by-construction; decoupled-codes regression reinterpreted as removing an accidental disambiguating correlation signal, not a genuine architecture failure. Proposes zero-compute re-scoring test (SET-ACCEPTING + GOAL-CARRYING framings) on already-landed v3 data before funding further architecture cells.
plain_language: We asked whether our failing multi-hop memory test is even fair, by looking at how real brains handle the same situation (following a fact from something with several possible next steps). Brains never guess blindly from just the starting point and relationship type -- they hold an active goal in working memory and preview candidate next-steps weighted toward that goal before committing. Classic memory-reasoning lab tests and modern AI multi-step-question systems both independently confirm the same rule: that kind of question only has one right answer if you add a goal or extra context; otherwise it is a coin-flip by design, not a capability gap. This means our recent test failure may be measuring an unfair question, not a real wall -- and we have a cheap, zero-new-compute way to check by re-scoring data we already have.

summary: autonomous_subgoal_derivation: 3-angle lit-scan (hippocampal replay/SR/bottleneck; PFC/HRL subgoal decomposition; VSA/HDC realization) converges on generate-and-verify + real-local-structure recombination as the only precedented waypoint-generation pattern; unbind-and-solve-for-X (original leading hypothesis) is the weakest-precedented option with one negative result found. Proposed substrate mechanism: greedy landmark-seeded hop selection reusing existing local-neighborhood scoping + already-certified goal-cosine bias, no new primitive. Discriminator: autonomous reach@2 >=0.40 HARD-PASS vs <0.20 HARD-FAIL (vs supplied-waypoint ceiling 0.500 / memoryless floor 0.121). P_deflated=0.38.
plain_language: We asked how a system could figure out its own waypoint toward a goal, instead of being told one. Brains and AI planners both turn out to reuse real, already-known local structure and check-before-committing rather than inventing a step from nothing -- so we propose the substrate do the same: look at its real nearby neighbors, pick whichever looks most like the goal, and verify it is actually getting closer before moving. This reuses two things we already built (no new mechanism) and has a clear pass/fail test against the numbers we already measured.

summary: landmark_subgoal_hub_routing: 3-angle brain-first drill (hippocampal/BVC/VTE landmark navigation; graph-science ALT/hub-labeling/highway-hierarchies/betweenness-subgoal HRL; substrate design) converges on landmark/hub decomposition of long routes as the fix for the just-landed MIDDLE_BAND_CG_PARTIAL result (autonomous greedy-toward-final-goal reach@2=0.181, only 0.363x supplied-waypoint ceiling 0.499). 2/3 angles converge cleanly on the mechanism (graph-science load-bearing: ALT/hub-labeling/transit-node-routing exist specifically to fix this failure mode; brain: Balaguer et al. 2016 human hierarchical subway-hub planning); honest caveat: direct rodent single-unit test of hippocampal gateway/hub-tagging is DISCONFIRMED (Duvelle et al. 2021), and the mechanism is explicitly NOT free -- vacuous on expander-like graphs with no clean bottlenecks (graph-science angle), a risk not yet checked against the actual KB graph. Proposed substrate mechanism: precompute degree-proxy landmark set (one-time, reuses existing local-neighborhood-scoping primitive), route via a flat 2-leg landmark skeleton using the already-certified goal-conditioning MM re-targeted onto the landmark instead of the distant goal, zero new primitives. Discriminator: landmark-seeded reach@2 HARD-PASS>=0.40 vs HARD-FAIL<=0.20 (vs already-measured plain-greedy 0.181 / ceiling 0.499), gated by a cheap pre-check (KB graph degree distribution + nearest-landmark hop-distance) that must run before the build. P_deflated=0.35.
plain_language: We asked how the system could steer itself better through a chain of memories toward a distant goal, since aiming straight at the far-off target only partly worked. We looked at how GPS-style route planners solve this exact problem (precompute a few well-connected hub points once, then route hub-to-hub instead of all at once) and how human brains plan complicated routes (chunking a trip into hub-station legs, per a subway-navigation study), while being honest that one careful rat study did NOT find brain cells that specially mark hub locations. Both outside fields agree hub-routing is a real fix for exactly the weak-signal problem we just saw, and we designed a cheap way to build it using tools we already have -- plus a cheap check to run first, in case our own memory map turns out not to have clean hubs at all.

summary: successor_representation_reachability_autonomous_traversal: 3-angle lit-scan (hippocampal SR/predictive-map; ML successor-features/closed-form resolvent; graph-mining personalized-PageRank feasibility) converges 3/3, including a directly-published mathematical equivalence (SR = personalized PageRank, Millidge arXiv 2512.24722), that explains BOTH prior autonomous-traversal failures at once: greedy-cosine (reach@2=0.181) was single-step/static, landmark-routing (reach@2=0.111, worse than greedy) was goal-agnostic (degree-centrality). Proposed fix: closed-form resolvent M=(I-gamma*T)^-1 scored per-goal via single sparse linear solve (backward-push analog, cheap at n~4440, no full inverse needed), substituted into the same argmax loop, reusing local-neighborhood-scoping. Discriminator: reach@2 HARD-PASS>=0.40 vs HARD-FAIL<=0.20 (or <=0.111 floor-parity with landmark HARD_FAIL). P_deflated=0.42, capped at novel-synthesis 0.50. Honest risk: KB graph expander-vs-community structure diagnostic flagged 3x across 3 drills now, still never run.
plain_language: We asked why two attempts to make the substrate find its own way toward a goal both fell short, and found a math object from hippocampus research (the successor representation) that is literally the same thing search engines use to score how related two web pages are (personalized PageRank) -- a genuinely published paper proves this equivalence directly. This one idea explains both earlier failures at once: aiming straight at the goal failed because it only looks at how similar things seem right now, not where a path actually leads over many steps; routing through well-connected hubs failed because being generally important says nothing about being important specifically toward the current goal. The fix we found is cheap ordinary linear algebra (no new learned component, no new lookup mechanism) that is both multi-step-aware and goal-specific, which is the missing combination. It has a clear pass/fail test against numbers we already measured, and one honest, unresolved risk we have now flagged three times: whether our knowledge map has real neighborhoods and bottlenecks or is just a uniform tangle, which we still have not checked.

summary: learned_partial_graph_SR_reasoning_vs_search: 3-angle lit-scan (hippocampal TD-SR learning/Bono2023 eligibility mechanics; ML successor-features/learned-world-model generalization boundary + inductive-vs-transductive discriminator design; node2vec/DeepWalk proven resolvent-factorization + held-out-subgraph memorization-signature benchmark arXiv2510.23532) converges 3/3 on: (1) genuinely learned reachability = TD-sampled-transition SR (never known-T), matching what the just-certified cell explicitly bypassed; (2) raw sampled SR alone does NOT generalize to unvisited structure (Russek/Momennejad + Barretos own stated SF boundary) -- the corrective finding; (3) generalization to held-out structure requires smoothness in the substrates OWN LEARNED CODE SPACE (successor-features/Nystrom/node2vec-style), not the raw transition table. Proposed substrate realization: build T from a withheld/partial subgraph, score reachability to withheld nodes via code-space-similarity smoothing over already-scored neighbors, same argmax loop as certified cell. Decisive discriminator: held-out reach@2 HARD-PASS>=0.32 (80pct retention of certified 0.434) AND code-aliasing collapses held-out performance toward memoryless floor 0.121 (confirms codes do real work) vs HARD-FAIL held-out reach@2<=0.20 OR code-aliasing has zero effect on held-out condition (still leakage/search, not reasoning). P_deflated=0.30 (compounded risk: code-space-vs-hop-distance correlation never checked, held-out-split leakage risk from embedding co-training). Honest risk: even full success only fixes routing half, cannot lift 0.500 binding-fidelity retrieval ceiling.
plain_language: The just-certified route-finding result looked great (beats older attempts) but a careful check showed it was secretly reading a map we handed it, not actually reasoning -- disconnecting the substrates own understanding from the calculation changed nothing. We researched how real brains build this kind of skill purely from experience (never a handed map) and found the missing piece: the brain also cannot answer for places it never visited unless it generalizes through its own learned sense of similarity between places. We designed a concrete build -- hide part of the knowledge map, force the substrate to learn from what remains, and let its own learned similarity sense fill in the hidden part -- plus a clean pass/fail test that specifically checks whether disconnecting the substrates understanding NOW hurts performance on the hidden part (proving real learning) or not (proving it is still just clever map-reading). This is the actual fork between an impressive GPS and genuine reasoning, which is the deep prize this research line has been aiming at.

summary: inductive_inference_enablement_richness_vs_mechanism: 3-angle brain-first lit-scan (hippocampal transitive-inference/schema/analogy convergence; graph-ML richness-axis ranking; SCAN/COGS/CFQ/grokking mechanism-vs-knowledge fork) opened by tonight #4-VET resolution (substrate reasons over known knowledge MM reach@2~0.46, cannot infer beyond ingested graph, held-out margin~0.011, graph ~85% knowledge-thin, density-via-k-core refuted as branchiness-confounded). Convergent finding: brain mechanism is comparison/alignment (Gentner/DORA) producing a compositional low-conjunctivity additive-geometric code (Lippl et al 2024 PNAS direct-read formal proof) or schema-slot (Tse et al), NOT discrete chaining; richness axis ranked cross-domain relation-composition transfer (ULTRA arXiv:2310.04562, zero-shot across ~57 KGs) > relation-type/composition-pattern diversity (AMIE/RuleN/GraIL/NBFNet) > degree-matched density (configuration-model, clean design, no direct KG-completion precedent) > more entities (weakest); mechanism-vs-knowledge fork resolves to BOTH with a real interaction (CFQ: diversity alone collapses accuracy at fixed architecture+volume; grokking: critical-data floor that is itself mechanism-shiftable via distillation). Proposes ONE buildable next-experiment: relation-type-richness ladder on the existing #4 graph-inductive-ceiling harness, configuration-model degree-matched across rungs (explicit fix for the k-core branchiness confound), KNOWN-T oracle ceiling as mandatory degree-control-validity check. P_deflated=0.35 (capped novel-synthesis).
plain_language: We asked the brain-research and computer-science literature what actually lets a mind or a well-designed system guess a brand-new relationship it was never directly shown, since last night we found our substrate can follow a map it already has but cannot guess facts beyond it, and traced that to the knowledge itself being thin rather than the machinery. We found the brain does this by comparing several known relationships and boiling them down into a compact organized code, not by chaining facts step by step -- and computer-science research on knowledge graphs says the fix is not more raw facts or more distinct things, but more distinct KINDS of relationships, or even better, borrowing relationship-patterns from a richer related body of knowledge. We also found both knowledge and machinery matter together: a system needs a minimum amount of the right relational variety before any method can generalize at all, which matches exactly what we saw (a much fancier method failed the same way ours did). We proposed one concrete, cheap next experiment reusing existing tools that targets the specific richness axis the evidence favors, carefully designed not to repeat an earlier mistake.

summary: offline-consolidation/multi-view-agreement/degree-invariance prior-art scan: CLS-replay-for-generalization (Sun et al Nat Neurosci 2023, weak-item rebalancing), predictability-gated consolidation (Go-CLS, overfits-to-noise if unregulated), co-training independence (Blum-Mitchell breaks under real correlated views), KG degree-bias (Shomer WWW23) + benchmark-leakage precedent (Sun 2019 re-eval, 19-175pct inflation), DEAL dual-encoder structure+attribute alignment as closest architectural skeleton, SSL dimensional/informational collapse as the dominant failure mode for iterative self-refinement loops with no external labels. No prior work combines offline consolidation + cross-channel agreement + degree-invariance target -- genuine novel synthesis, P capped and deflated.
plain_language: Researched who else has tried our planned sleep-like consolidation architecture (rearranging concept representations offline so two independent views agree, to fix the popularity/degree bias). Found related pieces in neuroscience-inspired ML (replay for generalization, gated consolidation) and graph-embedding bias literature, but nobody has built our exact combination. The literature is full of warnings about ways this kind of thing fakes success (channels not really independent, benchmark leakage, representation collapse) -- those are now written up as a pre-registered pitfall list and a cheap decisive test with hard-fail thresholds before we build the real cell.

summary: spectral/diffusion concept geometry: normalized-Laplacian random-walk diffusion (x <- (1-a)x + a*P*x) is a proven, degree-invariant, no-eigendecomposition consolidation update rule; equivalent to Euler-discretized heat diffusion (incremental GFT solver); provably collapses to trivial mode without a restart/anchor term (Oono-Suzuki oversmoothing rate); Nystrom-style neighbor-averaging gives O(degree) incremental concept placement; composition-lands-meaningfully and hyperbolic-geometry-fit are NOT proven, flagged aspirational/gated.
plain_language: Researched whether there is a clean math shortcut for keeping the concept-vector map coherent as the knowledge base grows. Found one: a well-known graph-math technique (spectral/diffusion methods, the same kind of math used in image processing and even in theories of how the brain maps space) can arrange related concepts near each other and compress to a low-rank gist, and a simple degree-normalization trick (well-proven in the literature) fixes the exact popularity-bias problem we just fixed elsewhere. It also turns out the slow consolidation-loop idea IS mathematically this technique running incrementally, with one real risk (it can collapse everything to the same point if not capped) and a known fix. Composition (adding concepts to get a new meaningful concept) is NOT proven to come for free from this method - flagged as aspirational.

summary: multi-attribute grounding fusion (ATL hub-and-spoke): brain combines many weak independent channels via reliability-weighted MLE cue combination + inverse-effectiveness (weakest channels gain most from fusion) -- directly matches our marginal single-attribute regime. BUT candidate psycholinguistic attributes are not all independent (imageability/concreteness r=-0.80 in one proxy dataset) -- naive fusion of correlated attributes gains little; sensory-modality norms (Lynott/Connell) are the best-evidenced non-redundant addition. Recommend: alpha-sweep + coverage-density ablation on existing single-attribute cell FIRST (cheap disambiguators), THEN multi-attribute fusion via separate-per-attribute diffusion + reliability-weighted late combination, gated by an own-data pairwise-correlation pre-flight check and per-attribute scrambled-control fairness gates. P_deflated=0.40 (novel-synthesis cap 0.50, deflated for unverified English-specific correlation numbers and unproven sqrt(K) transfer to this exact setting).
plain_language: We asked: how does the brain make grounding robust instead of marginal? Answer: it never uses one signal -- it fuses many weak, independent senses (vision, sound, touch, emotion) into one hub, and the weaker each sense is alone, the bigger the payoff from combining them, which is exactly our situation. The catch: not all of our candidate human-rating attributes (concreteness, valence, age-of-acquisition, sensory-strength) are actually independent from each other -- some overlap heavily, so naive fusion would not help as much as hoped unless we check independence first and pick genuinely different attributes (sensory-strength norms look like the best bet). Recommendation: run two cheap sanity checks (tuning knob sweep, denser single-attribute coverage) before building the multi-attribute fusion, then build fusion with built-in fairness and independence checks.

plain_language: Shipped the Pillar-2 native-router test to FULL and it landed the same session: does a low-rank spectral (successor-representation) router keep routing as memory load grows, where the standard dense router collapses? The FULL load-sweep flipped the hopeful smoke lean: at real scale (P=20) the SR router does NOT rise with load -- it collapses to near-random (0.084 at the hardest load) and is actually WORSE than the dense router it was meant to beat (dense 0.289). The test itself was clean -- the dense router genuinely collapses, the oracle scores perfectly, and the SR router does NOT cheat by peeking at answer labels (unchanged under label-shuffle). So this is a real, valuable NEGATIVE: low-rank spectral routing bought nothing here -- the cross-literature inference that a low-rank router escapes the sqrt(D/M) capacity collapse is REJECTED at this scale. This vindicates holding smoke leans until the FULL decides. Handed to the cert-auditor for landed-VET before any claim is recorded.

summary: generate-and-test relational inference (Candidate B): hippocampal encoding/retrieval-based recombination + KG-completion rule-induction (AMIE/RNNLogic/Rel-SAR) literature independently converge on propose-composed-relation + discrete verify (support/confidence) as the mechanism class passive geometric read-off lacks. Causal-discovery active-intervention theory backs the necessity of an exogenous verifier. IterE/RulE precedent shows Candidate-A (denser knowledge) and Candidate-B (generate-and-test) are complementary (rules densify graph -> embeddings improve -> more material for rules), not competing.
plain_language: Researched how brains and AI systems invent new facts/relationships that were never directly stored. Both the hippocampus (via memory recombination) and modern knowledge-graph AI (via propose-a-rule-then-check-it systems) use the same two-step trick: guess a candidate new relationship by combining known ones, then check the guess against real data before trusting it. This is likely the missing piece for the substrate to infer new relationships instead of just recalling stored ones — and it needs a real, cheap self-check step, plus a reasonably rich knowledge base to guess from.

summary: Candidate A drill (knowledge-density vs inductive relational inference): brain lit (schema/chunking/structure-mapping/Halford/Cyc/Battaglia relational-inductive-bias/far-transfer) unanimous that knowledge volume never substitutes for a matched inference mechanism. Graph-theory ceiling (matrix completion coherence bound, SBM/Kesten-Stigum detectability, giant-component threshold) gives a real quantified density floor: substrate tested subgraphs avg degree ~2.7-7.7 (off-disk from existing metrics.json) sit in the WN18RR hard-benchmark regime (avg deg 4.24, 40943 ent / 86835 triples) not the FB15k-237 works regime (avg deg 37.4, 14541 ent / 272115 triples) -- roughly 5-10x density gap. This gives a mechanism-free statistical explanation for why relation-richness/k-core-density/structure-aware-encoder all went flat/negative: none crossed the density floor. Pre-registered HARD-PASS (real degree-uniform density to avg-deg 15-20, oracle-ceiling rises >=0.05, mechanism closes >=50% of that rise) vs HARD-FAIL (ceiling flat = density not the bottleneck; ceiling rises but mechanism/ceiling ratio flat = mechanism now the bottleneck, redirect to spectral/message-passing decoder not more ingest). Confounds to avoid vs the failed density cell: hold node-count + held-out query-set + degree-uniformity constant.
plain_language: We asked: could just adding a lot more real relational knowledge (not attribute-grounding, not subsetting) finally let the substrate infer brand-new relations, after every representation-quality lever this session failed? Brain science says knowledge alone never works without a matching reasoning mechanism -- but graph math gives a real, measurable reason the substrate has not actually tested this yet: its knowledge graph is about as sparse as the single hardest, most notoriously difficult benchmark in the field (WN18RR), not as dense as the benchmark where relation-prediction reliably works (FB15k-237) -- roughly a 5-10x density gap. So the past flat/negative results may simply reflect a graph too thin for ANY method to succeed, rather than proof the idea is impossible. We pre-registered exact pass/fail numbers and the confounds to avoid (based on what sank the earlier density experiment) so the next real test is decisive either way.

summary: Corpus survey (BUILD vs ADOPT vs COMPOSE for ingest): scored 15 public KG/corpus candidates against 6 must-have criteria (density vs ~37 avg-deg floor, relation diversity, low-leakage split, grounding/attributes, public availability, scale/quality). No single off-the-shelf corpus clears all 6 -- density-clearing candidates (FB15k-237, Hetionet, CoDEx) are symbol-only; grounding-rich candidates (Wikidata quantities, Visual Genome, WebChild) are sparse/fragmented/uncanonicalized. Verdict: COMPOSE -- k-core-densify CoDEx-M/L (Wikidata-sourced, engineered low-leakage split, saves the leakage-engineering + entity-resolution work) as the relational spine, graft Wikidata-quantity (numeric) + WebChild (perceptual, WordNet-sense-linked) attributes onto matched nodes for grounding. Honest gaps: k-core yield at scale is unverified, attribute coverage will be partial, and no corpus choice touches the separate mechanism/decoder gap (density necessary but not sufficient per prior finding). Pre-registered cheap decisive test: does CoDEx-M/L have a k-core at avg-deg>=37-40 retaining >=5000 entities (HARD-PASS) or does density collapse before the floor at useful scale (HARD-FAIL, strengthens build-own case for the spine specifically).
plain_language: We asked: before building our own knowledge corpus, is there an existing public one that is already close to ideal? We scored 15 well-known public knowledge-graph/corpus resources (FB15k-237, WN18RR, CoDEx, OGB biokg/wikikg2, Hetionet, Wikidata, YAGO, ATOMIC, Visual Genome, NELL, DBpedia, ASER, WebChild, ConceptNet-full) against our 6 real needs (dense enough to support inference, relation-diverse not just taxonomy, honest held-out test split, real measured attributes for grounding, freely downloadable, clean/large). None of them checks every box -- the dense, richly-related ones have no measured attributes, and the ones with real measured attributes are too sparse or too fragmented to use as a single connected graph. So the answer is neither pure build-from-scratch nor pure adopt-one-thing: take a well-engineered public Wikidata subset (CoDEx) that already solved the tricky honest-test-split problem, filter it down to its densest connected core, and graft on two other public resources for grounding (Wikidata numeric facts like population/elevation, and WebChild sensory-attribute data already linked to the same word-sense vocabulary we use). This saves real weeks of work others already did well, while leaving the genuinely new parts -- filtering for density and joining in the grounding -- as our own work, plus a clear next test to check whether this actually clears our density bar before we invest further.

summary: Deliberate ingest spec (spanning-basis reframe): grounded core = dictionary grounding-kernel/MGS (Vincent-Lamarre/Blondin-Masse/Harnad) UNION NSM 65 semantic primes+50 molecules (Wierzbicka/Goddard) UNION Lancaster sensorimotor 11-dim, cross-source-resolved via CSKG (2.2M nodes/6M edges, ConceptNet+ATOMIC+WordNet+Wikidata-CS+FrameNet+Roget+VisualGenome already merged). Density is now a SECONDARY constraint on a spanning core, not the primary selection criterion -- dense named-entity corpora (FB15k-237 avg-deg 37.4, Hetionet avg-deg 47.9) are confirmed anti-patterns: dense enough for KG-inference but cannot ground sadness/multiplication/rough-texture/because. Pre-registered grounding-reach acceptance test (diverse 6-domain probe set, 70% HARD-PASS bar reusing this session own multi-attribute fusion discriminator) to make span-completeness falsifiable rather than assumed, plus a local-density cheap decisive test on the core subgraph itself.
plain_language: We designed the actual recipe for what to feed the substrate first so new knowledge can genuinely connect to real-world meaning, not just to other symbols. The key correction (from the Director mid-task): the first batch should not be picked because it is the densest available knowledge graph -- it should be picked because it covers all the basic BUILDING BLOCKS of meaning (physical senses, emotions, quantities, logic/causation, social concepts), the way children learn a small set of concrete, universal words first and then everything else hooks onto that foundation. We found a very well-matched published recipe for this small foundational set (linguists have already identified both a minimal dictionary-definition core and a list of 65 universal meaning-primitives found in every language), a way to attach real sensory/emotional grounding data to those words, and an existing free resource that already links different knowledge sources together so we do not have to solve that stitching problem ourselves. We also flagged the trap: some of the best knowledge graphs are extremely dense but only about narrow topics like movies or diseases -- using one of those as the starter set would look impressive but would leave whole categories of meaning (like emotions or math) permanently ungrounded. The next concrete step is a cheap check: is this foundational word-set actually well-connected in the data we have, and does it genuinely cover diverse test concepts we did not train on.

summary: CSKG prior-art/novelty due-diligence: CSKG (USC-ISI, ESWC21) confirmed passive symbolic-only resource not a reasoner; no measured-grounding CSKG variant exists (MMCOMET grounds ATOMIC2020 via CLIP images, not norms); exact self-contained+glass-box+VSA+CSKG+spanning-core-grounding+open-relation-generate-and-test combination not found built anywhere, but PRISM (unpublished VSA cog-arch, ~3/5 pieces) and Rel-SAR (published VSA propose+verify, closed-vocab) show convergent partial invention already underway; Soar/OpenCog/NARS confirmed NOT already doing this. P_deflated=0.35.
plain_language: Before building on CSKG we checked whether anyone already built what we are planning. CSKG is just a big pre-merged commonsense knowledge graph (built by USC researchers to be reused, not a thinking system) -- safe and correct to build on. Nobody has combined all our pieces (self-contained no-LLM reasoning + transparent math + grounded-in-real-sensory-data + generate-and-test-with-a-checker) into one system yet, but we found a hobbyist project (PRISM) that already built about 60% of our architecture as a side project, and a published paper (Rel-SAR) that already proved our core reasoning trick works (just on a narrower puzzle-type problem). So the idea is real and the gap is real, but it is not an empty field -- other people are actively poking at the same space, which means we should move with real urgency rather than assuming we have unlimited runway.

plain_language: We asked: will the new resonator-network fix (an iterative search technique) actually recover the missing search results the crux test lost, or will it hit its own wall first? Answer: plausibly yes for most of the gap, but only if it reuses two tricks this substrate already proved work (trying several random restarts, and an existing capacity-boosting rescue) rather than a bare-bones version. We flagged three specific things that could cap the recovery below what is needed, and gave a cheap, pre-registered test to tell which outcome we are in before committing more build time.

summary: math/social/abstract grounding core-expansion: sensorimotor-only core cannot ground MATH (-0.43 cosine) because brain grounds number via a distinct magnitude primitive (ANS/mental-number-line) + structural metaphor-mapping (Lakoff/Nunez 4 grounding metaphors), not perceptual content; SOCIAL (+0.015) needs a 2D power-x-affiliation relational channel (hippocampal social-space / Interpersonal Circumplex), not more affect. Recommend: add MAGNITUDE/ORDINALITY + SOCIAL-RELATIONAL attribute channels (same hub-and-spoke architecture as existing Lancaster/VAD channels) first; reserve a METAPHOR-structural graph-edge bridge for the residual (higher math, justice/causation-type abstractions) that literature (Pecher & Zeelenberg) predicts may resist scalar-channel grounding entirely.
plain_language: We found out WHY our grounded-core (which ties abstract words to physical/sensory experience) could ground emotional and physical concepts but not math or social concepts: math and social relationships are not perceived through the five senses at all -- the brain grounds numbers through a separate built-in magnitude sense and grounds social relationships through a two-dimensional power-and-warmth map, both totally different from sight/sound/touch. The fix is to add two new measured channels (a magnitude/quantity channel and a social power-and-affiliation channel) using the same method already working for physical/emotional concepts, plus a structural bridge for the hardest abstract cases. This turns a mysterious failure into a concrete, buildable next step.

plain_language: Studied whether the substrate should sometimes hold onto a fuzzy, unresolved set of possibilities longer before picking one clean answer (rather than deciding early at every step). Found real, well-established math (from statistics, communications engineering, and this substrate own past experiments) saying: yes, deciding too early throws away information you might need later -- but only when that information is still there to use. When noise has already scrambled the signal before the decision point, waiting longer does not help. Proposed a cheap, concrete test to check this on the multi-hop reasoning work already in progress.

The plumbing works and passes every fairness check (a scrambled magnitude channel correctly kills any fake gain). summary: crux_v3_sharded_recovery_capacity: CONDITIONAL on in-flight decode-budget sweep (t_iter 20->100) confirming crux-v2 wall is genuinely encode-side not under-iteration. Corrects initial pointer (plate-bound/FHRR-chain memory = partial-fit, corruption-robustness not bundling capacity) to tighter on-substrate precedent: PP-127 sharding scaling law (mono-collapse 0.060 near-matches crux failing 0.058) + Op B/Op E negatives bounding how v3 aggregation must be built (discrete list-merge only, never joint vector op -- both on-substrate negatives show joint cross-shard operations fail). Verified capacity formula (Frady/Kleyko/Sommer 2018, fetched) gives K_max~38-152 at N=2048-8192 vs V=14541, tighter than back-of-envelope, same conclusion: heavy-tailed real K explains why N-scaling alone stalled. Relocation risk is concrete (not hypothetical): degree-stratified crux-v2 data already shows gap concentrated in mid/high-degree tertiles, exactly where per-rule-path sharding is weakest. Brain: theta-gamma sequential slotting is maximal-sharding, prescribes degree-adaptive granularity not flat shards. Corrected prior Hersche/BCF citation (re-fetched: no bundling-capacity claims, factorizer-only). Pre-registered 2-stage test with degree-stratified must-fail control bolts onto existing crux-v2 scaffolding.
plain_language: The reasoning-engine test failed because too many candidate answers get mashed together into one signal before the system tries to read them out. exp_dev proposed splitting that signal into smaller per-path groups (sharding) before reading, citing our own past finding that sharding beats one-big-bundle. We confirmed that finding is real and even found a closer match (a past experiment where one big bundle collapsed to almost the same failure number as this new test), but we also found the fix is not automatic: for topics with a lot of connections (hub relations), a single per-path group can itself still be too big, so sharding could fix the easy majority of cases while leaving the hardest ones exactly as broken -- and our own data already shows the failures cluster on exactly those hard, well-connected cases. We designed a test that checks specifically for that blind spot, not just the overall average. We also caught and corrected an over-claimed citation in the prior report, and confirmed via fresh internet research that the brain's own trick for this exact problem (processing memories one at a time in rapid brain-wave cycles instead of all at once) matches the deeper fix. This work is explicitly conditional on a cheaper check running right now to first rule out that the test result was just under-tuned rather than a true wall.
