summary: grounded_ingest_at_scale: dev-psych lit gives order+bootstrap mechanism for grounding (concrete/basic-level first, abstract bootstraps via metaphor/simulation) but no sufficiency-scale number; bulk no-LLM measured sources exist at real scale (Materials Project/AFLOW/OQMD/PubChem/Wikidata/USDA) with proven exact-ID join paths (QID/CAS/InChIKey) and literal-fusion KG-embedding precedent (LiteralE ~31% relative MRR gain fusing numeric literals) plus direct cold-start-rescue precedent (ConMask/DKRL beat structure-only baselines in open-world regime); KG-percolation/k-core threshold framing for grounded ingest is NOT attested anywhere in literature -- flagged as novel unattested analogy, P capped. First buildable step: exact-ID join hit-rate + k-core movement test on 500 sparse-tail entities vs Wikidata quantity-claims dump, hours of scripting, HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL pre-registered.
plain_language: We researched how to give the reasoning system real, measured facts about the world (not just word-relations) to fix entities that currently have zero or one connection in its knowledge graph. Good news: there are large free public databases of real measured facts (materials science, chemistry, nutrition, general knowledge) we can join in without needing any external AI language model, and similar techniques have measurably helped other systems in comparable situations. The open question -- whether our specific sparse entities actually overlap with what these databases cover -- is still unmeasured, so we defined a cheap first test (a few hours of data-matching, no training) to find out before building the full pipeline.

summary: SR-compose gap-to-additive: SR-compose (0.073) beats its own SR-oracle (0.051) because SR is a local Bellman fixed-point (compose IS the defining recursion), unlike LAP/PPMI which are global objects -- explains the 7x SR-vs-LAP compose gap mechanistically. Ranked levers to close the 1.75x gap to additive (0.128): (1) score-level fusion of SR-compose + additive-compose (both already VET-confirmed FULL, near-zero build cost, literature-convergent GraIL/InGram precedent) -- top rank; (2) multi-gamma SR codebook (Momennejad multi-scale-SR, honest GDC counter-signal); (3) bootstrap neighbor-subset ensembling; (4) Hopfield/kNN cleanup (CS theory predicts small recovery given measured spectral spread). exp_dev handoff filed with both anchors pre-registered.
plain_language: We found out WHY a brain-inspired code (successor representation) transfers to new concepts 7x better than a rival code style, and why it still falls short of our best trained method by about 45%. The explanation is clean: this brain code is defined as "combine your neighbors" so guessing from neighbors basically IS the exact answer, recomputed -- the rival codes only make sense relative to the whole map, not a neighborhood, so they do not transfer as well. The single best next step, costing almost nothing, is to just combine our two working methods scores (not their internal math) the way search engines combine two rankers -- outside research says this kind of teamwork often beats either method alone, especially on the hardest cases.

summary: llm_reasoning_interp_glass_box_lens: mech-interp lit-scan (induction heads/Othello-GPT/grokking vs frequency-effects/CoT-unfaithfulness debate) maps DAS/Interchange-Intervention-Accuracy + RAVEL specificity as a directly-portable causal gate for VSA role/filler binding (IIA available for free -- coordinates known by construction, no subspace search needed unlike transformers). Superposition-necessity lit shows storage capacity is generous for any high-dim code (JL) but active COMPUTATION on superposed features has a tighter bound independent of opacity (arXiv:2409.15318) -- glass-box sidesteps the SAE retrofit-decoder problem (splitting/absorption/incompleteness) but inherits the open storage-vs-computation efficiency question, which our additive-vs-multiplicative-bind and SR-vs-additive-compose cells are already the live experiment for. Cheap decisive test proposed: IIA+specificity diagnostic on already-shipped additive_map.py/SR-compose, stratified by degree bucket.
plain_language: We researched how outside AI scientists try to prove a language model is genuinely reasoning rather than just reciting memorized patterns, since our own project faces the identical question. The clearest, ready-to-use import: a causal test where you swap one specific piece of a paired comparison and check whether only the intended output changes -- for us this is nearly free because our building-block vectors are labeled by design, unlike a trained black-box model where researchers must first hunt for the right internal location. We also found the field is honestly split: some brain-like circuits are proven genuine, but a lot of apparent reasoning is proven fake (the stated explanation is not what actually drove the answer). One deeper worry does carry over to us and is NOT resolved by being transparent: outside theory suggests that actively computing with compressed, overlapping codes may be fundamentally harder than just storing them, regardless of whether the code is see-through or not -- meaning our transparency is a real advantage for TRUST but not a free pass on CAPACITY, and our current live map-building experiments are exactly the test of that open question.

summary: cold_start_intrinsic_content_vs_relational_inference: 3-way lit-scan (fast-mapping/hippocampal-indexing, schema-consolidation, feature-to-relation/zero-shot-KGC) explains WHY AdditiveKGMap/SR-compose/grounding-bound-onto-neighbors structurally cannot help cold (0-support) entities -- brain uses a categorically different content-only hippocampal-index mechanism for isolated concepts, not composition. One-anchor is a QUALITATIVE (not incremental) threshold per Shohamy-Wagner single-shared-edge transitive-inference result. Honest Q4 verdict: zero-anchor+content is NEVER sufficient for relational inference alone in either brain or ML lit (essentialism/label-dominance, DKRL/BLP) -- content-similarity always functions as an implicit pseudo-anchor-manufacturing step. On-disk stratification (59pct degree-1, majority name-transparent single-synonym/hypernym children) means cold IS winnable for that name-transparent taxonomic majority via borrowed-parent content-placement, but name-opaque cold entities are a genuine literature-confirmed floor (retrieval-only, not relational-inference-capable). Cheap decisive test pre-registered (borrowed-parent placement + scrambled-name must-fail control) reusing on-disk Test3 BFS harness, zero new data/training.
plain_language: We asked: how does a brain represent a brand-new idea it has never connected to anything else (zero context), versus one it has heard mentioned once? Answer: with zero context, the brain only keeps the raw sensory/definitional impression -- it cannot yet reason about how the idea relates to other things, because that requires at least one connection. One connection turns out to be a hard on/off switch, not a small boost: it is enough for the brain to start inferring new relationships. For our system, this explains exactly why its coldest, most isolated entries score at zero: the machinery it uses composes new knowledge FROM existing connections, and a zero-connection entry has none to compose from -- same wall the brain would hit too. The fix is not to tune that machinery harder; it is to add a second, content-based placement path (borrow a similar, well-known concepts profile from the new entrys own name/definition) for the subset where that is possible, while accepting that a smaller, name-opaque subset genuinely cannot be placed this way.

summary: consolidation_confidence_permanence: schema-consistent info consolidates fast via mPFC-hippocampus congruency circuit (Tse/Morris one-trial schema learning, van Kesteren SLIMM); transitive-inference-after-sleep is real but modest and gated by encoding strength (Ellenbogen, replicated); Wagner insight result contested/not cleanly replicated even by original co-author; sleep necessity itself contested (properly-powered interference-protection replications mostly null, awake quiet-rest replay works too) -- what transfers is a dedicated OFFLINE phase, not sleep physiology; false-memory/schema-distortion (Payne, Alba and Hasher) shows the same mechanism that produces true relational generalization also produces false-positive confabulation, pre-register as expected cost; biology supports graded confidence/permanence (systems consolidation gradient, reconsolidation Nader/LeDoux = confidence can drop and revise on contradiction, precision-weighting/Kalman-gain, synaptic tagging, metaplasticity) but these are 3-4 distinct mechanisms not one scalar; designed minimal glass-box experiment: per-relation confidence scalar (separate from bundle magnitude per store-vs-retrieval decoupling law) + precision-weighted consolidation update on content-placed cold entities, with random-replay and confidence-blind must-fail controls plus a non-negotiable revisability check (high-confidence relations must NOT be permanently locked).
plain_language: Studied whether the brains sleep/memory-consolidation system is a real precedent for letting the substrate check and update its guessed relations for a new entity. Found: yes for evaluating and fast-tracking correct guesses (well-supported), modest support for actually generating new inferences beyond what was trained (real but small effect, and the sleep-specific framing is itself scientifically contested), and an important honest cost -- the same mechanism that generalizes correctly also fabricates false schema-consistent guesses, so we should expect and measure that rather than assume it away. Biology also supports giving each relation a graded confidence/permanence level that can rise with confirming evidence or fall and get revised on contradiction, which is a genuinely new design element (not yet in the store). Designed a cheap experiment to test this directly, with strict must-fail controls.

summary: brain_grounding_flexibility_open_spoke_registry: hub-and-spoke + CDZ bind is a well-evidenced multi-scale universal operator; open-endedness = admission-test (contingency+active-loop) not channel taxonomy (converges across sensory-substitution/tool-embodiment/expertise); reliability-weighted routing+conflict-gate at semantic level is THIN extrapolation from low-level Ernst-Banks/Kording, flagged separately falsifiable; missing-channel grounding (our case) transfers relational/causal content well (rho~0.99) but not arbitrary-associative content (50%% vs 95%%) -- predicts differential text-spoke transfer by content type, not uniform pass/fail. P_deflated=0.42 (sub-claims 0.55 bind/registry, 0.25 routing-arithmetic).
plain_language: Studied how the brain keeps its grounding system flexible instead of a rigid fixed pipeline: it uses one universal binding operation everywhere, and admits any new sensory/data channel automatically as long as that channel reliably correlates with something already grounded and is exercised through active feedback -- no rewiring needed. It also confirms that when a channel is missing (our situation, zero sensory data), text/definitions can genuinely ground relational and causal facts well, but cannot ground arbitrary factual details (like exact colors) -- so our design should expect and flag that split rather than assume text grounds everything equally.

summary: ideal_foundation_spec: CORE (dense shared relational graph: Wikidata-full+ConceptNet+ATOMIC+WordNet+Wiktionary+YAGO4-constraint-check+BabelNet-labels) + open MODULE REGISTRY (PubChem/periodic-table/FoodData/GeoNames/UMLS, admitted via anchoring-test+non-redundant-content+declared-provenance, mirroring same-day brain-side spoke-registry finding) architecture, replacing raw-node-count target with per-concept relation-TYPE-bucket coverage (>=4-5 of ~7 applicable buckets: taxonomic/property/part-whole/functional/causal/spatial/social) as the real density metric -- our 59pct-degree-1 tail is pathological because it is characterized along at most 1 bucket, not because count is low; redundancy (many edges, one bucket) is a SEPARATE over-density failure mode. Cross-module interconnection happens ONLY through shared core entities (diamond node carries materials+chemistry+use attachments independently), never module-to-module; collision reconciliation uses declared MEASURED/RATED/DERIVED provenance + YAGO4-style constraints. Concrete literature backing: KG-RAG over-inclusion actively hurts (arXiv:2602.04926), common-neighbor density not raw degree drives accuracy (arXiv:2503.12139), YAGO4/CSKG/BabelNet each pay real quantified vetting costs (28pct fact-loss, 51pct entity-link precision, sub-0.5 recall) -- fully vetted is an explicit tradeoff, not an absolute. First buildable step: two-part audit (k-core proxy + per-concept bucket-coverage measurement) on our own active partition, zero new data.
plain_language: We designed a concrete blueprint for the ideal knowledge foundation, built the same way the brain grounds new senses: one shared universal core graph (identity, categories, general relations, multilingual labels) that every concept gets, plus swappable domain add-on modules (chemistry, materials, geography, medicine) that attach to core entries without ever needing the core rebuilt. The key fix from our first draft: bigger is not better by node count -- the real target is whether each concept has a handful of DIFFERENT kinds of connections (what it is, what it does, what it is part of, what it causes), not just a raw connection count. That explains exactly why 59 percent of our current entries are barely usable: they typically have only ONE kind of connection (usually just a category label), not zero connections. We also specified how two add-on modules that both describe the same thing (say, both giving a hardness value for diamond) get reconciled without a mess, and how new languages and even untranslatable culture-specific concepts fit in without restructuring anything. The first concrete next step costs nothing new to run: measure our own existing knowledge base against this per-concept connection-type checklist.

summary: dense_kg_prior_art_and_source_depth: 3-way lit-scan confirms dense per-concept multi-relation-type-bucket general KG is genuinely unbuilt (ConceptNet 5.7 broadest relation vocabulary but per-concept thin/skewed; CSKG inherits same skew >50pct top-3-relation mass; BabelNet 99.98pct untyped; Dense-ATOMIC/COMET prove multi-bucket generation possible but only within social/event domain, and exists precisely because full ATOMIC2020 stayed sparse per-node -- direct evidence against re-ingest-alone). Re-ingest/enrich/acquire split estimated ~40-50/15-20/20-25/10-15 (re-ingest largest lever, not dominant/sufficient alone), mostly-estimated not measured. Sharpest finding: the same-day sibling >=4-5-of-7-bucket density-optimum target is UNVALIDATED, and the one directly relevant paper (arXiv:2508.15291, Node-level Maximum Relation Diversity) found relation-type diversity INVERSELY correlated with link-prediction MRR in fused dense-embedding models (FB15k-237/WN18RR/CoDEx) -- opposite sign from what the target assumes. Whether this fragmentation mechanism transfers to our structurally-separated bind/unbind VSA readout (vs fused TransE/ComplEx-style embeddings) is the new falsifiable gate, operationalized as Part C (degree-controlled bucket-diversity-vs-retrieval-quality stratification) added to the sibling note Section 7 test.
plain_language: We checked whether some existing knowledge database already gives every concept a rich, many-sided description (what it is, what it does, what causes it, etc.) so we would not have to build one -- answer: no, nobody has built that yet, even the best public knowledge bases are lopsided (mostly one type of fact repeated many times, not a genuine mix). We also found the single most useful next building-block to pull in (a fuller download of an already-existing free resource) and estimated how much of our gap that alone would close versus needing smarter automated fact-generation versus needing brand-new data sources -- roughly a third to a half from the free download alone, the rest needs other methods. Most important finding: outside research on other AI systems found that having MANY different kinds of facts about one thing can actually make some AI models more confused, not smarter -- which complicates our working assumption that more variety is always better, and we now have a specific, cheap test designed to check whether that problem applies to our own system or not before we invest further.

summary: grid-code algebraic binding: grid/entorhinal codes are NOT one universal algebra reused verbatim -- brain factorizes structure from content (TEM) and derives a per-relation spectral/successor-representation basis via predictive TD learning; this reframes the 0.11(SGD)->1.0(hand-designed FHRR) conjunction gap as a missing CODE-CONSTRUCTION stage (Laplacian-eigenvector/successor-representation codes), not a missing bind operator. Ranked 5 candidates; top = spectral/SR code feeding unchanged FHRR bind, P_deflated=0.40 on cheap decisive test (novel-pair accuracy on held-out (A,B), HARD-PASS>=0.70, HARD-FAIL<=0.20).
plain_language: We asked how the brain builds relational codes that generalize (grid cells for space) versus our own learned codes which only memorize. Finding: the brain does not reuse one fixed spatial code everywhere -- it relearns a new but similarly-structured code for each type of relationship, using a predictive learning signal (successor representation) that mathematically forces a compositional/additive structure. This gives us a concrete, cheap-to-test next step: build entity codes from a predictive/spectral objective over the relations own structure (instead of plain gradient descent on the task), then plug those into our already-working binding operator, and see if novel combinations jump from 11% correct toward the 100% we get with hand-designed codes.

summary: realworld_conjunctive_determination_prevalence: 3-way lit-scan converges -- genuine no-dominant-driver conjunctions are the MINORITY regime generally (ANOVA meta-science: interactions ~1 order of magnitude smaller than main effects, McClelland-Judd 1993 + Gelman 16x-sample-size; additive genetic variance dominates typical quantitative traits, Hill-Goddard-Visscher 2008; GA1M additive models already capture most black-box ML accuracy on tabular data) but clusters predictably in discrete/threshold/molecular pockets: synthetic lethality (purest AND-gate), chemistry/QSAR potency-binding nonadditivity (majority regime, 30-58 pct of assays per AstraZeneca/public data), drug-drug synergy (Loewe additivity is the violated null not the default). Ecology/organismal/economic domains rank near bottom (conjunctive in theory via Hutchinson niche hypervolume, single-driver-dominant in practice via Liebig law of the minimum) -- exactly the domain class our metabolic-rate finding came from, so that result is predictable not unlucky. Brain rationale for conjunctive coding splits into TWO separable reasons: (1) non-monotonic/context-flipping contingencies (negative patterning, biconditional discrimination -- provably unsolvable by additive learners) which requires the world to actually be interactive, and (2) hippocampal pattern-separation/episodic-individuation (avoiding interference when facts share overlapping features) which does NOT require attribute-level interactivity -- this decouples the conjunctive-coding architecture bet from the attribute-selection bet. Hedge: pre-filter candidate held-out attributes via single-factor-MI-vs-joint-MI triage; target molecular/chemistry/threshold-logic relation pockets for conjunction-rich foundation content; keep conjunctive/orthogonal storage architecture regardless (interference-avoidance justification independent of this verdict). P_deflated=0.50 (capped per calibration discipline).
plain_language: We asked: is the world actually full of situations where an outcome needs a COMBINATION of factors (no single one dominates), or does one factor usually win by itself -- because our last test (animal metabolic rate) turned out to be dominated by one factor (activity level), which raises a worry that our whole conjunctive-reasoning bet might be chasing something rare. The answer from biology, statistics, genetics, and machine-learning literature all agrees: single-factor-dominance IS the common case in general, but genuine combinations that need both factors together cluster in specific places -- gene pairs where knocking out either alone is fine but both together is lethal, chemistry where combining two structural changes to a drug produces an effect neither change produces alone, and drug-drug interactions where two medicines together do something different from either alone. Ecology and everyday physical traits (like metabolic rate) are exactly the kind of domain where one factor usually wins, so our finding was predictable, not bad luck. Practical takeaway: aim our conjunction-hunting at genetics/chemistry/threshold-type relationships, not general animal or physical traits, and keep our combination-detecting memory design anyway since brains use it for a second reason (avoiding mixing up similar memories) that has nothing to do with whether any one fact is a true combination.

summary: ordinal_magnitude_coding_bestinclass: brain runs monotone(parietal)+tuned(prefrontal) magnitude codes plus log/Weber compression before readout; current thermometer code has monotone-vs-cyclic right but is missing compression (linear-uniform bins). Ranked upgrades: 1) log-compressed thermometer bins (P=0.35), 2) reliability-weighted additive combination (P=0.30), 3) dual monotone+tuned hybrid (0.20), 4) grid-like joint magnitude code per Park/Miller/Boorman 2021 (0.15, high-risk/high-reward, separate branch), 5) nonlinear monotone lattice combiner (0.15, ML lit predicts null per Xu et al 2021/NALU). HARD-PASS/FAIL pre-registered for top 2.
plain_language: We researched how the brain encodes and combines magnitude (like quantity or size) for judgments, to find the best upgrade to our crude ordinal-magnitude code. The brain compresses magnitude logarithmically before it reads it out -- our code currently does not do this. The single cheapest fix is to space our encoding bins logarithmically instead of evenly; a same-day test with clear pass/fail thresholds is specified.

summary: brain_nonadditive_interaction_relational_coding: brain uses TWO separable mechanisms for the substrate architectural wall (commutative bind + symmetric readout provably cannot represent AND/XOR/asymmetric structure) -- conjunctive units (hippocampal DG/CA3, PFC nonlinear mixed selectivity, Rigotti/Fusi 2013 Nature) expand dimensionality so a LINEAR readout can solve XOR-class problems, while parietal gain fields (Zipser/Andersen 1988) and PFC rank-x-identity conjunctive cells (Dehaene et al 2015) show genuinely multiplicative/asymmetric binding that is plastic/learned not fixed. Negative-patterning/biconditional discrimination (Pearce configural theory vs Rescorla-Wagner elemental) is the animal-learning XOR-equivalent proof animals solve non-linearly-separable tasks; hippocampal necessity for this specific finding is CONTESTED (Rudy and Sutherland 1995 walked back their own 1989 claim). Direct new evidence (Dang et al 2021 J Neurosci) shows PFC mixed selectivity partly EMERGES WITH TRAINING (task-selective), refining the textbook fixed-random-expansion-plus-learned-readout account. Ranked 6-item shortlist for the substrate: TOP = learned low-rank bilinear/gated multiplicative bind (Kim et al 2016 Hadamard-product-as-low-rank-bilinear-pooling; a minimal-diff upgrade from current elementwise bind, LEARNABLE not just CONSTRUCT), second cheapest = fixed random permutation to break symmetry (standard VSA Gayler MAP Permute primitive, CONSTRUCT, near-zero cost but narrower scope, order-only not full interaction). Pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds for top mechanisms. Connects to June 2026 GHRR non-commutative pilot (already-validated existing order-sensitive operator) -- recommendation reuses/extends that operator class rather than proposing new architecture.
plain_language: We asked the brain how it represents two things our reasoning system currently cannot: combinations that need BOTH ingredients together (like AND or XOR, not just addition) and relationships where order matters (A relates to B is different from B relates to A). The brain turns out to use two matching tricks: special neurons that respond only to specific COMBINATIONS of inputs (found in memory-forming brain regions and the frontal cortex), which effectively expand the problem into a bigger space where simple downstream readout can succeed; and multiplicative (not additive) combination rules, cleanest seen in neurons that combine eye position and gaze direction, which are naturally order-sensitive and are shaped by experience rather than fixed at birth. Animal-learning experiments (rats and pigeons solving a classic combination-only puzzle) prove animals can learn exactly this kind of combination structure, though which brain region is strictly required for it turned out to be more debated than the original theory claimed -- an honest scientific walk-back we found and flagged. Practical result: we now have a ranked list of concrete upgrades to try on our own reasoning system, with the top pick being a small, well-precedented tweak (a multiplicative combination rule with trainable parts, directly inspired by both the brain evidence and existing machine-learning techniques) rather than a brand-new architecture, plus exact pass/fail numbers to test it against.

summary: brain_unifies_symmetric_asymmetric_binding: resolved the coexistence/unification question left open by the prior separate-mechanisms drill. Verdict = JOINT CODE + SELECTIVE LINEAR READOUT (Bernardi/Benna/Rigotti/Fusi/Salzman 2020 Cell: same HPC+PFC population carries both abstract-invariant and nonlinear-conjunctive signal, separable only by which linear projection is applied), NOT physically separate subsystems composing only downstream (that separation is real only at the DG/CA3-vs-MEC content/structure-construction stage, upstream of the bind, per lesion-dissociation evidence). Where asymmetry physically lives is contested across 3 non-reconciled accounts (TEM non-commutative transition matrices; CA3-symmetric/CA1-asymmetric plasticity-rule split; Lippl et al 2024 PNAS additive-representational-geometry+linear-readout account) -- genuinely open, not settled. Top ranked substrate design: shared combined vector z=(r1(x)a+r2(x)b)+lambda*(a(x)b) (role-keyed TPR-style asymmetric term bundled additively with existing symmetric elementwise-product term, both CONSTRUCT/near-zero-cost reuse of existing bind+bundle primitives) with two LEARNABLE linear readout heads (unbind-by-role for order channel, role-agnostic projection for configural channel) -- directly mirrors the Bernardi 2020 same-population-different-lens finding. Second-ranked: tied-vs-untied bilinear pooling heads (P=Q gives symmetric channel, P!=Q gives asymmetric channel) extending the prior drills learned-bilinear-bind recommendation. Pre-registered HARD-PASS/FAIL on cross-channel interference (<=10pct degradation = ship; >25pct = fall back to fully separate parallel vectors, the DG/CA3-vs-MEC-style fallback).
plain_language: Follow-up to todays earlier finding that the brain uses two SEPARATE tricks for combination-logic (AND/XOR type) versus order-sensitive (A-relates-to-B versus B-relates-to-A) relationships. This drill asked the harder question: how does the SAME brain system hold both at once and use them together? Answer: it is not one all-purpose neuron doing everything, and it is not two totally separate systems that only meet at the very end either -- it is a middle path. The brain first builds a content piece and a structure piece separately, then glues them into ONE combined memory trace, and different downstream reading strategies pull out either the order information or the combination information from that SAME trace, proven directly in a well-known hippocampus/frontal-cortex study. This gives us a concrete, buildable design for our own system: combine our existing building blocks (which we already have) in a specific recipe -- keyed-by-role combination plus plain combination, glued together -- and add two small trained reading heads, one for each type of question, with exact numeric pass/fail criteria to test whether this works without the two reading strategies interfering with each other.

detail: LOCAL restart recovery; remote runner ALIVE (running consol_inductive). SCP-recovered 5 FULL metrics (SH-9 gap on joint/random_expansion/interference). joint MIDDLE, 3x HARD_PASS, random PARTIAL. ordinal FAILED metrics_invalid. Shipped consol_inductive to remote_cpu_queue.

summary: real_nonadditive_experimental_datasets_for_conjunction_module: 3-domain lit-scan finds public downloadable datasets carrying MEASURED (not narrated) interaction terms in all 3 target domains -- chemistry MMP nonadditivity (Kramer 2021 J Cheminformatics, Nonadd_pC column, ~4500 rows, 3 CSVs, verified-live unauthenticated download), genetic epistasis (Costanzo 2016 yeast SGA, epsilon score, ~23M measurements, bulk TSV, thecellmap.org), drug synergy (NCI-ALMANAC ComboScore ~290K rows direct ZIP; DrugComb Bliss/Loewe/ZIP/HSA via TDC). #1 recommendation for first ingest: Kramer 2021 chemistry nonadditivity CSVs -- smallest (4500 rows), cleanest (single scalar Nonadd_pC per compound from closed 4-point cycle, pure arithmetic not narrative), verified reachable, fact-crisp (no synergy-model-choice ambiguity). Pre-registered HARD-PASS (>=30pct relative MAE reduction vs additive baseline on noise-floor-cleared nonadditive subset) / HARD-FAIL (module improvement collapses to noise-floor range, or <15pct of rows clear the 0.3-log-unit assay noise floor) thresholds. Directly closes the gap from 2026-07-14 realworld-conjunctive-prevalence drill: that drill correctly predicted WHERE genuine conjunctions concentrate (chemistry QSAR nonadditivity, synthetic lethality) but the 2 live attempts used LLM-narrated proxies instead of the measured data -- this drill sources the real measured datasets directly.
plain_language: We went looking for real, publicly downloadable scientific datasets where a combination-effect (not a single ingredient acting alone) is actually MEASURED in a lab, not just described in words -- because our last two attempts used AI-narrated descriptions of chemistry and genetics scenarios that turned out to be fakeable by a simple single-ingredient model. We found solid real options in all three areas we checked (chemistry drug-design data, gene-pair genetics data, drug-combination cancer-treatment data), each with an actual computed number for how much two things interact beyond just adding up. Our top pick for the first real test is a small, clean chemistry dataset (about 4500 rows) where a computed nonadditivity number is already in the file, ready to download right now, with a clear pass/fail bar set in advance.

summary: Cross-module entity-interface drill: brain-aligned + best-in-class answer is a thin canonical-ID hub registry (ATL hub-and-spoke / NCATS Babel-NodeNorm pattern) with each conjunction module (epistasis/synergy/nonadditivity) keeping its own bind/relation machinery; cross-module reasoning = identity-anchored bind/unbind traversal, not merged embeddings. summary: grounding_scoping_subsumed_or_separate: verdict = CONDITIONALLY SUBSUMED. Canonical-ID hub solves IDENTITY (near-solved, Babel/NodeNorm pattern); measured-attribute modules (epistasis/synergy/nonadditivity) solve GROUNDING (instrument-measurement is philosophically on par with sensorimotor transduction per Kripke/Putnam causal theory of reference + Hacking entity realism -- if you can measure it via a real assay/instrument, it is grounded, no perception required). Brain answer: abstract concepts grounded by RELAY/composition from already-grounded anchors (Harnad zebra=horse+stripes licensing; Reinboth and Farkas 2022 indirect-grounding; Mason/Schumacher/Just 2021 fMRI shows physicists reason about fermions via non-perceptual inference machinery). CRITICAL CAVEAT: identity != grounding -- a canonical ID with zero reachable measured content is a bare symbol with a good name tag (Bender-Koller octopus / closed relational island), not grounded. Missing piece: a reachability-audit tool (cheap graph traversal, not yet built) to certify which hub entities are genuinely measured-reachable vs bare-ID islands -- this is the cheap decisive test, pre-registered HARD-PASS/FAIL. No sensorimotor/embodied layer needed for this domain (3 independent literatures converge).

plain_language: We asked whether our new knowledge-foundation design (one shared ID system plus separate modules carrying real measured lab data) already solves the deep problem that our system currently just manipulates symbols with no connection to reality. Answer: mostly yes, with one important catch. The shared-ID part just tells you two mentions of a gene are the same gene -- it does not by itself connect that gene to anything real. The real grounding comes from the measured-data modules (actual lab measurements), and philosophy of science says that is exactly how scientific concepts like genes and electrons have always gotten their meaning -- through instruments, not through seeing/touching them. The catch: we need a checking tool (not yet built) that verifies which entities actually have a real measured-data connection versus which ones only have an ID tag and nothing behind it -- an ID tag alone is not grounding, and mixing the two up would let us silently believe things are grounded when they are not.

summary: brain_grounded_data_composition_scope_growth: biology drill on foundational grounded-data base. Composition: sensorimotor/perceptual + motor-action-outcome is the converged foundational anchor (Barsalou perceptual symbols, Mandler image schemas, Lakoff/Johnson primary metaphor, Glenberg indexical hypothesis); statistical-regularity learning (Saffran TP) is the domain-general acquisition mechanism from birth; social/linguistic is the latest, most abstraction-heavy layer, still indexed to embodied base. Scale: raw sensory ~1e6-1e9 bits/sec collapses to ~10-50 bits/sec functional (Zheng and Meister 2024); synaptic capacity ceiling ~1e14-1e15 bits (Bartol 2015) vs Landauer 1986 actually-retained ~1e9 bits (5-6 OOM gap); adult vocabulary ~4e4 words. Growth: synaptic density front-loaded (peak age 1-3, Huttenlocher) with real critical periods (Hubel-Wiesel vision, Lenneberg language-softened), BUT strict Piagetian grounding-then-abstraction sequence is REFUTED by infant core-knowledge findings (Baillargeon, Wynn, Spelke/Carey) showing relational/numerical primitives present in first year -- conclusion is co-development with grounding head-start, not sequential gating; Halford relational-complexity theory gives an independent capacity clock (unary/binary/ternary/quaternary ages 1/2/5/11) separable from grounding richness. Density: ~13.4 features/concept (McRae 2005), multi-modal graded profile across 3+ of ~5-6 modalities (Lynott and Connell), ~6+ exposures for robust (non-fragile) representation vs 1 for fast-map. Substrate-product implication: two independent levers (content density vs relational-capacity) may explain no-advantage-on-thin-data separately; concrete calibration floors now available to test current near-empty substrate metadata against before concluding architecture (not data) is the bottleneck.
plain_language: We researched how the human brain builds its foundational knowledge base: what raw material it uses (mostly touch/sight/motor-action experience), how much data that involves (a huge compression funnel from raw senses down to what actually gets remembered), how it grows over childhood (early and fast, but abstract reasoning does NOT wait for grounding to finish -- they grow together), and how richly a single concept needs to be grounded before its used in reasoning (about a dozen features, several senses, several repeated exposures). This gives us concrete numbers to check our own systems grounded data against, and suggests two separate things may be missing -- not just data volume, but also how many relations our reasoning engine can hold at once.

summary: brain_extrapolation_reasoning_gated_on_grounded_scale: verdict = STRUCTURE-NOT-SCALE two-stage bootstrap (four convergent lit-scans: one-shot concept learning Lake/Tenenbaum, schema-dependent one-trial learning Tse 2007/2011, corvid-vs-pigeon transitive inference split, grid-cell pup development). Brain evidence does not support relational reasoning requiring a large/dense grounded base -- a relational scaffold (schema/compositional prior/relational code) is built once cheaply (10-100 structurally-analogous instances, not thousands) then exploits genuinely sparse new data (1-shot to few-shot) better than associative baselines. Systems lacking the right scaffold need dense trial-by-trial data and still plateau below true relational performance (pigeon TI analogue). Direct implication: too-far-ahead-on-scale is probably a misdiagnosis of our real-data null result; more likely our compositional operator is not exploiting repeated-relational-template structure already present in the 7k-point module. Cheap decisive test pre-registered: stratify module by relation-multiplicity (schema-like repeated-template vs singleton), measure compositional-vs-sum-of-parts advantage separately per stratum, zero new data required. HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds registered.

plain_language: We asked biology whether our reasoning engine needs a much bigger pool of real-world grounded data before it can show an advantage over simple baselines, or whether we are simply testing it unfairly too early. The evidence from child development, animal cognition, and brain-schema research says: no, the brain does not need a huge pile of grounded experience to reason well -- it builds a reusable relational scaffold once from a small structured set (dozens of related examples, not thousands), and after that the scaffold works great even on very sparse new data. Animals/systems without the right scaffold need lots of dense repetitive training and still never reason as well. This means our null result on the small module is probably NOT because we are ahead of our data -- it is more likely because our reasoning mechanism is not yet exploiting the repeated relational patterns already present in the data we have. We registered a same-day, no-new-data test to check this directly.

summary: why_real_interactions_additive_capturable: genuine non-additivity is a structured minority operating on two compatible axes -- population-genetic allele-frequency projection (Hill-Goddard-Visscher) makes bulk/genome-wide measurement additive-dominant AND aggregation dilution hides real interaction-rich pockets (protein-complex-internal pairs, paralog-buffering near-zero-singles synthetic lethal pairs) that curated high-confidence subsets reveal; top genuine-interaction domain = synthetic lethality/AND-gate pairs (no allele-frequency escape hatch, direct fixed-genotype measurement); brain shows same allocation ratio (~5-10pct of PFC/PPC neurons carry genuine nonlinear mixed selectivity, dendritic nonlinearity spatially localized + reserved for correlated inputs per efficient-coding theory) -- refines (does not replace) the sibling Costanzo/Kramer real-dataset ingest test: restrict to complex-internal/near-zero-singles subsets rather than genome-wide averages.
plain_language: We asked why three real datasets (chemical mixing, gene epistasis, real yeast genetic interactions) all turned out to be capturable by a simple additive model even though interactions should matter there. The literature says this is expected at bulk/genome-wide scale (a known population-genetics theorem) but curated high-confidence subsets -- gene pairs in the same protein complex, or pairs where both single-gene effects are individually near-zero but the combination is severe -- reliably show much stronger genuine interaction. The brain itself allocates only about 5-10 percent of neurons to this kind of nonlinear conjunctive processing, reserving it for cases that truly need it, which matches this pattern. Net effect: this is not a dead end, it is a targeting refinement -- retest on the curated subset, not the domain average.

Recommendation: keep the tool, re-test it on a better-chosen slice of the same data before concluding anything further.

Switching to a ranking/detection-style grading (used by the actual gene-interaction research field) should let us tell whether the signal was there all along and just mismeasured, before assuming the method itself needs a bigger change.

plain_language: We asked how real brains encode directed relationships (A relates to B is different from B relates to A) after our own learned multiplicative operator failed at this (it could tell parity apart but not which of two things dominates the other, tying the plain symmetric version exactly). We found and biology-checked three candidate brain mechanisms -- sequential path-like transformations (like how the hippocampus tracks direction of travel), one-shot associative memory writes (like simple Hebbian learning), and firing-order-within-a-brain-wave-cycle coding -- and designed a fair three-way test against our current working solution (tagging each item with an explicit role) using the same test arena as the failed attempt. The path-like mechanism looks most promising; the associative-memory one is expected to memorize but not generalize (a useful, literature-predicted negative if it happens); the brain-wave-phase one is the weakest bet, partly because a well-powered 2025 human brain study just directly challenged that specific theory.

plain_language: Built the small go/no-go test the auditor asked for: instead of measuring average prediction error (which was blind), ask a yes/no detection question -- can we rank the truly synthetic-lethal gene pairs above the neutral ones using only the two gene identities, on pairs held out from training? Using the cleaner published lethality score as the label. But there is a catch we measured up front: in this dataset almost every gene is tested in only ONE pair, so there is nothing to learn a gene's lethality-proneness from -- which would make ANY identity-based method look like chance for a boring structural reason, not a real biological null. So the cell first measures whether enough genes recur; if not, it says 'untestable here, go to a denser screen' rather than falsely declaring the interaction absent. All heavy computation runs remotely; I only did syntax/import checks locally. Ready for the orchestrator to ship.

summary: rank_vs_dimensionality_brain_check: brain is rank-limited per readout unit too (Poirazi/Mel dendritic subunits, Rigotti/Fusi mixed-selectivity capacity bounds) and evades this by SUMMING many independent low-rank (near rank-1) nonlinear terms, not by building one high-rank operator. Rank==dimensionality equivalence is CONDITIONAL: exact/no-tax for LEARNED expansions (Eckart-Young-Mirsky / CP-rank identity, D=R), but random/fixed expansions pay a real dimension-overhead tax that grows with target interaction rank (TensorSketch: exponential in degree; JL: log(N) tax for task-agnostic maps). Substrate recommendation: explicit learned rank-R (R in {2,4,8}) bilinear readout as the near-term cheap fix (zero-overhead, homologous to dendritic sigma-pi subunits), NOT blind-widening the existing sparse-expansion regime (contrast-arm test proposed but expected to be the more expensive route unless its nonlinearity is already product/quadratic-capable).
plain_language: We asked: does the brain hit the same wall our simple bind-and-compare mechanism just hit (it can only cleanly read simple, single-pattern interactions, not richer multi-part ones)? Yes -- individual brain readouts (single neurons, single downstream decision units) are also limited this way. But the brain works around it by adding up many small simple detectors (either many branches on one neuron, or many neurons in a population) rather than building one big complicated detector. We also nailed down a subtle math question: is expanding into a bigger, richer representation the SAME fix as building a fancier detector, or a different one? Answer: same fix, for free, ONLY if the expansion is tailored/learned to the problem; if it is just made bigger blindly, it costs much more room than the tailored version. Recommendation: build a small number (2-8) of learned simple detectors summed together, matching what individual brain neurons do with their branches -- cheaper and more reliable than just making the existing expansion layer bigger.

summary: transition_op_real_data_test_target: scouted real-data test target for VET-CHAIN_GRADE synthetic TRANSITION_OP operator, avoiding the frequency-cap trap. Ranked candidates: (1) CSKG typed-relation (IsA/PartOf/Causes/HasPrerequisite/HasSubevent, verified 419927 rows / 7.3% of CSKG) 2-hop order-reversal split -- zero-acquisition, extends the same-day v3 relation-diversity re-slice from the reachability-audit note, and additive_map (score = -||X_h+D_r-X_t||) has a construction-level commutative-vector-sum flaw analogous to the diagnosed bilinear negative, giving TRANSITION_OP a concrete live target; (2) FB15k-237 DihEdral-style composition subset (external precedent, needs new acquisition); (3) SIGNOR multi-hop signed causal chain (real gap, unbuilt fair-test methodology). Fair-test design: Gregucci et al. 2025 irreducibility filter + CLUTRR-style order-reversal split (train A.B test B.A) + degree-product/frequency-composition floor as mandatory pre-registered arm -- this is what makes asymmetry load-bearing instead of frequency-capped. Brain-grounding: naturalistic transitive inference (real animal dominance hierarchies) is an existence-proof for order-beyond-frequency, but TEM/successor-representation operators have never been tested on real-world data (explicit 2026 literature gap) -- so this is a genuine novel transfer test, not lit-confirmed.
plain_language: We found the right real-world test for our new order-sensitive relational math trick: a subset of our own knowledge graph with genuinely directional facts (part-of, causes, is-a, prerequisite chains), tested with a specific design that rules out the trap of the system just learning which facts are common rather than genuinely understanding order. We also discovered our current live reasoning system has a structural blind spot (it adds directions together, so it cannot tell A-then-B from B-then-A) which this new operator is specifically built to fix. No experiment was run yet -- this is the target scouted and the test designed, ready to hand to a cell author.

summary: brain foundation-building ingest gate: CLS (hippocampus fast one-shot -> neocortex slow interleaved) gated by schema-fit (Tse 2007/van Kesteren SLIMM) + prediction-error/surprise (Lisman-Grace, Duszkiewicz two-novelty-system) + recurrence (Schapiro-Turk-Browne); no unified formal combination rule exists in the literature (confirmed by 2 independent lit-scans) so an explicit decision-tree gate is proposed reusing already-VET-confirmed scoring primitives (additive_map.score_all = surprise; reachability_audit.py = schema-fit; recurrence-count = hard floor). Keystone prediction-error trigger spec + linchpin pilot cell (exp_ingest_gate_consolidation_loop_pilot_v1, 4-batch pre-reg) delivered design-only. Explicit caution: a structurally similar static-tag idea (R7 concept-tag replay priority) already failed on this substrate; this design is built closed-loop specifically to avoid that failure mode, but that is an argument not yet a measurement.
plain_language: Studied how the brain (sleep-consolidation / hippocampus-to-cortex system) decides which new information becomes permanent long-term knowledge versus staying temporary or getting discarded as noise. Found the brain uses three separate signals (does it fit existing knowledge structure, was it surprising, does it keep recurring) but never combines them into one formula in the literature. Designed a concrete, inspectable version of that gate for our substrate, reusing tools we already built and validated, plus a cheap pilot test to check it works before committing to a real build.

summary: consolidation_gate_quantitative_signals: dopamine PE dose-curve is a saturating Hill fn (Eshel 2016, R2=0.84); Tse schema-consistency gate is a narrow 3h-fail/48h-pass window (~15-240x compressed vs ~1mo schema-formation baseline); recurrence is graded/log-sum-power-law (ACT-R), no hard floor found. No paper jointly quantifies PE x schema-fit x recurrence (3rd independent confirmation). Derived substrate rule: fast_track_score=raw_PE*schema_fit / slow_track_score=raw_PE*(1-schema_fit) (Friston precision-weighting decomposition, replaces v4 ad-hoc decision tree, directly fixes coarse-surprise complaint) + recurrence-driven local_precision saturating gate (conjugate-Bayes form). Form borrowed from theory, weights (TAU/PRECISION_MIN/SURPRISE_FLOOR) explicitly ours to calibrate. Cheap decisive test specified (schema_fit-tertile MRR-improvement differentiation, reuses v4 pilot batches, zero new acquisition).
plain_language: Dug up the actual numbers behind the three signals (surprise, fit-with-existing-knowledge, repetition) that gate what a brain (and now our foundation-builder) commits to permanent memory. Found real measured curves for two of the three (surprise follows a specific curve-shape in dopamine neurons; schema-fit has an exact narrow time-window in a classic rat study) but confirmed, for a third independent time, that no study measures how all three combine. Used the math theory that DOES combine surprise with prior-knowledge-confidence (precision-weighted prediction error) to derive a concrete, buildable formula that directly fixes the coarseness problem flagged yesterday -- it uses schema-fit as a splitting weight rather than a separate filter. The exact tuning numbers are still ours to measure, not something biology hands us.
