plain_language: We asked four questions about why our new self-learning reading loop came back null on the McGuffey corpus. Best answer: the loop was predicting the wrong thing (a bag of upcoming words) when it should predict whether the same character/thing comes back later in the story -- that signal survives even in a small, repetitive vocabulary. We also found good evidence that blaming the corpus (need a richer one) is probably a repeated excuse rather than the real problem -- a very similar mistake was already diagnosed and fixed in a famous language-model training method by changing what gets scored, not by getting more data. There is one genuine open question the science does not yet answer: whether simple childrens text specifically makes all the plausible continuations too similar to tell apart, which we can test cheaply. Finally, the fix for the learning loop and the fix for giving words meaningful (not random) codes turn out to likely be the same underlying trick, so we should build them together, cheaply, reusing what already exists, before spending effort on a new corpus.

summary: self_monitoring_build_prior_art_3x: metacognition/abstain -- Chow reject-rule + post-hoc OOD scores (margin/entropy/Mahalanobis) + meta-dprime(Fleming) all ADOPT closed-form; hdlab/conformal.py correct but INCOMPLETE (needs Mondrian per-partition quantile + Gibbs-Candes adaptive-alpha for drift + explicit set-size abstain rule) before it is a production abstain path. Attention/salience -- Kalman-gain precision-weighting + Reynolds-Heeger divisive normalization + sparsemax are the 3 strongest zero-training candidates; existing surprise ingest signal likely already implements IDF/contrast-style salience, missing piece is a source-reliability multiplier + hard-gate stage, not a new signal. P_deflated<=0.45 all claims (cap 0.50).
plain_language: We did a deep literature and build-mechanics scour for two missing pieces of the substrate: (1) knowing when it might be wrong and should say so (abstain), and (2) deciding what incoming information deserves attention when there is too much to process. For abstain, the existing conformal-prediction code is mathematically correct but needs three small, cheap additions (per-category calibration, an adaptive update for when the kind of questions being asked changes over time, and a clear rule for when to actually say I do not know) before it is production-ready. For attention, we found two clean, no-training formulas (borrowed from neuroscience and vision research) that can filter noisy or unreliable information before it gets processed, and confirmed the substrate likely already has a basic version of this via its existing surprise-detection signal -- it just needs a reliability check added on top.

summary: foundation-core 3x build-drill + prior-art scour: codebook=RI/BEAGLE+PPMI-weighting (P_def=0.32), coherence-loop=entity-grid+Guinaudeau-Strube out-degree hardened w/ ALBERT-SOP negative design (P_def=0.50, capped), homeostatic=Oja rule primary + Turrigiano EMA layer if needed (P_def=0.35, zero direct VSA precedent). Integrated system P capped at 0.50 (AND-gate on codebook+stabilizer pilots). Must-fail gameability control flagged (arXiv 2110.07198 shuffle-test critique) for coherence-loop cell design.
plain_language: Researched how to build the three missing pieces of the reading-learning system (a word-vector codebook shaped by real similarity, a self-supervised coherence signal to pick the better sentence-parse, and a stability rule to keep learning from blowing up) glass-box, with no external AI at runtime. Found solid, adoptable prior work for all three (classic distributional-semantics methods, an entity-tracking coherence model with a genuine zero-neural-net implementation, and a classic stabilizing learning rule) but flagged real risks: our corpus may be too small for some methods, and the coherence signal needs a specific extra check to make sure it is not just detecting shallow word-overlap tricks.

summary: second-order learning-system layer (neuromodulatory gating, hierarchical timescale stacking, consolidation/schema-extraction, learned structure-derivation): 4x parallel Sonnet scour found real glass-box-adoptable prior art for all four (Yu-Dayan/Mathys HGF; HTM temporal pooler + Hasson TRW; CLS theory + prioritized replay; SR-eigenvectors + Oja PCA). 3 of 4 are strict second-order (base-loop-gated); structure-derivation (element 9) is base-loop-INDEPENDENT and has a cheap standalone decisive test now. P capped at 0.50 (elements 6-8, novel-synthesis cap) / 0.45 (element 9) per calibration discipline.
plain_language: Researched how to build the next layer of the learning system that would sit ON TOP of the basic reading-learning loop once it exists: (1) multiple independent dials on the learning rate (like reward, confidence, surprise-driven resets), (2) tracking meaning at multiple time-spans (sentence vs paragraph vs whole conversation), (3) compressing many similar experiences into a reusable general pattern instead of storing everything separately, and (4) deriving the systems internal geometry from the data itself instead of hand-designing it. Found solid, credited scientific precedent for building all four without needing an external AI at runtime. Three of the four cannot be built or tested until the basic learning loop exists first; the fourth (deriving structure from data) can be tested cheaply right now, independent of that loop, so a hand-off was filed to try that one first.

brain systematicity/binding drill (3x parallel Sonnet lit-scan): dual-code account (conjunctive+factorized, Bernardi et al 2020) plus fixed TPR/HRR operator (Smolensky/Plate) is the brain binding-systematicity mechanism; NVSA/NS-CL learned-frontend+fixed-composition division has real neural analog (Kymn et al 2024 hippocampal-entorhinal fixed-binding+learned-heteroassoc); CLEVR-CoGenT ablation is the causal proof fixing composition buys held-out generalization. Counter-evidence: Lake and Baroni MLC (Nature 2023) shows fully-learned meta-seq2seq matches human systematicity with NO fixed operator. Delivered a design sketch (learned front-end + fixed native FHRR binding vs flat learned baseline, held-out role-combinations) with 8 explicit construction-determinism guards, the top one (Greff et al 2020 binding-problem critique) independently corroborating our own atom-29369 structure-derivation kill.
plain_language: Researched how the brain lets known building blocks (roles and fillers, like agent/patient in a sentence) be recombined into never-before-seen combinations and still be understood immediately -- the brain keeps two codes at once: a flexible one for capacity and a fixed, algebra-like one that mathematically guarantees new combinations decode correctly. Found strong outside evidence (a 2023 Nature paper) that a fully learned system can ALSO achieve this without any fixed algebra, which is an important caution. Delivered a concrete experiment design -- learned recognizer plus fixed binding math vs. a fair flat-learning competitor -- with explicit guardrails so a win could not be rigged by construction, since a very similar rigging problem already fooled an earlier attempt in this project.

summary: confidence-weighted learning/consolidation: brain uses self-generated (no-ground-truth) confidence/precision to gate plasticity+consolidation via 4 convergent mechanisms (Yu-Dayan ACh/NE precision-weighting, dopamine RPE, Kepecs/Lak OFC confidence-as-decision-byproduct causally dissociated from accuracy, Lisman-Grace hippocampal-VTA salience-gated LTP + CLS salience-weighted replay). Candidate: gate real codebook consolidation by reader own metacognition score (29367) vs the 29376 injected-reliability gate mechanism, held-out on word-similarity AUC (avoid re-entering closed patient-selection well). Brain-faithful in mechanism (P_deflated~0.65); HARD-PASS on a real cell P_deflated~0.35 (capped, and pulled down by S1 being a RELATIVE not absolute signal + arc history of composition over-reads). Guards: self-generated-only (never retune S1 on this task), shuffled-confidence + inverted-confidence + oracle-ceiling controls, distributional precondition check, monotone dose-response.
plain_language: Researched how brains decide what to remember strongly vs weakly: they use their own internal confidence, not an outside answer-key, and that confidence-gating is a real, causally-shown brain mechanism (with known failure modes when confidence is miscalibrated). Sketched a real, can-fail test that uses our reader own confidence score to decide how strongly new text gets folded into its knowledge, checked against a fair ungated baseline and several must-fail controls.

summary: brain source-independence monitoring: source-monitoring framework + illusory truth + crowd-wisdom-collapse literature shows humans have NO default competence for discounting repeated-but-same-origin information (repetition read as independent corroboration by default; override only under salient source cues or accuracy-priming). Designed a graded real-document validation (verbatim/paraphrase/distant-topic tiers via wire-dedup, PAN plagiarism corpus, MRPC/Turku paraphrase corpus + a same-event-independent-authorship hard-negative) with explicit construction-determinism guards and HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds for a real-document common-mode detector test.
plain_language: Researched how the human brain fails to notice when three corroborating sources are secretly one source repeated (illusory truth / crowd-wisdom collapse) -- humans do this badly by default. Used that to design a fair, real-document test (real near-duplicate/paraphrase news corpora, not synthetic) for validating the substrate common-mode detector, with a hardest case (same event, truly independent authors) as the key differentiator.

summary: brain settling/coherence parse-selection: Kintsch CI settling + Rabovsky N400-residual give direct precedent for settling-residual-as-coherence; Hopfield/resonator lit gives explicit construction-determinism traps (beta hyperparameter, D/N capacity cliff, fast-converge-worst-reliability); richness-sharpens-signal leg is analogy-only (no direct brain study). Design sketch: settling-parse-selector for genuinely-ambiguous role assignments, scored by settled-state residual, with 9 fairness guards and a richness sweep isolated from the capacity-cliff confound (fixed codebook size/N, vary relational-structure density only).
plain_language: Studied how the brain settles on the right meaning of an ambiguous sentence (Kintsch construction-integration model) and whether that settling process itself signals confidence, and whether more life experience sharpens that signal. Found strong support for using how cleanly a candidate interpretation settles as a coherence score, but only indirect (not direct) support that more experience sharpens it. Wrote a experiment design with explicit fairness traps to test this on the substrate, including a corpus-richness sweep designed to avoid known false-positive pitfalls from the literature.

summary: ingestion valve (what to consolidate): 5 selection signals (novelty/prediction-error, schema-fit, importance/reward, emotional-arousal, desirable-difficulty/spacing) combine as a branching gain-gated structure, not additive; highest risk = substrate surprise=IDF is a static frequency tag matching the exact static-tag pattern that already lost in-house (R7 wave14b/c) to dynamic model-relative selection; design sketch = branching 5-signal gate (surprise/schema-fit/reliability/coherence/recurrence) onto existing signals+codebook+common-mode-detector, held-out codebook word-similarity AUC target, frequency-confound scrambled-text must-fail check as the first gate.
plain_language: Researched how the brain decides what new information is worth remembering long-term versus letting fade. Found the brain uses several signals (surprise, fit-with-prior-knowledge, importance, emotional weight, effortful recall) combined in a branching way, not just added up, and that our current surprise signal is a simple word-rarity count -- the same kind of static shortcut that already lost to a smarter dynamic signal in an earlier in-house test. Designed a fair, can-fail test for a combined ingestion gate built from signals we already have, with a specific check for the biggest risk (the gate secretly just detecting rare words) built in first.

summary: event-plausibility-web: brain event-knowledge = domain-general EST segmentation (Zacks) distinct from content-bearing GEK/scripts (Schank, McRae, Elman); Elman-SRN proves pure text distribution induces verb-argument expectations without embodiment. Perception-vs-corpus head-to-head: Kauf et al. 2023 shows LLMs solve categorical possible/impossible role assignment but fail graded animate-animate affectedness plausibility -- matches the readers exact stuck point; PIQA attributes the gap to reporting bias (corpora under-sample explicit outcome language), a fixable composition problem not an embodiment requirement. Blind-acquisition lit (Landau-Gleitman, Bedny) undercuts strong perception-necessity for perception-verbs (change-of-state verbs specifically under-evidenced, flagged as gap). Recommend capacity-controlled event-outcome-density corpus ablation (token/vocab/perplexity-matched, BabyLM-style composition sweep, Chambers pseudo-disambiguation + McRae/Ferretti norms as frozen yardstick) BEFORE escalating to perception; prior more-corpus refutation tested SIZE not DENSITY so does not pre-empt this fork.
plain_language: We researched how brains and language models build knowledge of who-gets-affected-in-an-event, comparing seeing real events happen versus just reading a lot about them. Finding: reading alone gets you most of the way there, and the specific gap our reader is stuck on (telling apart two plausible-sounding but different affected parties) is the SAME gap the wider AI research field has already found in text-only language models -- and the leading explanation is that ordinary text rarely spells out physical outcomes explicitly, which is a fixable data-curation problem, not proof we need to add perception/vision. Recommend testing a smarter text diet before building any perception capability.

summary: active-learning loop (curiosity/gap-detect + comprehension-monitoring escalation + belief-revision-needs-replacement-explanation) designed on existing metacognition-abstain + reliability/common-mode components; cheap decisive test = ACTIVE-vs-PASSIVE reading accuracy with bad-source-injection must-fail control; P_deflated=0.35 (whole-loop, capped)
plain_language: Researched how the brain notices it does not know something, decides whether it is worth looking up, and revises its beliefs when new information conflicts with old (including the human failure modes: sticking to debunked beliefs, and the well-known backfire effect turning out to be mostly not real). Designed a build plan for a substrate active-learning loop using pieces we already have (the confidence/abstain signal, the source-trust checker) plus a simple, auditable revise-with-provenance step that does not depend on the still-being-audited learning-loop crux. Gave a fair pass/fail test, with the single most important check being: can the loop be shown to make things worse if fed a bad source with its trust-check turned off (if not, the trust-check is decorative).

summary: learned_recurrent_settling_sentence_gestalt: 3 parallel lit-scans diagnose the settling-parse-selector HARD_FAIL (beta=20 one-shot cleanup collapses in ~1 iteration, residual pinned at float32 noise floor) as the ZERO-NOISE-LIMIT endpoint of a proven Hopfield/EBM/diffusion unification spectrum (arXiv:2506.05178, 2026). Sentence-Gestalt (Rabovsky et al. 2018) gives the exact brain precedent: SU=sum|delta(SG-layer)| stays graded because training targets graded conditional probabilities (no one-hot/argmax target) and shifts labour from activation to connection weights over training -- structurally opposite to a fixed high-gain cleanup. Fix (ranked, both glass-box, no runtime LLM): (1) learn a single scalar effective-beta fit to plausibility-labeled data targeting the proven beta_c phase transition (arXiv:2311.18434); (2) cap per-iteration step size via a damped update (diffusion-style, DIFUSCO/arXiv:2503.21592) forcing multi-step-by-construction independent of training. Pre-registered cheap decisive test reuses the prior note's existing ambiguous-sentence item set with a must-fail random-recurrent-update control. Genuine open risk flagged: codebook pattern-separation may place beta_c above beta=20's neighborhood entirely, meaning no beta fix restores gradedness without also changing codebook construction.
plain_language: We drilled into why our sentence-plausibility-scoring experiment failed (it produced pure random noise instead of a signal) and found the brain literature explains exactly why: a well-known family of memory-network math shows a too-sharp one-shot cleanup step collapses instantly and destroys the signal we needed, while a LEARNED, gradually-settling version (matching how the brain's N400 brainwave response works) stays informative. We have two cheap, fully-inspectable fixes to try next, plus a pre-registered test that can cleanly fail if the fix does not work.

summary: functional_vs_topical_encoding_dependency_context: 29391 location/artifact conflation localized to WINDOW-context choice, not a data/capacity limit -- Levy & Goldberg 2014 dependency-vs-BoW embeddings is direct mechanistic precedent (Florida~Texas functional co-typing vs Gainesville/Tampa topical clustering); brain taxonomic(ATL)/thematic(TPC) dissociation + place-network/tool-network dissociation independently corroborate location/artifact as a real functional-category split, distinct from the 29375 affectedness wall which the same-shape lit (GEK/typicality vs situational-specificity, PIQA reporting-bias) says stays closed. Cheap decisive test: dependency-typed PPMI-SVD codebook variant (same 29368 pipeline, re-keyed context) vs window baseline vs combined vs random-context control, on the exact 29391 typing task, with pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL margins and a design-gate.
plain_language: We found a likely fix for a specific gap: our word-meaning codebook mixes up locations with man-made objects. Well-established language-tech research shows that switching from counting nearby-word co-occurrence to counting grammar-role co-occurrence (subject/object/preposition-of) reliably separates that exact kind of functional distinction -- and the brain shows an analogous separate place-vs-tool wiring. This looks like a cheap, fully-inspectable encoder tweak to try, distinct from the harder who-is-affected problem which stays a genuine wall.

summary: affectedness decomposition: type-level selectional-preference component IS lookup-able (VerbNet SELRESTRS class-level fit confirmed; PropBank/ATOMIC weaker-than-assumed, verb-specific/event-specific not class-general) but bounded by a documented selectional-preference ceiling (Resnik 44.3pct/28.5pct baseline, Heinzerling near-flat 65.60->65.90 F1) and a verified near-chance floor (Chersoni/Bicknell 53pct) on maximally-ambiguous items; honest split ~55-70pct type-discriminable / 30-45pct genuinely per-instance residual (synthesis, not literature-stated); design-gated can-fail test proposed against the closed 29375 baseline (0.474); does NOT reopen 29375 text-derivation null
plain_language: We asked whether the who-is-affected problem (already closed for text-only derivation) could be partly solved by looking up known verb-type facts from dictionaries like VerbNet instead of deriving them from raw text. Answer: partly -- verb-class dictionaries do encode a real, general pattern (break affects breakable things, give affects recipients), but two of three candidate lookup sources turned out less generalizable than hoped, and even where lookup works, published studies show it plateaus well short of solving the hardest, most ambiguous cases. We estimate a meaningful minority of cases stay genuinely case-by-case. Proposed a cheap, fair test to measure this directly rather than guess further.

summary: cheapest-glassbox-grounding-for-perinstance-affectedness: infant causal-perception lit (Michotte/Leslie-Keeble/Spelke) confirms contact+motion-transfer IS a genuinely minimal, object-identity-independent primitive (present 6.5mo) -- cheaper than full scene perception -- but only verified sufficient for THAT-something-changed, not WHICH-of-several-type-compatible-candidates or full Dowty change-of-state affectedness (Woodward goal/agency primitive is separate+richer, untested for sufficiency). Engineering ranking of cheap grounding proxies: VerbNet/curated-signal already closed (type-level only, 29392/29373); ProPara/OpenPI per-instance state-change annotation is cheap+glass-box but CIRCULAR (annotator must already resolve patient to label it) and has ZERO literature evidence of transfer to independent thematic-fit/SRL disambiguation (confirmed gap, not dismissal); synthetic procedurally-generated event-outcome corpora (no dedicated system exists yet for this exact question) are glass-box-legal+cheap-to-build but carry VERIFIED HIGH shortcut-risk across 4 independent analogs (ALFRED microwave-shortcut, CLEVR/CLOSURE compositional failure, Dyna-bAbI 99%->62-72% OOD collapse, Gururangan hypothesis-only artifacts) -- untrustworthy without mandatory anti-shortcut design (systematic-generalization held-out split + scrambled-generator must-fail control); real image/video grounding (Visual Genome-cost-tier) is 2-3 orders of magnitude more expensive with ZERO verified per-instance-affectedness transfer evidence (only type-level/aggregate NLU gains). VERDICT: no off-the-shelf cheap option exists; recommend sequential can-fail testing (ProPara-signal cheapest-first, then anti-shortcut-guarded synthetic generator, then real-perception only if both fail) rather than committing to the big grounding build now.
plain_language: We researched whether there is a cheap shortcut to giving our reader the missing who-was-affected signal, short of building full visual/physical perception. The brain does use a genuinely cheap minimal signal (detecting contact and motion transfer, present in infants before they even recognize objects) -- but that alone only tells you something changed, not which of several plausible candidates changed or what specifically happened to it, which is what we actually need. We ranked every engineering shortcut we could find (borrowing existing state-change-annotated datasets, building a small synthetic simulated-world text generator, or going all the way to real image/video grounding) by cost and reliability. Bottom line: there is no free cheap win sitting on a shelf. The best next step is a cheap, low-risk test using an existing state-change dataset first; only if that fails should we consider building a small synthetic simulator (with careful safeguards against the AI just learning shortcuts instead of the real pattern, a documented failure mode in similar past systems); full real-perception grounding should be a last resort, not a default, since even that has no proven track record for this exact problem.

summary: drill5x #1/5 brain reading-stack component inventory: HAVE/NOT-HAVE across 10 components (visual word recognition, lexical access, morphosyntax, semantic integration, thematic-role/patient assignment, situation-model, predictive-coding loop, consolidation, metacognition, attention/salience); 8/10 have VETd substrate equivalents; the one confirmed wall (thematic-role/patient assignment) is a CONTENT gap not a machinery gap; second unbuilt item (hierarchical multi-timescale prediction) is machinery but sequence-gated, not competitive for most-load-bearing today.
plain_language: We mapped every stage of how a human brain reads and understands a sentence (word recognition, meaning lookup, grammar parsing, who-did-what-to-whom, mental model of the story, prediction-and-correction loop, memory) and checked our reader against each one. Eight of the ten stages already have a working, tested equivalent. The one real gap is not a missing piece of machinery -- it is missing content: knowledge of who typically gets affected in an event (like knowing a dropped glass is the thing that breaks). We proposed a cheap test that tells us whether adding that missing knowledge (vs. adding new architecture) is what actually fixes it.

summary: bootstrapping co-growth loop (drill 3/5, KEY drill): the human+ML evidence splits cleanly into two halves. CONTENT growth via scaffolded read-lookup-verify-bind is well-precedented (Share 1995 self-teaching per-item mechanism; Snedeker/Gleitman/Brent cross-situational noun-seed; P=0.55 deflated). RULES improving from content growth ALONE is the literature-disfavored half, not merely uncharted: explicit correction has near-zero effect on grammar rules (Brown and Hanlon 1970; Marcus 1993), bare dictionary lookup does not transfer to general skill (Miller and Gildea 1987), and the Matthew-effect-as-compounding-widening-gap claim FAILS to replicate across 25+ years (Pfost et al 2014 systematic review; Protopapas et al 2011 direct non-replication) -- P=0.20 for this component, whole-loop AND-gate capped at P=0.25 (below standard novel-synthesis 0.50 cap, pulled down because one required component is actively disfavored by direct evidence not just silent). ML self-training/model-collapse literature (Shumailov 2024 Nature; Alemohammad 2023; Gerstgrasser 2024; Gupta et al 2024 ROME/MEMIT catastrophic forgetting) independently converges on WHY: self-referential loops collapse without an independent (not self-generated) verification anchor each round -- which is architecturally what the existing reliability/common-mode gate already is (P=0.50, strong structural match). Substrate-native reframing: since the free-algebra binding is CLOSED/fixed, rules-improving means SELECTION-among-fixed-options (thematic-fit/argument-role disambiguation), matching what syntactic bootstrapping actually claims, not new combinatorial capacity. Cheap decisive test designed: 3-arm (content-frozen baseline / content-growth-only / multi-generation gate-on-vs-off) plus seed-ablation threshold test, reusing existing codebook-AUC metric + frozen thematic-fit yardstick, with 5 must-fail controls. Prediction: content-growth half HARD-PASSES, rule-improvement-from-content-alone half HARD-FAILS -- redirecting future work toward an explicitly rule-task-supervised calibration step (reciprocal-teaching analog) as a SEPARATE buildable component, not a setback to the learning-layer program.
plain_language: We asked the core question directly: can a reader grow its world-knowledge AND its grammar/comprehension rules together by reading more with a helper (dictionary/KB), each improving the other in a loop -- the way some theories of child language learning describe? The honest answer, from both child-development research and machine-learning research on similar self-improving loops: growing the KNOWLEDGE side this way is well-supported and buildable now. Growing the RULES side just from more knowledge, with no direct feedback on the rules themselves, is NOT well-supported -- correcting a childs grammar directly barely works, looking up a word in a dictionary does not make you better at grammar in general, and the classic rich-get-richer reading-snowball effect does not actually show up cleanly in 25 years of studies when researchers looked for it directly. The machine-learning side explains why: a loop that only ever learns from its own outputs tends to degrade unless something independent checks it at each step -- which is exactly the role our existing source-trust checker already plays, a genuinely lucky architectural fit. We designed a fair test that predicts the knowledge-growing half will pass and the rules-growing-from-knowledge-alone half will fail, which would mean rules need their own separate, directly-supervised training step rather than growing for free from more reading.

summary: grammar-construction resources for role assignment: VerbNet per-alternation static frames (not a generative rule engine) + UD obl:agent (confirmed named passive-agent relation) + TPP/PDEP preposition-sense lexicons stack to give a machine-readable STRUCTURAL role-assignment layer, orthogonal to and upstream of the already-drilled SEMANTIC thematic-fit/type-lookup axis. Before-connective construction has zero resource coverage found this cycle (flagged gap). P_deflated=0.45 for HARD-PASS on the 4 non-connective construction types; P=0.55 that this is genuinely additive vs the tried reader (uncertainty is substrate-side: whether the existing reader already exploits parse structure).
plain_language: We looked for grammar textbooks/resources that spell out WHO-DID-WHAT-TO-WHOM rules explicitly (word order, passive voice, load/spray phrasing, prepositions) rather than relying on world knowledge. Found: VerbNet already lists separate patterns per phrasing (a usable lookup table, not a smart rule), and the standard sentence-parsing convention has a specific named tag for passive-voice agent flips (near-free once a sentence is parsed). This looks like a genuinely different, cheaper lever than the world-knowledge problem we already hit walls on -- but one type of sentence (before/after connecting two events) has no matching resource yet, and we still need to check whether the reader already uses this information before banking it as new.

summary: Adoptable glass-box parser scan for reader extraction wall: 3-way reconcile -- REVIVE our on-disk June structured-perceptron dep-parser (hdlab/semantic_parser.py + perceptron.py, 0.787 UAS, MST/2nd-order cell ladder already authored) is PREFERRED over external adoption; Stanza (UD, Apache-2.0, June-2026-maintained, pip-only) is the FALLBACK if REVIVE proves stale. Neither auto-fixes subject-propagation across coordinated verbs -- a small glass-box rule layer is needed either way. AllenNLP SRL confirmed archived 2022, MINIPAR/RASP ruled out (abandonware/license). Design-gated can-fail test specified against the 56/67-miss McGuffey gold diagnostic.
plain_language: We scanned every mature open-source sentence parser (Link Grammar, Stanford tools, spaCy, Stanza, AllenNLP, etc.) to fix why the reader keeps missing who-did-what-to-whom in coordinated/relative-clause sentences. Mid-drill we discovered we already built our own transparent parser back in June that is 90% of the way there -- so the recommendation flipped to finishing that instead of bolting on an external tool, with Stanza kept in reserve as a fallback.

summary: step2_integrated_role_decision: dedup found 3 half-built pieces (LCCP structural weighted-vote, graded-thematic-fit gate, explicit-grammar rules) never jointly trained; brain-check (MacWhinney/Bates cue-validity) predicts English word-order dominance may make other cues redundant not complementary; designed exp_integrated_vote_role_decision_oracle_gold_v1 (joint logistic over structural+voice+prepsense+gfit+plausibility, conformal calibrated-abstain reusing hdlab/conformal.py, oracle-pairs harness parser-independent); P_deflated=0.35 integration beats best-single-cue.
plain_language: Researched how to make the reader combine multiple weak clues (word order, passive voice, preposition meaning, verb-typical-object facts, plausibility) at once instead of one at a time, the way humans do. Found we already have most of the pieces built separately but never combined into one trained decision; designed the combined test and pre-registered honest pass/fail bands, including the realistic risk that the clues may be redundant rather than complementary.

summary: verb-affectedness gate: reframed task-proposed hard 3-way categorical gate (patient/target/no-patient/abstain) as WRONG per the field -- Dowty/Beavers/Tsunoda all converge on GRADED affectedness (entailment-count / monotonic scale / continuum-with-cut), light-verb-hood is a cline too (Grimshaw&Mester + PropBank .LV + PARSEME). Design revised: graded verb-class score (VerbNet causative-inchoative alternation / Levin search-perception classes / PropBank .LV+PARSEME lookup) feeding a confidence/abstain weight into the Step-2 vote, not a hard filter. Construction gold (data/gold_construction_argstruct_ewt_v1) covers target+patient buckets but has NO light-verb bucket -- flagged data gap. Distinguishes from closed 29392 (SELRESTRS) and flags unresolved redundancy risk with closed 29373.
plain_language: We asked the linguistics literature whether who-is-affected should be a hard 3-way category (real patient / uninvolved target / no patient at all). The answer is no -- every serious framework treats affectedness as a graded score, not discrete buckets, so we redesigned the plan to score verbs on a scale and feed that into the existing confidence/abstain layer instead of building a rigid classifier. This also found we are missing example sentences for the no-patient (light-verb, e.g. take care of X) case in our test data.

summary: reader compgen edge dedup: naive reader-level binding-vs-flat compgen test is NOT novel vs atoms 29379-82 (re-derives free-algebra combination result when roles are gold, or mislabels ordinary parser-OOD-generalization when they are not, since binding sits downstream of the learned role-DECISION, not inside it). Genuinely untested slice = resonator/binding-MEDIATED role-decision vs flat classifier, matched features, CFQ-style compound-divergence held-out-combination split. P_deflated=0.30, capped 0.50.
plain_language: We checked whether testing our reader for compositional generalization (handling never-before-seen verb+sentence-pattern combos) would tell us something new. Verdict: the obvious version of that test would just re-confirm something we already proved with synthetic data, or would secretly just be measuring how well the parser generalizes (a separate, already-partly-answered question) rather than testing the binding mechanism itself. There IS one real untested question left: does making the actual role-decision (not just the downstream encoding) go through the binding mechanism help on real, noisy text? We designed a fair, can-fail test for that narrower question but have not run it -- expected outcome leans negative (extraction noise likely dominates), which would itself be a useful, informative result.

summary: self-improving reader learning curve: DEDUP correction (main finding) -- 29386/89 + same-day confidence-weighted-consolidation note already cover single-step gate + wiring + single-pass continuous rate, but band10_learning_curve is a 2-point occ1-vs-occ2 delta, NOT a multi-round trajectory, and the gate is binary not continuous-persisting. Genuinely novel slice = wrap existing v2 loop machinery in an outer 5-round loop with a continuous confidence-modulated rate, 5 arms (GATED/UNGATED/RANDOM-CONFIDENCE/INVERTED-CONFIDENCE/PASSIVE), new must-fail signature = GATED-vs-UNGATED gap must WIDEN with round count (compounding, not one-time). Brain: testing/spacing effect (climb) vs reconsolidation-update-failure + repetition-strengthened illusory truth (Fazio 2015, entrench). ML: Arazo 2020 confirmation bias, Rizve 2021 UPS calibration-dependence, Shumailov 2023 model-collapse / error-avalanche (2025) as the ungated-analog. Mandatory precondition: partition round-0 errors extraction-class vs decision-class (parser arc-margin AUC 0.807) before the round loop -- most likely HARD-FAIL is a flat curve because residual is extraction-bound, which is itself an informative, correctly-localized result per the design.
sub_agents: research:sonnet brain litscan (resumed after connection drop)
plain_language: We checked whether the reader-self-improvement idea (get better by correcting its own mistakes over multiple rounds, trusting confident corrections more than shaky ones) was already built. Mostly yes -- but only as a single-step version. What is genuinely missing and worth building next is the actual improvement CURVE across several rounds of self-correction, plus a test that a badly-tuned version should get WORSE the more rounds it runs (mirroring how humans can talk themselves into remembering something wrong if they keep re-telling it to themselves). We also flagged the most likely way this could fail cleanly: if most of the readers mistakes are about missing information rather than deciding wrong with the right information, self-correction has nothing to fix, and the test is designed to show that honestly rather than hide it.

summary: negation/factuality gate for who-is-affected reader: brain evidence (Kaup two-step simulate-then-negate, contested; Nieuwland/Kuperberg pragmatic-licensing cost) + glass-box NLP prior art (NegEx->DEEPEN/DepND dependency-scope fix; *SEM-2012 UiO1 F1=85.26 scope-resolution; UDepLambda UD-graph scope propagation; FactBank/De Facto compositional factuality) directly support a UD Polarity=Neg cue + advmod-attachment + conj-propagation gate, verified against real UD-EWT parses this cycle. Reader currently discards not/never as FUNCWORD noise (code-confirmed gap). Construction gold has real but thin negation incidence (~13-14/136 clean items after scope-check, ~10%) -- data-pull to n>=40 flagged as the single biggest risk, ahead of any mechanism-level HARD-FAIL.
plain_language: We researched how humans and prior NLP systems handle negation ("he did NOT break it") so the reader stops assuming every event it parses actually happened. Found strong, credited prior art (NegEx, *SEM-2012, FactBank) for exactly this kind of fix, verified our own parser can detect it, but found the current gold dataset only has about 10 percent negated sentences -- likely too few to properly test the fix without pulling more examples first.

summary: plausibility-trained coherence gate: the settling loop null (~0.003 coherent-vs-incoherent separation) is a codebook-content gap, not a dynamics bug -- cleanup memory stores identity atoms only, never role-filler typicality. Fix: reuse the already-banked Clark&Weir class-smoothed thematic-fit table (exp_graded_thematic_fit_integrated_reader_gate_v1, 26 WordNet supersense classes, 182 verbs, 99k-token mining corpus) as an FHRR attractor bundle P_role per verb-role, wired as a settling-ENERGY bias term (residual = identity_residual + lambda*energy_plaus) rather than v1s HARD_FAILED role-decision-classifier wiring. Cheap can-fail test specified with mandatory scramble-codebook must-fail control (reused from v1 arm C design) to rule out frequency/length confounds.
plain_language: The comprehension loops coherence check currently cannot tell a sensible sentence from a nonsense one because its lookup memory only knows which words exist, not which combinations of roles and fillers are typical. We already built a typicality table earlier this week for a different purpose; this drill designs how to reuse that exact table as a bias inside the settling process itself, plus a cheap test (with a built-in trap to catch false positives) to check whether that fixes the null result.

summary: sharded_situation_model: hippocampal indexing theory + relational memory + time-multiplexed WM (Lisman-Idiart theta-gamma) + event segmentation all converge on INDEX-PER-ITEM, never superposition -- fixes component#2 bundle-collapse (0.53@2->0.22@8) by replacing the accumulating VSA bundle with a sharded proposition table (index_key -> small local role-filler bundle), retrieval via key-lookup+local-unbind (matches measured 1.000), settling repositioned to degraded-cue index resolution (coref) not content disambiguation.
plain_language: Studied how the brain keeps track of many facts in a story without blending them together and losing detail -- it turns out the brain never blends; it keeps a separate pointer/index per fact and only holds a few active at once. Applied this to fix a just-measured capacity wall in the reading component that was blending facts into one vector and losing who-did-what-to-whom after just a few sentences.

summary: cross-sentence-integration task drill: UD-EWT who-is-affected measures ROLE ASSIGNMENT (local patient-NP), not IDENTITY RESOLUTION (bind NP to discourse entity) -- only the latter is structurally cross-sentence (Principle B excludes same-clause antecedents). Proposed concrete task: anaphoric-patient identity probe over LitBank gold coreference (real narrative, high pronoun density vs UD-EWT newswire) with a corpus-inspection design-gate (off-sentence-evidence rate >=90%, distractor rate >=25%) that verifies a per-sentence baseline is structurally blind BEFORE any reader comparison is run. Serves as the deferred prerequisite for component #2 (CI comprehension loop / sharded situation model) whose settling step needs a genuine degraded-cue index-resolution task to earn its keep.
plain_language: We found the reason the reading component was not showing any benefit from tracking entities across sentences: the test we were using only asks about facts fully contained in one sentence. We designed a new, more honest test using real published fiction (LitBank) with pronouns, where the answer genuinely cannot be found without remembering who was mentioned earlier -- and we specified a cheap check to confirm that before building anything.

summary: compgen decode-coupling brain-check: human compositional generalization also degrades with difficulty/WM-load (Halford relational-complexity, Waltz relational-integration-under-load, Bays-Husain, center-embedding, Fodor-Pylyshyn systematicity-as-competence-not-performance) -- no brain or ML evidence of difficulty-invariant generalization strength. Decode-coupling is STRUCTURAL not a substrate SNR bug. Proposed reframe: baseline-relative graceful-degradation CG bar (beat fair flat baseline + beat chance at every difficulty, absolute decline expected) instead of absolute held-out>0.70 floor. Recommend against attempt-5 on same decode mechanism; recommend cheap re-analysis/harness-reuse of fair-baseline arm at hard/harder difficulty settings before any new cell.
plain_language: Checked whether humans compositional-reasoning ability holds steady under difficulty/mental-load the way our compgen chain-grade bar demands, or degrades like our substrate does. Verdict: humans ALSO degrade under load -- no known system, biological or artificial, shows difficulty-invariant generalization. This means our decode-coupling wall is a structural property of any capacity-bounded reasoner, not a bug to fix with a 5th attempt. Recommends reframing the pass bar to be relative (beats a fair baseline at every difficulty) rather than absolute, and doing a cheap re-analysis before spending on new experiments.

summary: HP2 shared-factorization bar brain-check: Frankland-Greene (dedicated agent/patient populations) + eLife 2024 (null binding-signature) show the brain uses ROLE-SPECIFIC scaffolding + shared distributional-semantic geometry, NOT one shared cross-role bind operator -- structurally closer to the TIED control than to native compgen design. HP2 (shared-factorization-must-win) is PARTIALLY MIS-SPECIFIED: it conflates shared-vs-role-specific (biology says role-specific) with learned-vs-fixed (the real free-algebra concern, still valid). Proposed disentangling test: geometry-randomization ablation on the TIED control (unrun). Flags mandatory adversarial VET before any re-adjudication (conflict-of-interest), parallel to the difficulty-invariance reframe precedent.
plain_language: Checked whether the brain literally uses one shared role-binding scheme (which is the bar our closed compositional-generalization result was measured against and failed). Evidence says no -- the brain uses dedicated per-role populations plus a shared pool of word-meaning representations, which looks more like the plain control we tied with than like our fancier shared design. That means the bar that closed our result may have been testing for something brains do not actually do. Proposed a cheap follow-up test (scramble the control word-meanings and see if it still works) to settle it, and flagged that any re-opening of the closed result needs independent adversarial review, not self-review, before it counts.

summary: is_learned_not_algebra_free_CG_bar_coherent: adversarial refutation attempt on Director terminal hypothesis (atom 29437 geometry-ablation VET) -- Director half-right (any generalizer has SOME fixed function at decode-time, trivially true, brain not exempt) but over-reaches declaring the CG target incoherent; real discriminator is CONTENT-DEPENDENCE direction of the geometry-ablation signature (fixed-FHRR: random-beats-real = free-algebra; a genuine meta-learned/MLC-pattern operator predicts the OPPOSITE sign) -- this test has never been run on a meta-learned operator, only on fixed FHRR. P_deflated=0.35.
plain_language: Checked whether the Director is right that our compositional-generalization target was impossible to define coherently (making the recent null result a success in disguise). Found the Director is partly right (every system, brains included, applies some fixed rule at decode time) but is over-claiming when using that to close the search entirely: there is a real, testable difference between a rule an engineer fixes in advance and a rule a system acquires from data (like the MLC network from prior research), and we have a cheap way to tell them apart that has not been tried yet.

summary: puns/multiple-interpretation as learned-composition CG testbed: brain drill (Swinney exhaustive-access + Giora graded-salience + Coulson-Kutas N400/P600 pun-repair = incoherence-triggered re-search over already-active senses, not upfront rare-sense valuation; Tomasello/Goldberg usage-based construction acquisition = composition IS grammar-like/generalizing, contra meaning per-item lookup) -> design: reuse the validated atomize+sleep loop for composition, gated by puns (frequency-guess fails by construction) + the sign-flip discriminator (real-beats-random = genuine learned composition vs 29437 free-algebra random-beats-real signature). Cheapest first test = escalation-viability probe (atom 29411 contradiction-flag + selectional-restriction check) on curated puns, BEFORE building atomize+sleep infra.
plain_language: Researched how the brain handles puns/double-meanings (it activates both meanings then detects when the common one doesn't fit and re-searches for the rare one) and how kids learn grammar (by generalizing from many specific examples, the same way our reading system already learns new words). Designed a cheap first test using puns to check whether our composition-learning idea can beat the common-meaning-wins default, before building the bigger learning loop.

summary: brain-check on 29440 (linear composition loop = WordNet-similarity-kNN in disguise): does the brain also generalize composition via similarity, or does it genuinely beat similarity -- verdict: beat-similarity bar is BRAIN-FAITHFUL, not mis-specified. Four converging lines (wug test, Marcus 1999 infant ABA/ABB vs SRN failure, Lake-Baroni meaning-free primitives, Gentner relational-shift/structure-mapping) show human composition generalizes to semantically dissimilar novel combinations where a similarity-kNN has nothing to vote on -- Marcus 1999 is a near-exact historical precedent of our own finding (associative/similarity nets succeed only on near-neighbor test items, fail on designed-dissimilar ones, humans succeed). Explicitly checked against the adversarial guard (Director pattern of convenient mis-specification calls) and judged genuinely different: positive convergent evidence + a directly-adversarial precedent, not just brain-fails-too. Proposes a cheap relational-vs-similarity CONFLICT-corpus test for fork A (nonlinear settling / role-binding-with-conflict-resolution) scored only on cases where similarity-vote is wrong.
plain_language: We asked: when our learned composition system turned out to secretly just be a similarity-lookup (refuted last cycle), is that actually fine because the brain does the same thing? The answer is no -- well-established psychology (the classic wug test, a 1999 infant-language study, modern AI-composition benchmarks, and analogy research) all show people generalize to things that are NOT similar to anything they saw before, in a way a similarity-lookup cannot do. So the bar we set (beat similarity) is the right bar, not an unfair one, and we have a concrete cheap next test to build toward genuinely beating it.

summary: agreement-attractor real-text CG-bar scoping: GO on subject-verb agreement-attraction (Linzen 2016 + Gulordava 2018 nonce) as fork-A real-text relational-conflict LEARNING testbed; nearest-noun surface baseline wrong on 40-46 pct of attractor sentences; head-tracking feature learnable without explicit parse (Goldberg 2019 BERT, Hewitt and Manning 2019); brain-check shows human agreement is cue-based/similarity-sensitive by mechanism (Wagers Lau Phillips 2009), 5-20 pct attraction errors are brain-faithful not a bug; minimal design specified with dual fair baselines and no-parse-given single variable.
plain_language: Scoped a candidate real-text test for genuine compositional generalization: can the substrate learn that a verb should agree with its true subject (e.g. keys) rather than a nearby distracting word (e.g. cabinet) with the opposite number, purely from examples, without being handed the grammar rule. Human brains make similar mistakes about 5-20 percent of the time via a similarity-based memory process, so a comparable error rate in the substrate would match biology, not indicate a bug. Recommendation: GO, build this test next, with a concrete data source and fair baselines specified.

summary: glassbox consolidation vs relational geometry: CLS neocortex slow-learner is backprop-lineage (opaque) in original model (McClelland/McNaughton/OReilly 1995, Kumaran/Hassabis/McClelland 2016); flat prototype/overlap replay (Lewis and Durrant 2011 iOtA) IS a similarity statistic, matches our own 29440 refutation, NO-GO; but sequential/generative replay as multi-hop graph traversal (Kurth-Nelson et al 2016 Neuron, Liu et al 2019 Cell, Schwartenbeck et al 2023 Cell) provably escapes pairwise similarity while staying glass-box (sampling/rollout, no backprop) -- GO for a NEW candidate: atomize into typed relational edges + compositional-traversal replay, tested on validated 29443 agreement testbed with a scrambled-relation-type content-dependence discriminator. Residual risk: edge-extraction from raw text without oracle parse may itself require gradient-trained-like inference (deferred bottleneck, HARD-FAIL condition pre-registered).
plain_language: We asked: can a fully-inspectable (no black-box AI) memory-consolidation process, like the brain sleep-replay we were modeling, learn to spot relationships (like which word a verb actually agrees with) instead of just falling back on surface patterns? The brain literature gives a clear split answer: the simple version (average similar memories together) cannot do it -- confirmed dead end, matches what we already found. But a different, well-documented brain mechanism (replaying learned steps in new combinations, like inferring a shortcut you never walked) DOES escape that trap, and it is still fully inspectable, no black-box needed. So we have a concrete, still-transparent next design to try, with an honest flag on where the remaining hard part might hide.

summary: glassbox_structure_induction_hierarchy_from_linear: 3-way lit-scan (brain stat-learning, glass-box grammar-induction prior art, hierarchy-from-linear crux) converges NO -- no published inspectable non-gradient mechanism induces genuine hierarchical/relational structure from raw linear data without a hierarchical prior/hypothesis-space handed in advance (MDL/BPL/Kemp-Tenenbaum/DMV-CCM/iterated-learning all selectors not inducers; best candidates ABL/ADIOS documented fragile on WSJ-scale natural text). Matches our own atoms 29437/29443 from the outside. Conditional GO for one cheap ABL-style falsification test on the 29443 testbed before conceding the glass-box-invariant tradeoff; pre-registered expectation is HARD-FAIL.
plain_language: I researched whether there is any inspectable (non-black-box) way for the system to figure out grammatical structure (like which word is the main word in a phrase) on its own from raw text, without secretly being handed the answer. Three independent research literatures all say no -- every known transparent method either gets handed the shape of the answer in advance, or needs an opaque optimizer somewhere. There is one cheap, narrow test worth trying before accepting that conclusion, but the literature predicts it will also fail on real text. This sets up a real program-level choice for the user: accept that limit, or trade away the transparency requirement.

summary: resonator/glass-box input-dependent selection: resonator networks are the right mechanism CLASS (iterative, non-gradient, content-dependent factorization) but wrong SCALE for subject-role selection over 2-5 sentence-local candidates (M^F tiny, nowhere near resonator limit-cycle onset ~1.2e5; own crux-v2 resonator smoke just HARD_FAILED w/ 95pct nonconvergence at large KG scale, a live caution). Right-sized fix = extend already-built+validated hdlab/iterative_attractor.py (ATT1, modern-Hopfield/attention-equivalent softmax settling per Ramsauer 2020) with a second bind-based agreement-compatibility energy term; converges with McClelland-Kawamoto 1986 constraint-satisfaction settling + Hummel-Holyoak LISA mutual-inhibition role-competition literature, both non-gradient. Honest fairness-gradient flagged: hand-set compatibility weights vs hand-labeled match features vs raw bind-derived scores differ in how much is mechanism vs smuggled rule. CORRECTED task premise on disk: dep-parser plateaued at UAS=0.7875 MIDDLE_BAND (not 0.85); its 2nd-order-features arm HARD_FAILED and its MST-global-decode arm never ran (infra failure, cheap untested lever). Pre-registered ARM_SETTLE test on the 29443 Linzen agreement testbed.
plain_language: We asked whether a specific brain-inspired mechanism (resonator networks, which iteratively figure out which pieces make up a mixed-together signal) is the fix for the reader not being able to dynamically tell which noun is the true subject of a sentence when it is not the first noun. Answer: that mechanism is the right FAMILY of idea but built for a much bigger search problem than we have here; our own recent direct test of it just failed badly at a larger scale, which is a useful warning sign. The right-sized version is a smaller, already-built settling mechanism on our own substrate, extended with one new ingredient (checking singular/plural agreement between candidates and the verb). We also caught and corrected a factual error: the dependency parser never actually reached the 0.85 accuracy level it was assumed to have hit; it plateaued lower, and the most promising unfinished lever for it never got tested due to a technical hiccup, not a real failure.

summary: incremental_stack_parsing_paradigm: transition-based (Nivre stack+buffer) parsing is real, buildable mechanism-class fix for buried-subject/positional-default failure (batch arc-factored decode disk-confirmed as the culprit), but NOT a structural guarantee (McDonald-Nivre 2011 error-propagation on long dependencies is the live risk) and does NOT resolve the b2 hierarchy-induction wall (the stack IS a hand-given prior, same fairness tier as ABL/ADIOS, not an escape from it). No VSA/HDC transition-parser precedent exists in the literature -- genuinely novel construction, moderate-high engineering risk concentrated in stack-depth crosstalk (may be brain-faithful per Miller-Chomsky center-embedding limits). GO, scoped narrowly to agreement+attachment+small-scale role-selection.
plain_language: Researched whether building sentences up incrementally (word by word, like humans do, keeping a mental stack of what phrase is currently open) fixes the reader bug where it picks the wrong subject when a distractor noun sits inside a side-phrase. Verdict: yes it should help and the biology strongly supports incremental processing, but it is not a guaranteed fix (a known NLP finding says this style of parser can actually struggle MORE on exactly this kind of long-distance sentence), and it does not solve the deeper problem of learning grammar structure from scratch -- it is a smarter way to use structure we already hand it, not a way to discover structure. Recommended as a real, worth-building next step with clear-eyed odds (about 40%) and named risks.

summary: exp_agreement_sigmap_depth_induction_v1 FULL inline HARD_FAIL: distributional-signature depth-map does NOT extrapolate to held-out function words (map_hf=0.6012 < majority 0.6279; isolation over scalar +0.0095; K-fold gap -0.0618). Mechanism validated (map_full=0.7071 -> ceiling 0.7561, scramble DROP +0.1924, flip=0).
plain_language: We tried to teach the reader to guess a NEW grammar-word's structural role (does it open an embedded phrase?) purely from how that word is distributed in text -- how often it appears, whether it sits between two nouns, at a comma, etc. -- so it could handle words it never trained on. It failed the honest test: when the decisive high-frequency prepositions were held out of training, the learned map could not reconstruct their depth-opening role from surface statistics, and actually did slightly worse than making no guess (it mis-assigns depth to neutral words like determiners that LOOK similar on the surface). The mechanism itself is sound (with all words present it reaches 0.71, near the 0.76 hand-coded ceiling, and the depth-scramble control confirms it really uses depth not word position). So this is a precise EARNED bound: surface distribution alone is insufficient to INDUCE the embedding-depth role -- confirming 29453 was correctly down-rated, and pointing the next build at richer structural input (the incremental transition-parser STACK) rather than more distributional features.
importance: high -- closes the surface-distribution route to genuine depth-role induction; first honest FW-holdout test of the induction wall; redirects the roadmap to the parser-stack depth feature

summary: Integrated vision pipeline (recognize+bind+ground) landed HARD_PASS locally; novel-class wall confirmed
outcome: FULL (5 seeds) local run: HARD_PASS_INTEGRATED_PIPELINE__NOVEL_CLASS_WALL_CONFIRMED. recog=0.837 (HP0.75) bind ATTN=0.831/FLAT=0.541 margin=0.289 (HP0.15) ground_hog=0.910 (HP0.30) e2e=0.813 (HP0.55). Novel-class probe (digits 8,9 held out from ALL training/binding): recognition/grounding accuracy exactly 0.0 (structural, no leakage); score-gap -0.015..-0.021 across seeds, well inside the pre-registered WALL_CONFIRMED band (<=0.05) -- the system cannot distinguish a genuinely novel category from an ordinary wrong-class mismatch (vision-side analog of the COGS unseen-filler wall).
substrate_product: Assembled the 3 separately-validated vision pieces (HOG recognition, Treisman attention binding, sharded grounding) into one glass-box battery on real sklearn digit photos; confirmed the recognize->bind->ground chain holds on held-out instances of known classes AND mapped the novel-category frontier honestly (structural inability to represent/flag unseen classes).
plain_language: We wired the three vision pieces together for the first time and it worked end to end on real photos; as expected, it cannot recognize or ground a digit class it was never shown, and it also cannot tell that such an image is unfamiliar rather than just another wrong guess.

summary: pivot_selectional_independent_kb_2afc_v1 ran to completion (local, no queue): tests whether an INDEPENDENT KB (VerbNet+WordNet, zero corpus attestation) reproduces the LLM-self-built rich-table lift from 29471.
outcome: FULL landed MIDDLE_BAND_PARTIAL_GRANULARITY_RECOVERY: acc_thin=0.4746, acc_indep_kb=0.5678 (gap=+0.093), acc_llm_rich=0.8136, frac_of_llm_lift_recovered=0.275, scramble_margin=+0.034 (clears 0.03 anti-cheat floor)
plain_language: Rebuilt the rich selectional-knowledge table from an independent, inspectable source (VerbNet+WordNet) instead of the LLM-self-built one, to test whether the earlier 0.475->0.814 lift was circular. The independent KB recovers about 27%% of the lift and the anti-cheat scramble control confirms the recovered lift is genuinely knowledge-driven (not an artifact), but most of the LLM advantage is not reproduced by this local symbolic KB -- points the foundation-build toward a richer/distributional local KB or an LLM-built-then-KB-vetted hybrid rather than pure VerbNet/WordNet.

summary: recall_miss_diagnosis: of 56 recall-miss gold patients (recall_ceiling=0.44), 54/56 (96%) are extraction misses vs 2/56 (4%) filter drops; dominant mechanism (38/56, 68%) = reader runs ONE main-verb role-assignment pass per sentence (find_main_verb picks first non-aux VB*), so any second predicate in a multi-clause sentence gets zero candidates; secondary (16/56, 29%) splits into imperative/null-subject agent-gate drops (4), phrasal-verb oblique-as-patient valency mismatch (1+), and coref-resolved-surface-vs-gold-surface scoring artifacts (>=3, not a knowledge gap); tertiary (2/56, 4%) = quantifier-pronoun POS-gate miss (one/those tagged CD/DT).
plain_language: We asked why the reader misses over half of the correct answers before it even gets to choose among candidates. Answer: the reader only fully analyzes the FIRST verb in each sentence -- if a sentence has two actions ("he took the ball and threw it"), the second action never gets looked at, and that explains 68 percent of the misses. A few more misses come from small rule gaps (commands like "Build it up" with no stated subject) and a scoring quirk (the reader correctly figures out who a pronoun refers to but gets marked wrong because the answer key wants the pronoun word itself). Almost none of the misses (4 percent) are due to over-filtering. This tells the team the next knowledge investment should be verb-frame / structural knowledge that lets the reader analyze every action in a sentence, not more word-plausibility ratings.

summary: multipred_subcat_argstruct_recall_v1 ran FULL locally (no queue): tests whether processing every predicate in a sentence (not just find_main_verb single pass), gated by VerbNet+curated subcat frames, recovers the 68%-dominant multi-predicate extraction miss class from the leg-2 diagnostic.
outcome: HARD_FAIL_MULTIPRED_NEEDS_REAL_PARSE: recall_ceiling 0.44->0.47 (rise 0.03 < 0.05 pre-registered floor); F1 0.2708->0.2782 (rose); precision 0.1956->0.1975 (no collapse); both must-fail controls fired correctly (keepall precision 0.1486 < frames 0.1975; scrambled recall_ceiling 0.45 < frames 0.47).
plain_language: Tried the cheapest fix for the reader recall ceiling: give every verb in a sentence its own argument search instead of just the first one, guarded by a lookup table of which verbs take direct objects. It only recovered a small slice of the misses (17 of 56) and regressed 14 previously-correct ones, so the honest verdict is that this cheap fix is not enough -- the remaining misses need a real shallow parse, not a smarter lookup table.

summary: online_knowledge_condenser_selectional_v1 FULL landed HARD_PASS_CONDENSATION_GENERALIZES: unseen-noun generalization accuracy climbs 0.500->0.750 with exposure while the verbatim/abstraction-off control stays flat at 0.500 (gap=+0.250); frozen-condenser control flat; shuffled-table control partially collapses.
outcome: ran local inline-local (no queue); self-test PASS, smoke PASS, smoke4x PASS, FULL landed HARD_PASS (commit 46bc8a76b)
plain_language: Built the first prototype of an online knowledge condenser: as the substrate reads real text it abstracts verb-noun evidence to a WordNet class (e.g. peel+FOOD) instead of memorizing exact word pairs, and this lets it correctly judge NEW nouns it never saw with that verb (e.g. peel+mango) -- a control that only memorizes exact pairs cannot do this at all, isolating abstraction as the mechanism that matters.

summary: multipred_argstruct_agentfix_kbgate_v3 FULL landed HARD_FAIL_INTEGRATION_BOUNDED_CEILINGS_COMPOUND (inline-local, not queued): parse-scoped agent/subject-routing fix worked (7/8=87.5% of 29478 localized agent-routing regressions closed; F1 0.4478->0.5738, recall_ceiling 0.60->0.70, precision 0.3571->0.4861, all clearing their pre-registered bars) but the knowledge-gate anti-cheat control (scrambled-table) FAILED TO FAIL: 0/76 multi-patient competition instances had a different argmax pick under the scrambled table vs the real one, because the 29479 table almost never covers BOTH competing candidates at once (coverage/OOV partitioning drove the pick, not the tables plausibility content). Honest verdict: the parse-fix lever integrates cleanly; the knowledge-gate lever as wired here adds precision from argmax-reduction/coverage-partitioning, not from demonstrated selectional-content value at this reader-integration scale.
plain_language: Fixed the agent/subject-routing bug in the parser-integrated reader (closed 7 of 8 localized regressions) and F1/recall/precision all improved past the prior cells own numbers, but the pre-registered anti-cheat control caught that the knowledge-gate lift is not clearly due to the knowledge tables actual content (a scrambled table produces the identical output) - a real, well-earned negative on the knowledge-integration claim specifically, not on the parse-fix.

summary: Beyond-linear real-language-structure candidate ranking: implicative-verb-class x negation entailment (Karttunen XOR truth table) mined from UD-EWT ranks #1 -- real external gold rule, ~184 clean-verb tokens/~72 negated cooccurrences verified live this cycle, held-out-verb split guards lookup-table circularity. Ranked below it: psych-verb animacy-conflict reversible roles (#2, needs curated conflict subset), PP-attach cue-conflict resubset (#3, cheap but re-slices already-tied data), double negation (#4, too rare), quantifier scope (#5, no local data). WSD-multi-cue excluded as already-closed frequency axis; garden-path deprioritized as construction-favorable trap.
plain_language: Looked for a real (not made-up-for-the-test) piece of language understanding that genuinely requires combining two clues in a non-additive way, the kind of structure our new nonlinear learner is supposed to be good at. Found one: verbs like fail vs manage flip the meaning of what happened depending on whether the sentence is negated, in a way no simple weighted-cue-adding scheme can capture, and there is enough real example text sitting in our existing corpus to test it fairly right now.

summary: multipred_argstruct_measuredreliability_joint_v1 ran FULL inline-local: fixes the saturated-combiner loophole in the prior jointreliability_positional_v1 cell by MEASURING (not hand-setting) the positional-cue reliability via leave-one-lesson-out cross-validation.
outcome: HARD_FAIL_KNOWLEDGE_STILL_REDUNDANT_ON_STRONG_BASE; P1 base-repro held (gap=0.0492); P2 scramble-fires held (n_diff_scramble=4, was ~0 in prior cell); F1 ARM_BASE=0.5246 == ARM_PLUS_KNOW=0.5246; rescue_rate=0.0 on structure-wrong subset; sensitivity-stable across 0.7x-1.3x positional-reliability scaling
plain_language: The prior test of whether word-knowledge helps the reader pick the right sentence-object was inconclusive because a hand-picked confidence number accidentally silenced the knowledge signal (scrambling it changed nothing). This re-run MEASURES that confidence from data instead of guessing it, and confirms the knowledge signal is now genuinely live (scrambling it does change picks) -- with a live signal, the honest finding is that this selectional-knowledge table still does not help this reader beat structure alone, a deeper and now-trustworthy negative result.

summary: learner_program_induction_symbolic_extrapolation_v1: PLUGIN 4 (program-induction DSL search) added to hdlab/learner, zero core.py changes; HARD_FAIL_UNSEEN_CELL_UNIDENTIFIABLE on the bother-negated cell (mechanism sound, cell is a provable exact MDL tie -- info-theoretic, not associative-vs-symbolic)
outcome: landed inline (foreground, no queue); commit c81b2364a
plain_language: Built a 4th learner hypothesis-class (program induction: searches boolean formulas like AND/OR/XOR/NOT and picks the most compact one that fits the data) to see if it could correctly fill in a fact the module previously got 0% wrong on (an unseen combination of two features). It turned out this specific case is a genuine tie between two equally-simple, equally-fitting formulas (a coin flip, not a search failure) -- the mechanism itself works correctly (verified on two independent test tasks), so this is an honest negative result about this one case, not a broken build.

summary: reader_component_oracle_ablation_audit_v1 run inline-local FULL: component-level oracle-ablation diagnostic on the who-did-what reader (V3_INTEGRATED, F1=0.5738)
outcome: AUDIT_SANITY_OK; reproduced baseline exactly; ranked uplift ENUM=0.0527 > ROLE=0.0391 > PARSE=0.0221; all-oracle ceiling=0.7106 (gap 0.2894, MIXED components+logic-bound)
plain_language: Ran a diagnostic that swaps each stage of the best sentence-reader (who did what to whom) for a perfect/gold version one at a time, to see which stage is costing the most accuracy. Candidate/predicate detection (missed words/verbs) is the biggest lever, followed by role assignment, then parsing. Even with every stage perfect, accuracy only reaches 0.71 (not 1.0), meaning some of the gap is the reader's own decision logic, not just its inputs.

summary: multipred_argstruct_enumext_v4 landed MIDDLE_BAND_PARTIAL_ENUMEXT (inline-local FULL, not banked): recall_ceiling 0.70->0.75, F1 0.5738->0.5882, precision holds 0.4861->0.4839.
plain_language: Extended the reader's candidate enumeration to recover do/have-as-lexical-verb and ECM/small-clause subject-sharing structures. Recall ceiling rose past 0.70 to 0.75 and F1 rose past 0.5738 to 0.5882 with precision holding, but fell just short of the pre-registered +0.02 hard-pass margin (genuine partial win, not vacuous). Key deliverable: all 25 remaining misses on this slice are single-sentence-parse-recoverable, none require cross-sentence/situation-model context yet.

summary: multihop_reasoning_layer_biology_and_design_sketch: forward-prep drill for ARC-Challenge multi-hop climb. Found substrate already has a production-validated Merkle-audited K-hop chainer (substrate/khop.py: FB15K-237 2-hop r@5=0.705, WebQSP 97.6%, CWQ 92.6%) -- no new mechanism needed. Traced d=25 depth-cliff to the F/N capacity bound already derived in wave14e theory doc (confirmed by disk data, not a mystery); refined by a 2026 mechanistic paper (arXiv:2606.24948) showing per-fact retrieval-capacity CONTENTION on high-degree facts (not average depth) is the real bottleneck, echoing this codebase own percolation annotation on PP-11. Biology (TI paradigm vs TEM/hippocampal-replay literature) shows two distinct regimes: small rehearsed relational sets are read out one-shot (symbolic-distance effect), while genuine graph-path traversal is modeled as iterative hop-by-hop retrieval-with-cleanup -- matching khop.py design exactly, and validating cleanup-per-hop as biologically correct not just engineering. Envelope-fit: WorldTree explanation-graphs show ARC needs ~6 facts on average but as an AGGREGATE support set, not a strict path chain -- a probable task-shape mismatch with khop.py machinery; also flagged a 2025 paper showing evaluation-format artifacts explain much of the ARC-Challenge/Easy gap. Recommends a cheap (~1-2hr) task-shape diagnostic BEFORE building any new chain-cell, reusing WorldTree/QASC annotations already public. Pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL/MIDDLE-BAND bands for the eventual 2-hop cell included in the note.
plain_language: I researched how the brain does multi-step reasoning (like A leads to B leads to C) and compared it to our own reasoning-chain code, to prepare for the next phase once the current fact-lookup work lands. Good news: we already built and proved out a working multi-hop reasoning chainer, so no new invention is needed there. But I found a real trap to avoid: the standard science-test benchmark (ARC-Challenge) may not actually need chained reasoning the way we assumed -- it looks more like needing several separate supporting facts at once, not a step-by-step chain, and some of its difficulty may just be a scoring-format quirk. So before building anything new, I recommend a cheap same-day check to confirm what shape the real questions need, so we do not spend weeks building depth into a chain when the real fix is something else (like making sure our fact library actually contains the needed facts, which is exactly what fixed a very similar problem earlier this year).

summary: bindsettle CI settle-dynamics: Kintsch 1988 primary-source verified signed connection-matrix relaxation (positive=coherent-support, negative=contradictory, zero=irrelevant; clip-negative-renormalize; epsilon=.001; his own worked example retains top-4 propositions between cycles = independent anchor for Cowan-4). Gives bipartite fact-vs-choice graph template + 10 concrete settle-dynamics choices for the staged aggregation-retriever cell. Theta-gamma multiplexing solves anti-blur maintenance, NOT combination (literature gap, confirmed by lit-scan); CI relaxation is the separate combination mechanism. Biased-competition/normalization/PBWM explain funneling MECHANISM but none derive why-4 (Cowan/Kintsch remain the only cardinality anchors). Eliasmith SPA/Spaun (KB-credited) grounds node-cleanup sub-step in the same FHRR binding algebra.
plain_language: Studied exactly how the brain combines a few facts into one answer (not just holds them in memory) using the Construction-Integration model of reading comprehension, read directly from the original 1988 paper. Found the real algorithm: facts that support each other reinforce, facts that contradict each other actively suppress each other, and this settles over several rounds to a winner -- and the original paper itself keeps exactly 4 facts at a time, matching our working-memory design. This gives concrete, brain-grounded rules for the in-flight aggregation-retriever cell (how many facts, how many rounds, how to declare a winner, what would make it fake vs real) instead of an ad-hoc scoring formula.

summary: ARC fact-combination prior-art scan: TableILP ablation shows multi-row combination beats single-row by +10.5pts on curated Regents tables (61.5 vs 51.0%), but every published multi-fact/structured solver (TupleInf 23.73%, TableILP 26.97%, DGEM 27.11%) is statistically indistinguishable from the 25.02% random baseline on ARC-Challenge -- AI2 own diagnosis (2018) is retrieval bias (IR favors question-similar sentences, misses partial-match chaining facts), not combination-mechanism weakness. VSA+iterative-settling-for-QA confirmed as a genuine gap (QAVSA=single-pass+PLM-dependent, ARC-VSA-2025=single-pass no settling, resonator nets factor one code not combine facts); closest settle-dynamic precedent is Thagard ECHO 1998 (non-VSA, non-QA) -- new build-on citation for the bindsettle-CI note.
plain_language: Checked whether anyone has already answered our exact question -- does combining several retrieved facts beat retrieving just one, for ARC science questions. Yes: a 2016 system (TableILP) proved combination helps a lot (+10.5 points) when facts are curated and dense, matching our own curated WorldTree fact source -- a good sign. But on the harder ARC-Challenge split, every combination method ever published has been stuck at chance level, and AI2 own diagnosis is that their fact-retrieval step (not the combining) was biased and missed the right facts. This gives our in-flight aggregation cell a precise new pre-check (verify our retrieval avoids that same 2018 bias) before it can honestly claim a win or loss on the hard split. Also confirmed nobody has built a vector-symbolic system that combines facts through an iterative settling process the way ours is designed to -- that piece stays genuinely novel.

summary: Contradiction/opposition representation drill: our GloVe+WordNet HD encoder gives all-positive cosines (0.04pct negative fact-fact edges) because this is the textbook antonym problem in distributional semantics (antonyms are paradigmatically close, not far) -- confirmed by lit-scan + direct code read of SemanticHDEncoder.fused() (synonym+hypernym additive pulls only, zero antonym term) and _ci_two_phase (FC/FF are raw cosine, no other signal). 3 convergent biology lit-scans (antonym/polarity vector-space fixes; N400/negation staged-processing; opponent/bipolar neural coding) all point the same direction: abstract propositional opposition is NOT brain-like sensory bipolar/anti-correlated coding (color/motion opponency requires a physical continuum to split) -- it needs an explicit LABELED relational link, computed by rule/lookup, not derived from similarity geometry. Recommended primary fix: a RELATION-POLARITY slot populated from WorldTree relation-type (IFTHEN/COUPLEDRELATIONSHIP, already-typed unused data), WordNet antonym lookup (already-loaded, zero new dependency), and negation-cue detection -- overriding cosine-derived CI edges, feeding the already-correct settle dynamics from the prior 07-24 drill. Antonym-repulsion retrofitting (counter-fitting/PILSA) is a secondary generalization layer; a vector-space negation operator is contraindicated by the two-step-simulation evidence (negation is staged suppression, not a clean algebraic flip). Cheap decisive test pre-registered: polarity-aware CI-settle must beat the pure word-overlap baseline specifically on the Challenge lexical-HARD subset (currently the baseline wins). P_deflated=0.42.
plain_language: We figured out why our fact-checking system could not tell when two facts CONTRADICT each other (it only measured how similar words sound, not whether they oppose). Turns out this is a well-known problem in the field (antonyms and synonyms look similar to word-similarity math), and brain research says the fix should be an explicit rule (using an existing science-fact database plus a dictionary of opposites) rather than trying to make the similarity math itself detect opposites. We wrote up a concrete design and a test to prove it actually helps before building it.

summary: ARC retrieval-is-the-wall: 3 convergent lit-scans (hippocampal CA3 attractor/modern Hopfield, Collins-Loftus spreading activation/ACT-R fan effect/HippoRAG, Tulving encoding-specificity + Badre-Wagner discriminative PFC retrieval) all point at the same fix -- retrieval must be RELATIONAL (spread via typed links, not raw cosine) and DISCRIMINATIVE (relevant to the choice-set, not just similar to the stem). Diagnosed our prior PPR/spreading-activation HARD_FAIL (exp_ppr_spreading_activation_cpu_v1, recall=0.217) as CONFOUNDED (synthetic 120-node random graph + single superposed bundle -- matches a documented HippoRAG failure precondition), not a refutation. Concrete design: multi-cue PPR/spreading activation over the REAL WorldTree fact-graph, seeded by SemanticHDEncoder entity-linking from question+ALL choices, node-specificity down-weighted, 1-2 hop capped, then discriminative re-rank (facts that separate choice scores, not just cosine to stem) -- feeding the existing unchanged bind+settle combiner.
