Pre-registered a 5-arm can-fail cell (baseline / PPR-only / PPR+discriminative / shuffled-graph control / hub-dilution ablation) with HARD-PASS = recall lift >=0.15 on WorldTree gold central facts AND end-to-end Challenge clears chance by 95% CI AND shuffled-graph control collapses to baseline. Not dispatched (research-only per contract).
plain_language: We figured out WHY our system fails to find the right facts to answer science questions: it only grabs facts that use similar WORDS to the question, but the brain finds relevant facts by following MEANING-based connections (like a mental web) even when the wording is totally different, and by asking which facts actually help tell the answer choices apart. We designed a concrete fix based on a real published brain-inspired AI method (HippoRAG) plus found that an earlier attempt at this on our system failed for a fixable reason (it used a fake tiny random test graph, not our real fact database). Wrote up the exact test that would prove or disprove this before we build it.

summary: mental simulation / model-based reasoning / grounding lit-scan for ARC causal-science questions: literature converges on a 3-way split (perceptual physics-engine simulation for dynamic scenes; Pearl do-calculus structure-propagation for known multi-variable causal graphs; cached covariation facts for canonical taught single-hop relationships) not a binary simulate-vs-retrieve. Substrate ALREADY has a working do-calculus primitive (cap_map PP-270 atomic, PP-307 L3-composition HARD_PASS recall=1.000) that the live ARC fact-retrieval pipeline (the_climb) does not route through. Diagnosed as a SECONDARY wiring gap, not a primary missing-mechanism gap. Pre-registered a 2-arm cheap decisive test (fact-retrieval vs do-calculus-routed on the COUPLEDRELATIONSHIP ARC subclass) with HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL thresholds.
plain_language: We asked whether our science-question-answering approach (look up facts, combine them) is missing the kind of mental simulation a person uses to reason about physical causes and effects. The literature says humans actually use a mix of three things depending on the question: real simulation for dynamic physical scenes, a structured cause-and-effect graph for known relationships, and simple memorized facts for things they were directly taught. The good news: our substrate already has a working cause-and-effect graph mechanism (Pearl do-calculus) that passed its test earlier -- it is just not currently wired into the science-quiz-answering pipeline. That is a cheaper fix than building simulation from scratch.

summary: learning_control_neuromodulation_inventory: biology-first inventory of brain LEARNING+CONTROL+NEUROMODULATION machinery (reward-RPE/basal-ganglia actor-critic, predictive coding, 6-channel neuromodulatory precision-weighting, CLS error-driven consolidation, credit-assignment [fresh lit-scan], unifying-principle debate [fresh lit-scan]) vs the hand-designed substrate. KB-check found 7 prior notes already covering items 1-4 in depth (RPE/basal-ganglia Go/NoGo already HARD_PASS-built on substrate; predictive_coding.py + Spoke1 cell MIDDLE_BAND-tested; 6-channel self-manager designed but unbuilt; CLS/consolidation heavily drilled, converging on the 07-20 SYNTHESIS finding that the ONE missing element is an error-driven correction loop). Two fresh lit-scans filled genuine gaps: (5) credit assignment -- brain never relies on a single global scalar signal alone, always pairs it with a local structural mechanism (three-factor eligibility tags, dendritic/cerebellar spatially-exact error channels); on this substrate, credit assignment for negative verdicts is currently performed by the human Director via manual research-drill diagnosis, the same functional role at hours-timescale instead of milliseconds. (6) unifying principle -- free-energy principle is a contested minority position among philosophers of science/neuroscientists, not consensus; brain is better described as a stack of interacting-but-irreducible mechanisms. Blunt assessment: the gap is not yet a blocker (todays 5 parallel ARC-pipeline threads each produced concrete hand-designed fixes without a native loop) but IS the compounding-return bottleneck -- the substrate only improves when a human runs a diagnosis cycle, never from its own graded experience. Proposed cheap decisive test: wire one existing hand-set ARC-pipeline weight to a duration-extension RPE rule keyed on real dev-set correctness, vs fixed baseline, with shuffled-signal and random-walk anti-tautology controls.
plain_language: I studied how the brain tunes and improves itself while running (reward signals, prediction-error, chemical messengers that adjust learning rate, overnight memory consolidation, and how it figures out WHICH part of itself to blame after a mistake) and compared that to how our own system currently improves. The honest finding: our system already has brain-like building blocks for some of this sitting unused on the shelf (a working reward-learning circuit, a prediction-error module), but none of them are hooked up to whether our science-question answers are actually right or wrong. Right now, the only way our system gets better is that I personally diagnose what went wrong after each test, the way a doctor runs tests to find a problem -- the brain does this automatically and locally in milliseconds; we do it manually over hours. This is not stopping todays progress, but it is the reason progress requires a human in the loop every time instead of the system learning on its own from experience.

summary: brain-architecture completeness lit-scan (biology-first): 11-stage / ~30-subsystem inventory of the brain pipeline for knowledge-based MC science QA, cross-referenced against our ARC/ingestion build. Converges with own diagnostics (29537/29538) that the missing primitive is Stage-5 retrieval CONTROL: Badre & Wagner anterior-VLPFC controlled/strategic retrieval + mid-VLPFC post-retrieval selection + retrieval-induced-forgetting competitor suppression -- distinct from the automatic/associative (cosine-similarity) retrieval we already have. Proposes a cheap decisive test (suppress+re-retrieve on the WorldTree/ARC-Challenge surface-trap lure subset, lure_rate 0.23) with pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL bands.
plain_language: We mapped out every brain system involved in answering a science quiz question from memory (perception, memory, reasoning, attention, executive control, metacognition, learning, grounding -- about 30 systems total) and checked which ones our AI already has versus is missing. The big miss: the brain has a way to override a tempting-but-wrong answer that just LOOKS similar to the question (a top-down search-past-the-obvious-match mechanism), and we do not have that yet -- which matches a wall we already hit independently. We proposed a cheap, concrete test to build and check that specific missing piece.

summary: Combiner robustness to imperfect facts: CI/PCS settling degrades brittly (basin-boundary snap) not gracefully near threshold; schema/frame gap-filling (Bartlett/Rumelhart/Minsky/scripts) is validated but has NO native confidence discount (Bower et al., DRM remember-judgments) -- naive gap-fill risks confidently-wrong answers; on-the-fly hippocampal bridging (REMERGE) is real but only over intact premises; khop.py + trustworthy-reader gate (29465) are the unwired primitives. Design: confidence-gated bounded escalation loop (gate/bridge-if-available/discounted-gap-fill/else-abstain) wrapping the unchanged CI settle. 7-arm can-fail cell designed, not dispatched.
plain_language: Studied how the brain stays correct when its memory search comes back incomplete or messy, since our retrieval will never be perfect. Found the brain uses three tools -- filling gaps with a typical guess (but ALWAYS flagging that guess as less certain, which our system does not yet do), bridging two known facts to infer a missing one, and knowing when to say I am not sure rather than guess confidently and be wrong. Designed a testable next experiment that wires these three things together, but did not build it yet.

summary: grounded/relational meaning for the 29544/29545 selection-relevance wall: 3 lit-scans (grounded/embodied cognition; relational/KG-embedding math; concepts-as-theories causal-feature cognition) converge on symmetric-cosine similarity being PROVABLY (RotatE lemmas, Tversky 1977 asymmetry, DistMult provable antisymmetry-blindness) incapable of encoding the asymmetric/causal relational structure relevance-judgment needs. Cheapest brain-faithful rung = structured-relational: route the ALREADY-BUILT typed role-bind (hdlab/hd_fact_store.py REL/ARG0/ARG1, proven no-crosstalk to 1M facts) into the 29545 selection-feature stage, which currently only reads the flat symmetric SemanticHDEncoder cosine. Perceptual grounding (Barsalou/Lambon-Ralph) ranked lower for THIS wall: real but modest, task-narrow (similarity/categorization) evidence, and an explicit confirmed literature gap on fact-vs-distractor relevance discrimination specifically (Jones et al 2022: even GPT-3 closes only 1/3 of a narrower affordance gap). Learned-interaction (29545 itself) already shown capped at 0.189 in-sample precision -- a representational not optimization ceiling. Concrete can-fail cell proposed: exp_arc_selection_relational_meaning_v1 (5 arms incl scramble control + swapped-argument mechanism-clean subtest), pre-registered HARD-PASS/FAIL bands, NOT dispatched.
plain_language: We asked biology and math why our fact-matching system cannot tell a genuinely relevant fact from one that merely sounds similar, even when we let it learn from examples (it caps at 19pct precision when 96pct is needed). The literature gives a clean answer: similarity-based matching is mathematically incapable of telling direction (X causes Y is not the same as Y causes X), the same way it cannot tell antonyms apart. The fix that is cheapest and best-matched to how brains judge relevance (weighing causal role, not just resemblance) is one we already partly built: our fact store already tags facts with typed roles (subject/relation/object) for storage, but the relevance-picking step never uses those tags, only a flat similarity score. We designed a concrete, cheap test to wire that in and see whether it closes the gap, without needing to build any new machinery.

summary: content-thin concept-meaning wall (hydroelectric-vs-nuclear-vs-coal): 3 lit-scans (situated-conceptualization/distributional-hypothesis; PDP semantic-cognition + McRae/Cree featural norms; Lambon-Ralph ATL hub-and-spoke + computational property-augmentation) converge that fine concept discrimination is NOT an emergent side-effect of co-occurrence -- Rogers-McClelland PDP models that reproduce it are trained on explicit property triples, not text stats; Lucy and Gauthier 2017 + Grand/Blank/Pereira/Fedorenko 2022 show distributional vectors are good at taxonomic (same-category) structure and weak/entangled/axis-dependent exactly on perceptual-mechanistic content. Our own failure signature (retrieves nuclear/coal facts for a hydro question) matches semantic-dementia coarse-preserved/fine-lost ATL-hub-damage gradient (Warrington 1975; Hodges/Graham/Patterson 1995). Cheapest brain-faithful rung (rank 1 of 3, disk-verified feasible): bind WorldTree property-relation rows (SOURCEOF/REQUIRES/CAUSE/KINDOF/PROP-RESOURCES-RENEWABLE -- confirmed on disk to contain hydro=renewable/water, nuclear=fission/waste, coal=nonrenewable/combustion/pollution rows) into the CONCEPT representation itself via the already-built hd_fact_store.py bind/bundle primitive, one level up from where it currently runs (fact-instance level). This is a DIFFERENT lever than the prior 07-24 structured-relational fix (which addresses relation-type/argument-order and cannot help when gold and lure share IDENTICAL relation shape, e.g. both are PRODUCES(plant-type, electricity)). Concrete 5-arm can-fail cell proposed (exp_concept_featural_enrichment_v1, incl scramble control + single-vs-multi-property binding ablation + a hand-verified hydro/nuclear/coal planted mechanism subset), pre-registered HARD-PASS/FAIL bands across 4 predictions, NOT dispatched. Confirmed literature gap: no study anywhere tests feature-augmented representations on a fact-vs-lure SELECTION task specifically -- P estimates deflated accordingly (0.25-0.45).
plain_language: We asked biology why our system cannot tell a hydroelectric dam fact apart from a nuclear plant fact when both are phrased the same way (X makes electricity) -- the words describing them are just too similar in our meaning-space. The science gives a clear answer: brains do not get this fine-grained distinguishing knowledge (water vs nuclear fuel vs coal) for free from reading text that mentions these things near similar words -- brain-like models that CAN tell them apart were specifically trained on explicit fact-properties (this thing uses water, that thing uses radioactive fuel), and people who lose that integrated property knowledge (a documented brain-damage condition) keep the general category (it is a power plant) but lose exactly this kind of specific distinguishing detail, matching our own systems failure. The good news: we already have, unused, a knowledge table with exactly these distinguishing facts (hydro is renewable and uses water, nuclear produces waste, coal is a fossil fuel that pollutes) and we already have the tool to attach properties to concepts -- we just are not doing it yet at the concept level. We designed a concrete, cheap test to check whether wiring that in actually lets the system pick the right answer, without needing any new infrastructure.

summary: holistic_set_selection: biology-grounded design for ARC-Challenge selection wall (29548) -- Kintsch CI over-generate-then-settle + Georgopoulos population-vector readout (=existing bundle combiner, unchanged) + Usher-McClelland/Wang/Albantakis-Deco N-alternative competitive margin (confirmation-trap guard) synthesized into a greedy set-construction algorithm scored by MARGINAL cross-answer-choice discrimination margin (group-level metric, not per-fact); must-fail control = random-same-size subset; cheap decisive test specified (gold-in-random-order margin separation) to run before full build. SHAPE+METRIC change, PLACE unchanged. P_deflated=0.38-0.40.
sub_agents: general-purpose:sonnet x3 (parallel lit-scan: global-workspace/population-coding, Kintsch-CI/Thagard-ECHO, hippocampal-attractor)
plain_language: Researched how the brain builds a group of supporting facts when no single fact alone proves the answer -- found 3 real brain mechanisms (population-vector voting, a construction-then-settling process, and racing multiple candidate answers at once) and turned them into a concrete next experiment design for the ARC-Challenge fact-selection problem, reusing the fact-combining mechanism that already works and changing only how the fact SET gets built.

summary: verification-by-derivation reasoning pivot (serving atom 29549, retrieve->select->combine=similarity-not-entailment root cause): biology-grounded design for VERIFICATION-BY-DERIVATION over ARC candidate answers. Backward-chaining-from-candidate (Tanji-Hoshi PFC, Rips PSYCOP proof search) meets forward-chaining-from-givens, reusing the ALREADY-PROVEN substrate bidirectional meet-in-middle search shape (0.620 chain-grade depth-5) retargeted onto a TYPED/DIRECTIONAL graph built from WorldTree relations (parse_tablestore_typed() reused as-is) restricted to LICENSED causal/conditional types. 4 converging literatures (LISA, Gentner systematicity, PFC relational-integration capacity limits, ACT-R basal-ganglia serial gated rule-firing) ground why typed/directional/serial structure -- not symmetric similarity -- avoids it-is-all-connected. Chain-consistency reuses existing polarity/CI settle. Must-fail controls: SHUFFLE_DIRECTION + UNTYPED_SIMILARITY_NULL (the second directly operationalizes similarity-vs-entailment). Cheap connectivity-only decisive test pre-registered GREEN/YELLOW/RED before full build. Honest flag: WorldTree causal/conditional coverage (~1700-2000 rows total) likely under-covers ~2200 questions -- coverage-subset reporting recommended. Joint P_deflated ~0.13-0.15.
plain_language: We researched how the human brain actually checks whether a proposed answer is correct -- not by seeing what sounds similar, but by trying to build an actual chain of reasoning steps from the question to that answer, the same way a detective builds a case or a lawyer builds a proof. We designed a concrete next build that reuses pieces we already have (a parser that already reads our knowledge base fact-tables as typed if-then/causes/requires rules, and a forward-and-backward search trick we already proved works elsewhere) to actually try to PROVE each of the 4 answer choices, instead of just picking whichever one sounds most related. We also designed the exact tests that would prove this is really working versus just faking it (scrambling the rule directions should break it if it is really using logic, not just closeness). We flagged honestly that our knowledge base may simply not have enough of these explicit if-then rules to cover every question, so we designed a cheap first check for that before committing to the full build.

summary: science-precise causal rule sourcing + rule-chaining vs model-based reasoning fork
plain_language: We looked for more trustworthy cause-and-effect science facts to feed the ARC quiz-answering system, and found something better sitting unused on disk: the WorldTree dataset already has 1145 hand-written, pre-typed causal-relationship templates (like "as X increases, Y increases") that need no extraction, plus we found the substrate ALREADY has a working what-if propagation tool that nobody wired into the quiz pipeline yet. We also asked biology whether humans even use a giant stored-rule lookup for science questions, or build small mental models instead -- the answer is a mix, and the mental-model approach only avoids the coverage problem for GENERAL relationship types, not for knowing specific entities (a dam vs a nuclear plant), which is the same wall the meaning-representation work is already chipping at from another angle.
recommendation: ship the do-calculus routing branch cell over the_climb using WorldTree CAUSE+IFTHEN+COUPLEDRELATIONSHIP tables (no extraction needed) before fetching any new external corpus
mechanism: schema-fragment-routing (do-calculus over hand-typed WorldTree relationship templates) vs flat semantic-fact-retrieval

summary: Learned meaning front-end (Component 1, atom 29555 target): biology-grounded design for a Rumelhart-style item+relation->property-vector predictor trained via error-driven/discriminative-completion signal (Rogers-McClelland PDP + Saxe-McClelland-Ganguli exact eigenvalue-ordering theory + Lambon-Ralph ATL hub-and-spoke + Gibson differentiation theory), replacing frozen GloVe/WordNet cosine at the concept-representation slot feeding the 29546 selection stage. Learning curve gate (coarse-before-fine, sigmoidal per mode), must-fail shuffled-label control, and a compositional-generalization probe (expected partial-fail, scoped separately from the native-bind roadmap item) all pre-registered. Distinguishes LEARNED (gradient/error-corrected, generalization-tested) from the prior HAND-BOUND property-binding arc that failed answer-agnostic selection.
sub_agents: research:sonnet (self, no child spawn per instruction)
plain_language: We looked at how the human brain learns to tell apart easily-confused concepts (like hydro vs nuclear vs coal power) that start out looking the same to it, and designed a concrete, testable way to give the substrate that same learning ability instead of hand-wiring the answer in. The design includes a built-in learning-curve check and traps that catch it if it is secretly cheating (memorizing) or if it cannot handle brand-new combinations it never saw.

summary: native_binding_compositional_generalization: designed exp_native_binding_compositional_generalization_v1 (extends 29556 flat-MLP-hub cell) -- fixed role hypervectors + fixed hdlab bind (Hadamard/circular-conv) + single shared LINEAR readout, vs flat MLP; corrected held-out split isolates CATEGORY-CORRELATED relations only (fair systematicity test, per Fodor-Pylyshyn/Smolensky-TPR/LISA/NVSA convergence); P_deflated=0.45, HARD-PASS ho_lift>=0.25, HARD-FAIL<0.10
mechanism: native VSA bind (fixed algebra) + single linear readout vs flat MLP hub
recommendation: dispatch hdi_exp_dev to implement exp_native_binding_compositional_generalization_v1 per the pre-reg (corrected held-out split MUST be built+unit-checked first)
plain_language: Researched why our item+relation-to-property learner memorizes instead of generalizing to new combinations (a well-known failure mode in cognitive science called lack of systematicity), and designed the next experiment: bind item and relation together using the substrates own fixed vector-symbolic algebra (not a flexible neural net) so new combinations compose correctly by construction, matching how a 2023 Nature-published brain-inspired AI architecture solved a similar puzzle-reasoning benchmark.

summary: master reasoning-stack map: 8-stage brain-QA architecture mapped end-to-end against disk-verified substrate state (10 VET drills + 25 ARC experiments synthesized); 7/8 stages have real brain-cited components (mostly WIRING debt, not missing capability, per integration audit); stage-8 (learning/credit-assignment) is the one genuine structural gap (Director does it by hand); the proven-failed shortcut across the whole ARC arc = similarity-scoring standing in for entailment/derivation over thin GloVe/WordNet meaning; dependency-sequenced build plan: (1) science-precise rule-supply extraction, (2) compose hdlab/reasoner.py (typed-graph derivation search, promotes 3 exp-trapped primitives), (3) wire already-certified do-calculus for coupled-relationship items, (4) RPE-tuned credit-assignment cheap test, (5) surgical meaning-foundation rebuild targeted by step-2 residual failures.
plain_language: We mapped, stage by stage, everything the brain does to answer a question by reasoning, and checked each stage against what we have actually built. Good news: most of the pieces already exist on disk (a real comprehension reader, a certified causal-reasoning tool, a proven multi-hop search engine, a working answer-scoring mechanism) -- they are just not wired together into one runnable reasoner yet. The one real capability gap is that a human (the Director) currently has to manually diagnose every failure by hand instead of the system learning from its own mistakes automatically. The next concrete steps are: expand the science-fact rule library, then build the one missing assembly point that chains typed rules into an inspectable proof for each answer -- this is the concrete path to a system that can show its reasoning, not just guess from similarity.

summary: earn_it_differentiation_loop_definitional_worldtree: pre-designed build B (dispatch-ready, gated on build A full-run greenlight). Build A (exp_intrinsic_foundation_loop_tie_gaps_defmatch_v1) confirmed live (smoke 2026-07-26T00:08Z); its feed_b field (concept_role_slot_profiles + concept_heldout_side) is Bs literal input. B retargets the already-twice-landed composed differentiation loop (v1 HARD_FAIL memorize, v2 MIDDLE 0.24 held-out/compression 1.17) onto As own tie-relevant concepts + specific discriminating slot. New biology: CLS-updated (Kumaran-Hassabis-McClelland 2016) maps onto existing KEEP_EPISODIC/compression gate; WAT theory (Borghi-Binkofski) predicts relational-not-perceptual grounding for these abstract concepts, convergent with Binder direct-supply closing structurally at the same seam (29571). Hard gate: if A HONEST_NEGs on its full run, B should NOT be dispatched.
plain_language: We designed the next-stage learning experiment (build B) so it is ready to launch the moment the current experiment (build A, running right now) gives the green light. Build A is testing whether matching on precise scientific definitions (not just word-similarity) helps the system break ties between confusable answers. If that works, build B teaches the system to figure out those same fine distinctions for brand-new concepts it has never seen the answer for, by learning from how other similar concepts relations are structured -- the difference between memorizing an answer key and actually learning the pattern. We built in strict tests so it cannot fool itself into looking like it learned when it only memorized, and an honest rule that says do not even bother running build B if build A fails its own test first, since that would mean the whole approach is capped from the start.
mechanism: retarget of already-landed composed-differentiation-loop (competitive-Hebbian ConceptEncoder + MDL learner) onto build A concept/split, CLS + WAT grounded
recommendation: hold dispatch of build B until build A full (n=128) run lands; if A HARD_PASSes, hand this note to hdi_exp_dev verbatim

summary: definitional_meaning_foundation_scale_audit: full-ARC-vocab (7787 Q, 10518 word types) vs WorldTree v2.1 def/prop tables -- 69.0pct token coverage, but depth shallow (median 1 fact/concept, frac_ge2=0.255, cross-validates a642b513 v2 0.24). WordNet gloss (already on disk, unnamed prior supply source) closes breadth to 92.3pct types/98.5pct tokens near-free; catch is polysemy (mean 5.1 senses/word) not scarcity. ConceptNet promiscuity quantified: 98.3pct lexical presence but 52-53pct of edges are generic RelatedTo regardless of slice; clean IsA/HasProperty/PartOf/UsedFor types are ~12-15pct minority -- explains prior ConceptNet HARD_FAIL. Binder confirmed thin at full-ARC scale (3.05pct/9.1pct). GenericsKB/CSLB/other OpenStax absent from disk. Verdict: SCALABLE at breadth (near-solved, near-free); DATA-BOUND at multi-relation depth (genuine gap). Ranked sourcing: WordNet+disambiguation first, then WorldTree domain-depth expansion, then OpenStax acquisition, then GenericsKB/CSLB, ConceptNet last-resort filtered-only.
plain_language: Checked whether the plan to give the substrate real definitions for ARC science concepts (tested so far on only 128 hard cases) will actually work across the whole test, or whether we run out of clean definition data. Good news: a free, already-on-disk dictionary source (WordNet) covers 92-98 percent of the vocabulary with clean one-line definitions -- the main remaining problem is picking the right definition when a word has multiple meanings, not finding definitions at all. Bad news: the richer, multi-fact profiles (what actually distinguishes similar concepts like hydro vs nuclear power) stay thin across the whole test, not just the 128 hard cases -- that part genuinely needs more data, and I ranked where to get it from cheapest to most expensive.

summary: sr_chaining_arc_reasoning_design: brain-drilled hippocampal SR/resolvent (Stachenfeld/Dayan/Bono/replay/TEM) + pinned the honest ARC target as the TIE bucket (66 co-derivable-candidate questions where symbolic-intent tie-break already measured d=0.000), not depth-extension of meet_connected (already exhaustive BFS at depth<=3, and the 82%% non-derived + 55%% dist_only buckets are entity-linking/rule-sparsity bound, not search-depth bound). Designed exp_arc_reasoner_sr_gated_tiebreak_v1 (NOT built/dispatched): reuses SRSolver resolvent (verbatim from the toy HARD_PASS cell) as a graph-support-strength channel, gated (learned convex blend, CV over the small tie-n) against the existing combiner-cosine channel via the gated-fusion cell pattern, with scrambled-graph + random-occupancy must-fail controls. Pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL bands mirror the prior symbolic-tiebreak cell for direct comparability. Honest structural risk flagged in advance: ARC rule-graph mean degree <1 vs the toy domain where SR was proven (mean degree 6.65, 22x denser) -- predicted most-likely outcome is SR-degenerate or lambda*->0, a third clean diagnosis of meaning-boundedness at this tie bucket if so.
plain_language: We studied how the brain finds multi-step paths to a goal (a hippocampal mechanism called the successor representation) and designed a test that wires two previously-proven brain-like tricks into the ARC reasoning system, at the one decision point where they might genuinely help: when two possible answers are both technically reachable and the system has to pick. We are upfront that the ARC knowledge graph is much sparser than the toy domain where this trick worked before, so it may fail cleanly -- but even that would be a useful, informative result.

summary: structure_content_factorization_generalizing_meaning: brain-drilled TEM+PDP+ATL, diagnosed exact gap off atoms 29556/29557 (neither trained a content-blind structural code, neither tested multi-hop composition or held-out-to-new-concept), designed (not built) exp_grounding_tem_factorized_heldout_concept_v1 on real WorldTree typed-relation data, P_deflated=0.18
plain_language: Studied how the brain factors WHAT something is (content) from HOW it relates to other things (structure) so it can reason about brand-new things it has never seen -- and pinpointed exactly why our two prior attempts to build this memorized instead of generalizing. Designed (did not build) the next test, on real science-relational data instead of a toy dataset, with an honest low odds of success stated up front.

summary: learned_inference_generalization_analogy_metalearning: architecture exhausted as generalization lever (29556 ho_lift=0.0, 29557 shuffle_sep=0.111, 29578/29579 factorized-g ties RANDOM_G control -- code-confirmed store-then-recall, not inference). Brain-drilled structure-mapping analogy (Gentner/SME candidate-inference, Hummel-Holyoak LISA/DORA, RLPFC/frontopolar neural basis) vs meta-learning-for-compositionality (Lake-Linzen-Baroni MLC) -- MLC requires few-shot support at test time (not zero-example), analogy is zero-example-by-construction, so analogy picked as primary lever, meta-learning named as fallback (train the alignment weights). Designed can-fail cell exp_analogy_candidate_inference_heldout_edge_v1: excludes queried edge from ALL storage (fixes 29578/29579 leak), structural-profile alignment mechanism, store-recall-floor + flat-MLP baselines must collapse to base-rate before any analogy number counts, 4 must-fail controls, degree-accuracy correlation check. Design only, not built.
plain_language: We figured out why the last attempt to teach the substrate to reason about brand-new concepts secretly cheated -- it had already been told the answer, just filed it under a different label. Studied how humans really do this (by analogy to a similar known thing, a brain-based mechanism located in front-of-brain regions) versus a rival machine-learning idea (a training regimen, not shown to work without hints). Picked the analogy approach as the better fit and designed a strict test for it that cannot be cheated, with a built-in tripwire to catch it if it slips again.

summary: prior_conceptnet_composition_lookback: read-only look-back finds the reframe (composition fires on redundant ConceptNet, tied floor only on curated WordNet/WorldTree) is NOT supported by banked work -- the one genuine held-out-edge inheritance test on ConceptNet (exp_substrate_conceptnet_kg_inference_transfer_cpu_v1, T3/CERT_CHAIN_GRADE) explicitly states coverage-completion-not-reasoning REPLICATED from WordNet to ConceptNet (substrate Hits@10 0.451 < frozen-BGE 0.502). A second attempt (semantic-seeded beam) also HARD_FAILs vs BGE and random. Best composition-alone result vs a real baseline is a statistical TIE (conceptnet_rerank_parity_multiseed_v1 deliverable B, MM not CG). The two apparent HARD_PASSes in the dispatch (glass_box_micro_loop_conceptnet_multihop_v1/_SCALE_v1, role_tagged_compositional_generalization_on_concept_KG_v1) do not test held-out-edge inference: the first chains KNOWN stored facts via a WM-gate-requery architecture (no FREQ baseline), the second is UNVETTED synthetic-toy data confounded by a concept-encoder swap applied only to the winning arm. role_filler_factorization_conceptnet_cg_v1 is the one VET-clean positive (factored beats flat on real ConceptNet+GloVe recombination) but VET narrowed it to a capacity effect, not evidence about redundant text or reading. RECOMMENDATION: exact composition-beats-FREQ-on-ConceptNet test already run twice (both HARD_FAIL) -- do not repeat; the open gap is redirecting the CHAIN_GRADE WM-requery loop at the existing never-ingested held-out split + BGE bar, which has never been tried.
plain_language: We looked back at prior experiments testing whether the substrate can compose/infer new facts from ConceptNet (a large real-world knowledge graph). The idea we were checking was: maybe the reasoning mechanism works fine on this redundant, richly-connected data and only failed on smaller curated datasets. It does not hold up: the most directly relevant already-graded prior experiment explicitly found the SAME failure pattern on ConceptNet as on the curated data, losing to a simple off-the-shelf embedding baseline. Two other attempts also lost. One cell that looked like a win is unvetted and has a fairness bug (comparing arms that are not actually apples to apples). We recommend not repeating the same test a third time, and instead trying the one mechanism that does work reliably on this data (an iterative retrieval loop) on the specific never-seen-edge question it has never been asked.

summary: scale_corpus_and_data_integrity_plan: designed real-text scale-up corpus + integrity analysis. ARC_Corpus.txt (data/corpora/arc/, 1.4GB, 14.62M sentences, 237.7M measured alpha tokens) is on-disk NOW and recommended as first corpus -- measured coverage against the exact 24275-concept single-token vocab from cskg_foundation_v1: median 376 mentions/concept, 68.1pct at >=100 mentions, only 2.33pct zero -- vs the prior data-starved deep-text run (265,273 tokens total, mean 3.07 mined sentences/concept, near-chance 0.519). Designed the full integrity pipeline: dedup/near-dup, quality filtering, from-scratch BPE tokenization, and critically a NEW concept-level held-out scrub (verified this session that cskg_foundation_v1 existing split is EDGE-level not concept-level -- 15,728 held-out-edge subjects still appear in training shards -- so it cannot be reused for a text-scale leak-proof test). Pre-registered HARD-PASS/HARD-FAIL fork: if the well-covered majority (>=100 mentions) still shows no margin over raw grounding at this scale, that refutes data-scale-as-the-lever and redirects to the R1 objective fix instead.
plain_language: We designed the plan for feeding the from-scratch meaning-learner a much bigger diet of real English text, plus the quality checks that plan must pass before we trust it. Good news: we already have a big, relevant, on-disk science-text corpus (no download needed) that gives about 100 times more real-world exposure per concept than the failed small-scale attempt. We also measured exactly how well that corpus covers the concepts we care about, and designed the specific anti-cheating checks (making sure test concepts are truly never seen during training) needed before any results from this can be trusted.

summary: Breadth corpus expansion: Simple English Wikipedia recommended first (load_dataset wikimedia/wikipedia, 20231101.simple, clean CC BY-SA license, ~150-400M tokens hedge) -- ranked shortlist Wikipedia > OpenSubtitles (dialogue/social register) > Gutenberg/SPGC (narrative) > FineWeb sample, with BookCorpus/Books3/Pushshift/CC-News flagged AVOID on legal grounds. Coverage measurement (40-word probe against 237.7M-token ARC corpus) found raw mention-COUNT for social/emotional words is mostly adequate (family=102473, respect=15979) -- the real gap is REGISTER (expository vs narrative framing), not presence, plus a genuine long-tail gap (doorbell=98, wallet=528). USER course-correction mid-task: scoped BOTH encoder (MLM) and reader (situation_reader->clarify_gate->sleep->cskg_foundation_v1) paths per corpus -- verified on disk that reader cycle2=HURT_REGRESSION (aggressive gate hurts, delta -0.338) and cycle3=MIDDLE_BAND coverage_frac=0.316 (throughput-limited), both flagged as must-fix before reader scaling, independent of corpus choice.
plain_language: Planned the next expansion of what the substrate reads: Wikipedia first (broad, clean-licensed, free), then movie-subtitle dialogue for everyday social language, then classic books for narrative structure -- while explicitly avoiding several popular but legally risky datasets. Also found that the science corpus already contains everyday words like family and respect fairly often, so the real gap is probably HOW those words are used (textbook-style vs real-life-style sentences), not whether they appear at all. Separately, confirmed on disk that the fact-extraction half of the learning loop has known bugs (an overly aggressive check hurts accuracy, and it only manages to extract facts from about a third of what it reads) that need fixing regardless of which corpus comes next.

summary: brainfaithful_consolidation_read_sleep_loop: diagnosed plain mention-averaging dilution as TWO separate failure modes (uniform-weight noise-dilution + systematic regression toward a shared cross-concept centroid/anisotropy) requiring TWO distinct fixes -- precision-weighted Kalman-gain update (fixes noise-dilution, reuses existing local schema-fit/coherence/reliability signals per landed race-cell lesson) PLUS explicit common-mode/shared-direction subtraction via streaming Oja/Sanger PCA before integration (fixes centroid-regression specifically, the DG-pattern-separation analog; precision-weighting alone does NOT fix this per anisotropy/representation-degeneration ML literature, Ethayarajh 2019 / Gao et al 2019 / Mu and Viswanath 2018). In-house schema_exemplar_bayes.py already shows 100x hardmax centroid pooling loses 96pct recall, confirming centroid-collapse is a real severe failure mode on this substrate. P_deflated=0.45 (compound claim, each half independently well-evidenced ~0.65-0.75 but combination untested). Session had a mid-drill connection interruption; wrote deliverable directly from gathered in-house prior-art review + partial lit-scan.
plain_language: Figured out why our reading-and-remembering loop keeps making concept representations blander instead of sharper as it reads more: two separate bugs, not one. First, it treats every mention as equally trustworthy (fix: weight by reliability, the brains confidence-based learning-rate trick). Second, and more importantly, all mentions share a hidden common background pattern that keeps leaking into every concept and making them all look more alike over time -- averaging never removes that, you have to explicitly subtract it (the brains pattern-separation trick, dentate gyrus). We already have in-house proof that collapsing to one blended representation is catastrophic (a 96 percent recall loss in an existing test), so this is a real, high-stakes bug, not a hypothetical.

summary: scour_prior_consolidation_fusion_selflearning: mined experiments/ + metrics.json + cert_ledger for reusable consolidation/fusion mechanisms for the self-learning loop. Top finds: CA3 pattern-completion-before-write beats plain averaging (exp_cls_ca3complete_consolidation_v1, HARD_PASS, retention 0.933 vs 0.020 naive, +0.055 lift p=0.0003 n=8 seeds); cluster-gated averaging (p4_replay_consolidation, HARD_PASS); learned convex gate recovers naive-fusion dilution (exp_grounding_gated_fusion_relation_inference_mammal_v1, HARD_PASS, +0.2332 MRR over naive 1:1 fusion); MDL accept/reject gate (hdlab/learner/core.py) already live-wired as a consolidation guardrail. Biggest known-broken: reader-feedback-into-knowledge override nets hurt 3x across corpora (cycle2 -0.1457 acc, cycle3 coverage_frac=0.316 ceiling, chaingrade_FULL naive baseline beats trained reader on cold transfer 11/13 vs 10/13) -- structural baseline headroom + coverage must be pre-measured before any override gate.
plain_language: Searched our own past 5000+ experiments for reusable techniques for the new read-and-learn loop. Good news: we already solved the two suspected weak spots (averaging that forgets things, and text+grounding blending that dilutes) in earlier experiments -- those fixes just need to be wired into the new loop rather than re-invented. The one real unsolved risk is letting newly-learned facts override the reader's existing guesses -- that has backfired three separate times because the reader is often already right most of the time, leaving no room for the new knowledge to help.

summary: loop_fairness_audit: self-learning loop v1-v3 audited element-by-element -- UNFAIR as a comprehension test (frozen encoder, mean-pool averaging cannot represent structure, word-scramble control preserves lexical content so it cannot discriminate content-driven from order-sensitive gain) -- and situation_reader.py (the codebase structured-relation extractor) is NEVER imported by any loop cell; the loop bypassed extraction entirely and measured distributional rep-pooling instead.
plain_language: We asked: was our reading-comprehension experiment actually fair, and what did we miss? Answer: the experiment measured whether a running-average of sentence embeddings drifts toward the right neighborhood -- a real but narrow effect -- not whether the substrate understood what it read. The bypassed piece is a fully-built module (situation_reader.py) that extracts who-did-what-to-whom from sentences; the loop never called it, so there was never any structured fact for the substrate to actually learn. The note gives the minimum fair test: wire in extraction, add a content-swap control instead of word-scramble, and probe for the specific fact taught instead of a generic neighbor-ranking score.

summary: brain_reading_comprehension_vs_our_loop: our self-learning loop pools (order-insensitive averages) encoder reps at mention sites, which is a permutation-invariant operation -- it is mathematically incapable of distinguishing coherent from scrambled text (mean({A,B})==mean({B,A})), which is exactly why scrambled text refined concepts AS MUCH (+0.029) as coherent text (+0.024). Brain pipeline (3 lit-scans: hippocampal binding, compositionality formalism, ATL/sentence-composition regions) extracts a role-labeled PROPOSITION (Kintsch predicate-argument, IFG/LATL thematic-role assignment) then hippocampally BINDS it (CA3 relational binding, order-sensitive by construction per Fodor-Pylyshyn/Smolensky/Plate formalism) before schema-gated cortical consolidation (Tse et al.). Fix: route concept-refinement through hdlab/situation_reader.py role-tagged event extraction (already banked, HRR-style bound not pooled) gated by clarify_gate.py role-completeness, write as discrete propositions not pooled averages, consolidate via schema-congruence in sleep step -- reuses already-built modules, no new invention needed. Cheap decisive test (<1hr): rerun situation_reader role-resolution rate on the same coherent/scrambled pairs -- should collapse on scrambled if the reader is comprehension-sensitive where pooling was blind.
plain_language: Diagnosed exactly why our reading-and-learning loop cannot tell real sentences from scrambled word-salad: it averages word representations together, and averaging literally cannot detect word order (average of A and B is the same as average of B and A, no matter what order they came in). The brain does something categorically different: it figures out who-did-what-to-whom (a structured fact) and stores that fact as a unit, which is why word order matters to a human brain within a third of a second. The fix reuses tools we already built (a reader that extracts who-did-what-to-whom from a sentence) -- it just is not currently wired into the self-learning loop, which instead takes a shortcut (averaging) that cannot possibly measure comprehension.

summary: v6 scoping: brain thematic-role learning is error-driven+slot-general (Frankland/Greene 2015 lmSTC; Rabovsky/McClelland N400-prediction-error), not innate lookup, supporting self-taught extraction over hand-labeled roles. Mapped to foundation-triples-as-distant-supervision (Mintz 2009 lineage); biggest risk is entity-pair/lexical leakage (Peng et al 2020: >50% of RE benchmarks solvable from entity identity alone) -- same failure species as v3 downgrade. Learned-VSA-binding precedent exists (Steinberg & Sommer 2019 learned role-filler binding; Ganesan et al 2021 gradient-stable HRR). Recommend a training-free offline diagnostic (identity-only B0 baseline + hard-negative distractors, held-out concept-PAIR split) before committing v6 GPU time.
plain_language: Researched how the brain learns to figure out who-did-what-to-whom in a sentence, and how to teach our substrate the same skill using facts it already has (the 1.24M-fact foundation) instead of borrowing an outside reading tool. Found a real risk: the substrate could cheat by memorizing which facts go with which concepts instead of actually reading the sentence -- so before building the real version we should run a quick, cheap check (half a day, no training) that would catch that cheat early.

summary: encoder ceiling scoping: on-disk inventory finds NO real breadth corpus staged (text8=17M tok, ~7pct of ARC pool; Simple-Wiki scoped not pulled) but relational-objective lever IS buildable tonight zero-dep (cskg_foundation_v1 482k nodes/1.24M edges HARD_PASS on disk; prior w_rel joint-objective code exists at exp_deep_text_encoder_self_teacher_heldout_new_v1.py, MIDDLE_BAND but confounded by 500x-smaller scale). 2 lit-scans: LinkBERT-class MLM+relation joint objective verified +5-7pct at moderate scale but self-derived-no-external-teacher version is extrapolation; near-chance-despite-exposure probe (our 0.56 vs chance 0.51) reads in the literature as objective/architecture-bound not data-bound (Capability Ceilings arXiv:2510.21866). plain_language: Researched why the substrates from-scratch text encoder plateaus at near-chance relational understanding. Found we do not actually have a big variety of extra reading material ready to use (that still needs downloading), but we DO already have the ingredients to try teaching the encoder to predict relationships directly (not just guess missing words) tonight, at no extra data cost. Outside research suggests this kind of stuck-at-chance pattern is usually a fix-the-training-goal problem, not a need-more-data problem, so that is the recommended experiment for tonight, with the bigger-corpus idea queued for a follow-up night.

summary: comprehension_eval_battery_lit_grounding: 2x2 parallel lit-scan (broad neuro/psycholinguistic assessment-of-knowing + narrow NLP shortcut-learning/eval-design) grounding a reusable memorization-proof comprehension battery. Convergent 3-part pattern found independently in both literatures: (1) novel-instance/relation generalization tests learned intension not exemplar lookup (Osherson 1990 category-based induction; Rogers & McClelland 2004 property/typicality verification; Gentner cross-mapped structural-vs-surface analogy); (2) an ablated identity/hypothesis-only baseline that MUST score near chance is the fields own validity gate (Poliak 2018 69pct vs 34pct chance SNLI; Gururangan 2018 annotation artifacts; Peng 2020 entity-identity RE shortcuts; LAMA-UHN/Cao 2021 knowledge-probing frequency artifacts); (3) tunable hard-distractor forced-choice/ranked pool gives dynamic range a pairwise AUC cannot (HellaSwag adversarial filtering drops SOTA <48pct vs human >95pct; KB-completion Hits@k/MRR full-pool ranking). N400 ERP literature (Kutas & Federmeier 2011; Rabovsky 2018 prediction-error account; Michaelov 2022 LM-surprisal-predicts-N400) supplies a neural analog and a direct LM-eval precedent. ~29 VERIFIED-LIVE citations, 5 flagged RECALLED-UNVERIFIED (numeric details only). Directly supports the 07-27 loop-fairness-audit diagnosis (mean-pooling cannot separate coherent from scrambled input) with the fields standard fix pattern. No design proposed -- citations/grounding only, synthesis left to Director.
plain_language: Researched how scientists (both brain researchers and AI benchmark designers) tell the difference between a system that truly understands a concept versus one that is just recognizing a familiar label. Both fields independently converge on the same 3-step recipe: test on a brand-new example never seen before, build a stripped-down version of the test that a system should FAIL if it is cheating, and use a multiple-choice format with deliberately tricky wrong answers rather than a simple yes/no. This gives the Director concrete, citable methods to build a reusable understanding-test for the substrates own from-scratch encoder, and it independently confirms a bug we already found in the reading-and-learning loop (averaging cannot tell real sentences from scrambled ones).

That check only tried it once, on one random draw, so tonight I turned it into a proper repeatable experiment: run the same check 3 different ways on the one trained model we have, plus try the same trick on two other trained models we already have sitting on disk, to see if the finding holds up or was a fluke. I was upfront that we only have ONE copy of the original model trained from scratch (would need to train a second one to fully close that gap) and flagged that clearly rather than papering over it. Shipped it to run on the spare CPU machine so it does not compete with the GPU work already in progress.

plain_language: We had a proven trick (a learned dial that blends two information sources) sitting unused. The readings-and-learning encoder already blends its own text understanding with structured word-knowledge using a FIXED 50/50 blend, and we noticed that fixed blend helps on one kind of question (what does a word mean) but actively HURTS on another (how are two things related), because the structured-knowledge source is basically useless for that second kind of question. So instead of a fixed 50/50, we tried the proven learned dial, tuned separately for each question type using only training-time data (never peeking at the held-out test answers). On the one seed thats finished so far, the learned dial beats the fixed blend on BOTH question types, and on the relationship question it recovers almost exactly back to as good as ignoring structured knowledge entirely -- exactly what we hoped. That is one data point though; a second training run needs to finish before we can call it proven.

plain_language: The proven learned-dial trick, applied to the reading encoders blend of text-understanding + structured-word-knowledge, PASSED on both training runs: the learned dial (tuned separately for meaning-questions vs relationship-questions, using only training data) beats the old fixed 50/50 blend on BOTH question types on BOTH runs. Its real value is narrow but genuine -- it undoes the damage the fixed 50/50 blend does to relationship-questions, turning the blend from a net loss into a small net gain over just using text alone. Important honesty: this does NOT mean the structured-word-knowledge experiment succeeded -- teaching the encoder with that knowledge separately FAILED to stick. So we WIRE the better dial IN (it is the right tool if we blend two sources at all), but flagged clearly that whether to keep blending in structured knowledge at all is a bigger call for the Director, since that knowledge barely helps. Also re-flagged that the remote machines code copy is badly out of date and needs a proper clean-up.

summary: brain-fidelity audit of as-built stateful core: mean-pool addressing + convex-blend write (no per-slot PBWM-style gating) is the top-ranked mechanism-limited gap explaining MES chance-tie-to-random-init; single shared content key compounds it for multi-entity MES; unprotected one-shot KB seed + gameable kb_consistency loss explains KD B<A. Verdict: mechanism-limited, not data-limited.
plain_language: Audited why the new working-memory module memorizes training examples but does not generalize, and why adding real-world-knowledge context made things worse instead of better. Root cause: the way the module decides which memory slot to update averages information across all slots before deciding, which destroys the very identity information needed to track multiple things at once -- this happens whether or not the module is trained, which explains why trained and untrained versions score the same. Recommends fixing the addressing mechanism next, before assuming more training data would help.

summary: forward_predictive_objective_from_wm_state: design spec for a genuine anticipatory PE objective (predicted_latent_t = predictor(slots_{t-1}), scored vs stopgrad(clause_rep_t)) coupled into the existing per-slot PBWM gate as a global situational-PE term alongside the existing per-slot local retrieval-PE; SimSiam-style stop-grad primary collapse guard + narrow VICReg variance backstop; keep MLM-bidirectional encoder (predict at situation-model granularity, not sub-clause); OOM-free (d-dim only, no vocab tensor); one-variable ablation Core vs Core+ForwardPred with HARD_PASS/HARD_FAIL bands pre-registered; build-order = AFTER audit-C per-slot-gating re-smoke confirms it clears random-init-core, not before (avoids confounded attribution).
plain_language: Designed (not built) the missing forward-prediction piece for the stateful working-memory core: a small module that guesses the NEXT sentence meaning from what it currently remembers, and gets scored on how close that guess was -- this is the anticipation mechanism the brain uses (predictive coding) that our system still lacked. Includes how to avoid the guesser cheating by predicting a constant, and exact pass/fail thresholds for the next build.

summary: Whole-architecture confirmation: stateful-core design vs SEM/EST/Zwaan/Rabovsky/Hasson/hippocampal-replay. Verdict PARTIAL, no wrong-hill evidence (SEM near-identical convergence); top gap = missing discrete bistable event-boundary segmentation (SEM+EST convergent, reframes existing convex-blend code bug); also symbolic/neural dimension-unification gap and scale-dependent multi-timescale-hierarchy gap. Recommend keep-going, reshape audit-C fix as segmentation+KB-slot-protection.
plain_language: Confirmed the stateful-core comprehension architecture against SEM/EST/Zwaan/Hasson literature: right hill, PARTIAL not CONFIRMED, missing explicit event-boundary segmentation is the top fix to reshape (not a new build).

summary: Encoder representation-richness lever ranking delivered
plain_language: Encoder representation-richness lever ranking: latent-PC (JEPA-style, standalone encoder-level) ranked #1 fix for the founding objective gap, OOM-free, measured independently via graded-geometry/held-out-NEW/linear-probe battery (29591-style) vs random-init + current MLM baseline; multi-timescale hierarchy #2, temporal-contiguity aux #3 (primitive banked, unwired), data-curriculum #4 (BabyLM-bounded), k-WTA deprioritized as a richness lever (sample-efficiency claim not supported in lit). Honest verdict: SOFT floor -- BabyLM anchor shows bounded not closed gains at our ~158M-token regime; validates prove-text-slice-then-expand-grounding over encoder-alone bet. Sequenced PARALLEL to the WM gate with fully separate measurement (no confound).

summary: binding credit-assignment: literature says structural warm-start, not more training; brain-faithful; held-out-role test designed
plain_language: Researched why our WM addressing key gets stuck (all queries collapse to the same slot) when trained end-to-end on downstream loss alone, even though a direct-supervision probe finds the address easily. Literature convergence (Sukhbaatar linear-start, Locatello slot-attention collapse fixes, DNC addressing-collapse fixes, attention rank-collapse theory) plus brain literature (hippocampal fast-Hebbian indexing, pre-structured grid-cell addressing, Complementary Learning Systems) both say: this needs a structural warm-start/auxiliary-supervision fix, not more training. Warm-starting from our own probe is brain-faithful (same class as the brains dedicated fast-binding stage), NOT a forbidden bolt-on, PROVIDED it generalizes to held-out roles never supervised -- designed the exact held-out-role test + two can-fail controls that would tell us which.

summary: forward_predictive_second_encoder: build plan delivered for JEPA-style latent-PC encoder (lever #1) FULL run + binding read-conditioning comparison vs frozen MLM v2 encoder. Diagnosed both prior blockers (data-prep silent hang at collect_pass = zero progress logging + redundant two-pass corpus scan; v5 causal-LM OOM = full-vocab logits tensor, structurally absent in the already-built exp_encoder_latent_pc_arc_v1.py latent-space-only design). No new architecture needed -- cell already exists per encoder_representation_lever_ranking lever #1; plan adds progress logging + single-pass data-prep merge + per-(seed,arm) checkpoint/resume + per-arm ckpt-save, then a new thin CPU-only harness (exp_binding_readcond_encoder_compare_v1) that swaps the frozen encoder into the proven read-conditioning binding-test mechanism. HARD-WIN = LPC encoder binds with none/whiten-only conditioning where MLM needed whiten+aux+warmstart. P_deflated=0.30 on HARD-WIN (new lit anchor this cycle: predictive-objective-yields-compositional-representations, bioRxiv 2025; binding-problem survey arXiv2012.05208).
plain_language: We planned out how to train a second, prediction-based encoder (instead of the current fill-in-the-blank one) to see if it naturally represents who-did-what-to-whom more clearly, without needing the extra math patches we currently rely on. We also found and fixed the exact reasons the last two attempts at this silently died (no progress messages during a multi-hour data step, and a memory blowup from an unrelated design). Go recommendation given; biggest open risk is whether the prediction objective actually reorganizes the relevant internal structure, which we wont know until the test runs.

summary: Build plan delivered for DG-analog fixed-projection addressing (replaces the learned per-role key that HARD-FAILED held-out-role generalization tonight). Fixed random expand+k-WTA sparsify+hash pooling, no per-role learned parameter, reuses certified block-local-K resonator (k=4/8) and Spoke-3 2x-expansion parameterization. Same held-out-role test/bands reused verbatim, one-variable swap. Honest risk: whitened role reps still ~0.80 cosine collinear, so a cheap pre-check (untrained geometry probe) gates the full run before spending training budget.

brain whitening/decorrelation vs DG pattern-separation fidelity drill: brain never runs global covariance-inverse whitening; decorrelation = local subtractive removal of expected/mean component + divisive gain control + sparse expansion, composed together. DG/cerebellar pattern separation = sparse fan-in expand + POST-projection divisive normalization (Golgi/basket-cell inhibition), not PCA/ZCA whitening. Our whiten-then-expand pipeline likely mis-orders one integrated brain operation; recommend inserting sparse-expand+post-projection-divisive-norm as an alternate arm in the pending DG pre-check, gated by a shared-axis-vs-role-identity control (residual shared component may be real signal, not nuisance -- direct precedent: exp_dense_KV_whitening_revival_v1_gpu HARD_FAILED for exactly this reason).
plain_language: Looked at how the brain removes redundant/shared signal (whitening) and whether that is the same thing as the hippocampus DG memory-separation trick we are copying. Finding: they are related but not identical, and our pipeline probably has the steps in the wrong order -- the brain normalizes AFTER expanding into sparse codes, not before. Recommend testing that reordering directly, with a safety check that the signal we would remove is not actually meaningful.

summary: Build-ready frontier design delivered: native-binding comprehension (tonight 3 VET-confirmed positives: novel-filler read-conditioning, native-VSA zero-shot-role, native-VSA cross-slot-relational) toward richer/naturalistic NL. Named 4 gaps (templated->varied NL, key-orthogonality-at-scale, no integration pipeline, longer multi-fact passages). Step 0 (fire first, cheap, closed-form): Lowdin symmetric orthogonalization of the existing role-key matrix in exp_vsa_native_bind_zeroshot_role_v1, tested at 15/30/60 roles -- directly targets the already-measured encoder_key_cosine_mean=0.35 bottleneck. Step 2 (gated on Step 0): new cell exp_native_binding_naturalistic_multirelation_v1 composing all 3 confirmed capabilities over a naturalistic 5-role (Fillmore case-grammar) multi-syntax (active/passive/relative-clause/cleft/pronoun-coreference) corpus, with mandatory pooled-reader + coreference-antecedent floors built and confirmed-collapsing BEFORE the native-VSA arm is trusted (reapplying the MES reservoir-decodable lesson). Honest risk: role-key derivation from genuinely varied syntax may hit the same context-entanglement wall that forced the earlier read-conditioning pivot.
plain_language: Designed the concrete next build to take tonight wins (the substrate binding words/roles/relationships using its own built-in algebra, not a learned mechanism) toward reading real, varied sentences instead of today's narrow templates. First cheap test: a fixed math trick to make the substrate role-signatures more distinct (needed once tracking many more roles). Second, bigger test: a richer made-up short-story corpus with varied sentence styles and pronouns, run through all three winning mechanisms combined. Flagged the most likely failure point: varied sentence styles might blur role-signatures the same way an earlier attempt got blurred, with a cheap early check to catch that before the full build.

summary: Brain-fidelity audit of native FHRR/VSA binding + 5 other comprehension components: native binding is Marr-L2-plausible (Nengo/SPA, resonator networks CITED) but rests on a CONTESTED binding-by-synchrony/phase-coding hypothesis (mixed-selectivity/conjunctive coding is a rival, arguably better-credentialed per 2024 Neuron review). Encoder statelessness and oracle-averaged role-key derivation are confirmed non-fidelity with no real defense. Superposition/bundling has a real capacity-tradeoff analog but unconfirmed literal mechanism. Moving from PBWM content-gated WM to algebraic binding was fidelity-NEUTRAL for binding specifically (PBWM answers maintenance/update-timing, not binding, per O Reilly-Frank/Chatham-Badre) but this exposes a real, distinct, still-ABSENT working-memory maintenance gap. Whitening fix already characterized in prior note.
plain_language: We asked: is our comprehension approach really modeled on how the brain works, or have we drifted into shortcuts that just happen to run? Honest answer: not fully. The core binding trick we built everything around is scientifically plausible but rests on a neuroscience hypothesis that is still actively debated, not settled fact -- a rival theory is arguably better supported. Two other pieces (how the encoder processes text, and how we derive role labels) are confirmed shortcuts, not brain-like. And a memory-maintenance piece we effectively dropped turns out to be a real, separate gap we still need to fill.

summary: learned_tpr_role_keys_binder_ablation: build-ready plan for gradient-learned TPR-factored role keys (replacing oracle-averaging) + 3-arm binder ablation (FHRR vs TPR-tensor-product vs mixed-selectivity conjunctive). Crux lit-scan (Webb/Sinha/Cohen 2021 ESBN vs LSTM/NTM arXiv:2012.14601; Schlag/Schmidhuber TPR-RNN arXiv:1811.12143) shows factored binding is a CITED, head-to-head fix for the flat-learned-key memorization failure the substrate already hit (exp_oracle_context_invariant_address_wm_v2 HARD-FAIL), but 3 2023-2025 critique papers (arXiv:2405.16391, 2406.01012, 2412.04671) show factorization is necessary-leaning not sufficient. Cheapest next step: effective-rank/KNN probe on the TPR key module alone (~1hr CPU) before full 3-arm ablation compute.
plain_language: We designed the concrete next build for two converging findings: our role labels were derived by an unrealistic shortcut (oracle-averaging) that literature says caps performance, and our binding trick rests on a contested brain hypothesis. The fix: learn role representations from scratch using a factored (role-times-filler) structure that the literature shows genuinely helps a related known failure (a flat learned lookup could not handle a never-seen role) -- then fairly race three binding mechanisms against each other on existing tests. Flagged honestly: factored structure helps but is not a guarantee; a cheap 1-hour check can catch the worst-case failure before spending the big compute budget.

summary: brain_syntax_to_role_mechanism_and_forward_predictive_encoder_spec: cited mechanism (Broca/BA44-45 TDH+eADM staged cue-integration explains measured passive-inversion; Schrimpf2021/Goldstein2022/Caucheteux&King show CAUSAL next-token-predictive transformers, not bidirectional-MLM, best-fit brain language processing) + build spec amending the existing never-run exp_encoder_latent_pc_arc_v1.py from bidirectional masked-span to causal next-latent + clause-level hierarchy head + reused PE-gated hold-then-revise layer at token granularity; reuses 100pct of existing OOM-safety/collapse-guard/checkpoint fixes; fair test = SAME exp_syntactic_role_agent_patient_voice_probe_v1 cell (74d4ea0c1) via path-swap, zero new probe code.

Found that brain-prediction research favors encoders that predict forward (like reading left to right) rather than seeing the whole sentence at once, and designed a concrete, cheap-to-verify change to our already-built next-encoder experiment (switch it from whole-sentence to left-to-right prediction, plus a small memory piece that can revise an early guess) using the exact same pass/fail test we already measured the failure on.
